title: Platelet satellitism due to EDTA  Anticoagulant - 7.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells, three morphologically normal segmented neutrophils and adequate, evenly dispersed platelets, mostly single with occasional doublets. Notably, no platelets are adherent to the neutrophils and no platelet clumps are seen, so platelet satellitism is not demonstrated in this field. The image may represent a comparison smear from a non-EDTA (e.g., citrate) sample in which satellitism resolves, or a field away from the phenomenon. As shown, the image does not demonstrate platelet satellitism and is discordant with the title; it shows a normal peripheral smear with adequate platelets.

title: Cytogram - normal peripheral blood - 4.
describe_en: Although the title refers to a cytogram, the image is a peripheral blood smear rather than an analyzer scatter plot. It shows two small mature lymphocytes, compressed into angular shapes by surrounding red cells, and a normal segmented neutrophil. Many red cells contain refractile, sharply outlined clear areas typical of drying (water) artifact, and a few stain precipitate particles are present; these should not be mistaken for inclusions or parasites. No blasts or dysplastic features are seen, and the findings represent normal leukocyte morphology.

title: Cytogram - normal peripheral blood - 6.
describe_en: Although the title refers to a cytogram, this image is a peripheral blood smear rather than an analyzer scatter plot. It shows two mature segmented neutrophils with 3-4 nuclear lobes, clumped chromatin, and finely granular pink cytoplasm without toxic change, hypersegmentation, or hypogranularity. Red cells are normochromic and normocytic, and platelets are normal in size. Findings represent normal neutrophil morphology.

title: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma-CD20
describe_en: Immunohistochemistry labeled as CD20 shows a nodular aggregate of small lymphoid cells in which the lymphoid cells lack membranous staining, with only faint, fine reticular brown signal within the nodule and a negative spindled background. This pattern contradicts the strong membranous CD20 positivity expected in splenic marginal zone lymphoma. The image is discordant with its label and more likely represents a negative or dendritic-cell-restricted marker (such as CD23 or CD21 staining a follicular dendritic meshwork) or a failed stain; correlation with the case's actual CD20 slide is required.

title: Figure 2
describe_en: Clinical photograph shows a seated child with marked globular swelling of the right knee and a swollen, bulbous contour of the left knee, held in partial flexion. There is relative wasting of the thigh and calf muscles. No overlying skin lesions or bruising are evident. Note that the record legend describes an agarose gel (inverse shift PCR), which does not match this image; the image is a clinical photograph. The appearance is suggestive of hemarthrosis/chronic hemophilic arthropathy in the context of hemophilia A.

title: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia, B/myeloid: Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear field shows red cells, many of which contain fine punctate basophilic dots that may represent basophilic stippling or stain precipitate, together with scattered crenated forms. A large polygonal eosinophilic anucleate structure with peripheral clusters of coarse blue granules is present; its identity cannot be established at this resolution and it may be artifactual or a degenerated cell. No blasts are identified in this field. The image does not by itself demonstrate the features of mixed phenotype acute leukemia; the diagnosis rests on blast enumeration and flow cytometric lineage assignment (MPO plus strong CD19 with CD79a/CD22/CD10).

title: Aggressive NK-cell leukemia H&E Bone Marrow Biopsy
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy section stained by immunohistochemistry (not H&E as titled), with hematoxylin counterstain. The marrow is diffusely replaced by sheets of medium to large atypical cells with round to oval nuclei. Most infiltrating cells show granular, dot-like cytoplasmic immunoreactivity, a pattern typical of cytotoxic granule-associated proteins, although the specific antibody is not identified in the image. Residual normal hematopoiesis is not evident in this field. In the appropriate clinical and immunophenotypic context (CD3ε+, surface CD3−, CD56+, EBER+), findings are consistent with marrow involvement by aggressive NK-cell leukemia.

title: Macrophage with phagocytosed red blood cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous medium-sized lymphoid cells with round to oval nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and moderate pale blue-gray cytoplasm bearing fine circumferential hair-like projections. An irregular purple cell or aggregate is present at the bottom of the field, but no macrophage with phagocytosed red cells is seen, so the image is discordant with its title. The morphology of the lymphoid cells is consistent with circulating hairy cells, supporting the clinical diagnosis of hairy cell leukemia; flow cytometry (CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123) and BRAF V600E testing are confirmatory.

title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis – reactive - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at scanning magnification shows a highly cellular specimen with dense sheets of nucleated cells and scattered larger dark cells. Cytologic detail is not resolvable at this power, and hemophagocytic histiocytes cannot be identified. The image establishes an adequate, cellular aspirate; evaluation for hemophagocytosis requires high-power examination of the smear.

title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis – reactive - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows an aggregate of mononuclear cells with overlapping nuclei, composed of smaller cells with dense chromatin admixed with larger cells with fine chromatin and pale cytoplasm. Scattered single mononuclear cells are present in the background. No definite hemophagocytic histiocyte is identified in this field. The image does not by itself demonstrate hemophagocytosis; the aggregate most likely represents clumped marrow cells, but a non-hematopoietic cluster should be excluded by review of other fields and ancillary studies.

title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis – reactive - 3.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive aggregate of medium-sized mononuclear cells with high N:C ratio, finely granular chromatin and scant pale cytoplasm, with focal nuclear molding. Scattered single mononuclear cells and red cells are present in the background. No hemophagocytic histiocytes are identified in this field, so the image does not by itself demonstrate hemophagocytosis. The nature of the cluster (clumped hematopoietic precursors versus non-hematopoietic tumor cells) cannot be determined from this field; correlation with the remainder of the aspirate, biopsy and immunophenotyping is required.

title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis – reactive - 4.
describe_en: Aspirate smear shows a cellular population dominated by medium-sized mononuclear cells with round nuclei, fine chromatin and pale blue cytoplasm, arranged singly and in loose aggregates. Several dark pigment or debris clumps are present, and occasional larger cells with more cytoplasm are seen. No definite hemophagocytic histiocytes are identified in this field. The image does not by itself demonstrate hemophagocytosis; the identity of the dominant population should be established with immunophenotyping and review of other fields.

title: Relapsed accelerated CML – T315I mutation - 5.
describe_en: Smear from a thick area shows increased blasts, which are medium to large cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, and basophilic cytoplasm. They are admixed with granulocytic precursors, including an eosinophilic myelocyte with coarse orange granules, a basophil, and a neutrophil. Red cells are crowded with drying artifact, and it cannot be determined with certainty whether this is blood or marrow. In the context of known CML, findings are consistent with disease progression with increased blasts (accelerated/blast phase); blast enumeration and ABL1 kinase domain mutation analysis (e.g., T315I) are indicated.

title: Metastatic prostate carcinoma - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy section shows thickened trabeculae with prominent lamellar lines, consistent with osteosclerotic change. The intertrabecular space is replaced by a population of pale, vacuolated cells with small hyperchromatic nuclei, with loss of normal hematopoiesis. Definite glandular differentiation or cytologic atypia is difficult to confirm at this magnification. In the clinical context, findings are suggestive of marrow involvement by metastatic carcinoma with osteoblastic reaction; confirmation with keratin and prostatic markers (PSA, NKX3.1) is recommended.

title: Döhle bodies - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a segmented neutrophil and a band neutrophil with coarse cytoplasmic granulation. A faint pale blue peripheral cytoplasmic inclusion suggestive of a Döhle body may be present, but it is not well resolved at this magnification. The red cells are largely normocytic with a few polychromatophilic cells, and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with reactive neutrophil changes such as toxic granulation, supporting an infectious or inflammatory process.

title: Flame cell - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large plasma cell (arrow) with a small eccentric nucleus, perinuclear hof, and voluminous blue-violet cytoplasm. The cytoplasm appears slightly mottled but lacks a clearly defined red-purple peripheral fringe typical of classic flame cells. Background maturing myeloid and erythroid cells and small lymphocytes are present. Findings represent a plasma cell with abundant cytoplasm raising the possibility of a flame cell, which is associated with IgA-secreting plasma cell neoplasms but is not specific.

title: Snapper-Schneid granules - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at low power is cellular with numerous fat spaces and mixed hematopoietic elements. Plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and basophilic cytoplasm appear increased, and some show faint azurophilic cytoplasmic granulation, although granule detail is limited at this magnification. Maturing granulocytes and erythroid precursors are present. Findings suggest a plasmacytosis with granulated plasma cells; higher-power review, plasma cell enumeration, and clonality studies are required.

title: CML - 3.
describe_en: Bone marrow biopsy section shows a fragment containing clustered large cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and single, round, hypolobated nuclei, in keeping with small hypolobated megakaryocytes. The intervening stroma contains streaming, hyperchromatic spindle nuclei suggestive of fibrosis with some crush artifact, and an adjacent area is hemorrhagic. Overall marrow cellularity and myeloid maturation cannot be assessed in this field. In the appropriate context, the megakaryocytic morphology is compatible with chronic myeloid leukemia; confirmation of BCR-ABL1 is required.

title: CML - 5.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of a bone marrow biopsy shows bony trabeculae with markedly hypercellular marrow spaces and near-complete loss of fat, admixed with abundant hemorrhage. Focal cellular streaming suggests crush or fibrosis. Individual cell lineages and megakaryocyte morphology cannot be assessed at this magnification. Hypercellularity is compatible with the clinical diagnosis of chronic myeloid leukemia, but the image alone is not specific.

title: CML - 6.
describe_en: Low-power section of a bone marrow biopsy shows diffuse dark brown staining with a dense fibrillary background, most consistent with an overdeveloped reticulin (silver) stain, in which fibers appear increased and surround numerous megakaryocytes. Areas of streaming are present. Heavy background staining and the low magnification preclude reliable fiber grading or cytologic assessment. The findings suggest increased marrow fibrosis in chronic myeloid leukemia, but a well-differentiated reticulin and trichrome stain are needed for grading.

title: Peripheral blood findings in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single neutrophil with a bilobed nucleus connected by a thin bridge, dense clumped chromatin, and pale hypogranular cytoplasm, consistent with a pseudo-Pelger-Huët cell. Red cells show mild anisocytosis with scattered echinocytes, and platelets appear reduced in this field. No monocytes, immature myeloid cells, or blasts are present in the field shown. In a child with monocytosis and splenomegaly, dysgranulopoiesis of this type supports juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, but the field alone is not diagnostic.

title: Peripheral blood findings in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia - 4.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a medium-sized mononuclear cell with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine open chromatin and a thin rim of basophilic agranular cytoplasm, consistent with a circulating blast. No Auer rods are seen. A large platelet is present nearby. In the setting of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, occasional circulating blasts are expected, but a blast count of 20% or more would indicate transformation to acute leukemia.

title: Marrow findings in JMML - 1.
describe_en: The smear shows a cluster of nucleated cells composed of monocytes and promonocyte-like cells with folded nuclei, left-shifted granulocytes including myelocytes and bands, occasional hypolobated neutrophils, and several nucleated erythroid precursors. Blasts are not increased in this field. This image is identical to the one labeled as peripheral blood for this case (record 1093), and the dilute cellularity makes it difficult to confirm that it is a marrow aspirate. The myelomonocytic proliferation is consistent with juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, but marrow findings in JMML are nonspecific and diagnosis rests on blood counts and genetics.

title: Marrow findings in JMML - 4.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain of a hypercellular bone marrow biopsy shows diffuse granular cytoplasmic positivity in the majority of cells, with scattered interspersed negative cells. The staining pattern is typical of a myeloid or monocytic marker (such as myeloperoxidase or lysozyme), although the specific antibody is not stated. The findings indicate that the marrow is largely occupied by myelomonocytic cells, consistent with juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia in context; CD34 staining would be needed to assess blast percentage.

title: Marrow findings in JMML - 5.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain on a bone marrow biopsy section shows a hypercellular marrow in which a large proportion of cells display coarse granular brown cytoplasmic positivity. The positive population includes medium-sized cells with oval to indented nuclei and larger cells with more abundant cytoplasm, consistent with expanded myelomonocytic elements. The specific antibody is not stated; the granular pattern is compatible with a myeloid/monocytic marker such as lysozyme, CD68, or MPO. In context, findings support myelomonocytic proliferation as seen in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.

title: Sezary syndrome - peripheral smear - 1.
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows an increased number of small, uniform, dark-staining lymphoid cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and few other leukocytes. Red cells and platelets appear unremarkable. The nuclear contours cannot be assessed at this magnification, so cerebriform morphology cannot be confirmed. The findings indicate a small-cell lymphocytosis compatible with Sézary syndrome in the appropriate clinical setting; high-power review and flow cytometry are required.

title: Sezary syndrome - peripheral smear - 2.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two lymphoid cells, one small with dense chromatin and one slightly larger with a mildly irregular nuclear outline and scant agranular cytoplasm, adjacent to a normal segmented neutrophil. The characteristic cerebriform nuclear folding is not clearly resolved at this magnification. Red cells show prominent central pallor. The lymphoid cells are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, Sézary cells; flow cytometry for CD4+ T cells with loss of CD7 and/or CD26 is required.

title: Refractory Cytopenia of Childhood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows leukopenia with few circulating leukocytes, mild anisocytosis with occasional macrocytes, and no circulating blasts identified. The bone marrow aspirate shows dysplastic megakaryocytes with widely separated round nuclei and clusters of erythroid precursors with megaloblastoid chromatin and occasional nuclear irregularity; blasts are not increased. The core biopsy shows trilineage hematopoiesis with small hypolobated megakaryocytes and immature erythroid islands; the low-power field illustrated appears cellular rather than hypocellular, so overall cellularity should be judged on the entire core against age-matched norms. Conventional cytogenetics shows 45,XY,-7 and interphase FISH confirms loss of one chromosome 7 (one CEP7 and one D7S486 signal). Findings are consistent with refractory cytopenia of childhood (childhood MDS with low blasts) with monosomy 7.

title: APL - biopsy - 2.
describe_en: This Romanowsky-stained preparation (aspirate smear or biopsy touch imprint) shows sheets of monotonous immature myeloid cells with moderate cytoplasm containing azurophilic granules and round to folded nuclei with fine chromatin. Residual normal hematopoietic elements are sparse. Although the title indicates a biopsy, the image is a cytologic preparation rather than a histologic section. Auer rods and bilobed butterfly nuclei cannot be confidently resolved at this magnification. Findings are consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia in context; confirmation of PML::RARA is required.

title: Herpes simplex lymphadenitis - 1.
describe_en: Lymph node section at low to medium power shows extensive eosinophilic necrosis with abundant karyorrhectic nuclear debris and scattered inflammatory cells. A more cellular area is present along one side, and vessels and fat vacuoles are seen within the tissue. Viral cytopathic changes cannot be evaluated at this magnification. Findings are those of a necrotizing lymphadenitis; in context, herpes simplex virus lymphadenitis is favored, pending higher-power review for intranuclear inclusions and HSV immunohistochemistry.

title: Herpes simplex lymphadenitis - 4.
describe_en: Lymph node section shows a polymorphous paracortical infiltrate composed of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid cells, histiocytes, and scattered large activated immunoblast-like cells with vesicular nuclei and nucleoli. Vessels with plump endothelial cells are prominent. Necrosis and definite herpetic intranuclear inclusions are not identified in this field. Findings are those of a reactive paracortical/immunoblastic hyperplasia, which can accompany herpes simplex virus lymphadenitis adjacent to necrotic foci.

title: Primary effusion lymphoma - 3.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (marker not specified) performed on a cell block/tissue preparation shows a mixed population of large atypical cells with vesicular nuclei and small lymphocytes. A subset of the large cells shows membranous and paranuclear dot-like positivity, while small lymphocytes are negative. The staining pattern is compatible with an activation or plasmacytic marker such as CD30 or CD138, but the specific antibody cannot be determined from the image. In the appropriate clinical context, findings support involvement by primary effusion lymphoma; confirmation requires HHV8 (LANA) positivity.

title: Amyloidosis - 4.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy immunostain shows numerous positive cells scattered interstitially and in small clusters throughout a cellular marrow; the membranous pattern is compatible with a plasma cell marker such as CD138, although the antibody is not specified. A pale, acellular, round homogeneous deposit is present centrally, which could represent amyloid but requires Congo red staining for confirmation. Kappa/lambda staining is needed to establish clonality and quantify the plasma cell burden. Findings are suggestive of an increased plasma cell population in a patient with amyloidosis.

title: Amyloidosis - 5.
describe_en: Bone marrow section stained with H&E shows a hypocellular, hemorrhagic marrow with fat spaces, an adjacent bony trabecula, and scattered small, poorly preserved nucleated cells. Pale eosinophilic, amorphous, acellular material is present in the interstitium, which may represent amyloid deposition but could also reflect edema or fibrin. Plasma cells cannot be reliably identified at this magnification. A Congo red stain with polarization (apple-green birefringence) and assessment for a clonal plasma cell population by CD138 and kappa/lambda immunostaining are recommended to confirm amyloidosis.

title: Marginal zone lymphoma: leukemic phase - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low magnification shows an increased number of lymphoid cells relative to other leukocytes. The lymphocytes are small to medium-sized with round nuclei, condensed chromatin and scant to moderate pale blue cytoplasm; cytoplasmic villi cannot be assessed at this magnification. Occasional neutrophils are present, and smudge cells and blasts are not evident. Red cells and platelets are unremarkable. The findings indicate a lymphocytosis of mature-appearing cells, compatible with splenic marginal zone lymphoma in leukemic phase when supported by high-power morphology (villous lymphocytes) and immunophenotyping.

title: Essential thrombocythemia: peripheral smear - 3.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells without significant poikilocytosis. Platelets are dispersed singly and appear increased, with normal to slightly large forms and no clumping. Several mature segmented neutrophils with normal granulation are present, and no blasts, immature granulocytes, teardrop cells or nucleated red cells are seen. The degree of thrombocytosis cannot be quantified from this field and requires correlation with the platelet count. Findings are consistent with essential thrombocythemia in the appropriate clinical and molecular (JAK2, CALR, MPL) context.

title: Essential thrombocythemia: peripheral smear - 4.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, examined in a relatively thick area, shows numerous scattered platelets with variation in size, including large platelets and a central platelet aggregate. A single mononuclear cell with coarse purple cytoplasmic granules is present, which may represent a basophil, although its lineage cannot be determined with confidence. Red cells appear normochromic without teardrop forms, and no blasts or nucleated red cells are seen. The findings suggest thrombocytosis with platelet anisocytosis and are consistent with essential thrombocythemia in the appropriate clinical and molecular context (JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation), although reactive thrombocytosis and other MPNs cannot be excluded on the smear alone.

title: AML with maturation - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several large circulating blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to slightly angular nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and a moderate rim of pale basophilic agranular cytoplasm; no Auer rods are identified. A segmented neutrophil with normal lobation and granulation is present for comparison. Background red cells show crenation artifact. The findings indicate circulating blasts in keeping with acute leukemia; classification as acute myeloid leukemia with maturation requires bone marrow evaluation of granulocytic maturation and lineage confirmation.

title: AML with maturation - 2.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single circulating blast approximately twice the size of a red cell, with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, a slightly indented eccentric nucleus, and a moderate rim of pale basophilic agranular cytoplasm. No Auer rods are seen. Background red cells show widespread crenation, most consistent with a drying artifact. A circulating blast indicates a leukemic process, but maturation cannot be assessed on this field; classification as acute myeloid leukemia with maturation depends on the marrow differential and lineage studies.

title: AML with maturation - 3.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at low magnification shows a markedly hypercellular preparation composed of a densely packed, relatively monotonous population of round cells, with loss of the normal heterogeneous hematopoietic appearance. Thick areas are present at the edges of the smear. Cytologic detail, including chromatin pattern, granules, Auer rods and the degree of granulocytic maturation, cannot be evaluated at this power. The findings are suggestive of marrow replacement by an acute leukemia and are compatible with the stated diagnosis of AML with maturation, which requires high-power morphology, blast enumeration and immunophenotyping for confirmation.

title: AML with maturation - 6.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low power shows a markedly hypercellular marrow, approaching 100% cellularity, with near-complete loss of adipocytes. The intertrabecular spaces are diffusely replaced by sheets of intermediate-sized immature-appearing cells, with effacement of the normal trilineage hematopoietic pattern and inconspicuous megakaryocytes. Bony trabeculae appear unremarkable. The low magnification does not allow assessment of granulocytic maturation, so correlation with the aspirate differential is required; in that context the findings are consistent with involvement by acute myeloid leukemia, reported as AML with maturation.

title: AML with maturation - 7.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at high power shows diffuse replacement of the marrow by sheets of intermediate-sized immature cells with round to oval nuclei, fine chromatin, small nucleoli and moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm. A subset of cells has more eosinophilic cytoplasm and smaller, more condensed nuclei, suggesting some granulocytic maturation, whereas normal erythroid islands and megakaryocytes are not evident. The histologic features support involvement by acute myeloid leukemia; enumeration of maturing granulocytes on the aspirate or CD34/MPO immunostains is needed to classify it as AML with maturation.

title: T-PLL - 1.
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows marked leukocytosis composed of numerous small, relatively uniform mononuclear cells distributed evenly among the red cells. At this magnification the cytologic features that characterize prolymphocytes, such as a single prominent nucleolus, irregular nuclear contour, and cytoplasmic blebs, cannot be evaluated. The image supports a marked lymphocytosis but is not diagnostic on its own. Correlation with high-power morphology and flow cytometry (CD4+/CD7+ bright T cells) and TCL1A rearrangement is required to confirm T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia.

title: AML with inv(3) - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is hypercellular with an increased population of intermediate to large blasts showing round nuclei, fine chromatin, occasional nucleoli and moderately basophilic cytoplasm. These are admixed with maturing granulocytic elements at all stages, scattered lymphocytes and occasional erythroid precursors, adjacent to a particle edge. Megakaryocytes are not well represented in this field, so the hypolobated megakaryocytes typical of MECOM-rearranged AML cannot be evaluated here. The findings support acute myeloid leukemia; assignment to AML with inv(3)(q21.3q26.2) or t(3;3) requires cytogenetic or FISH confirmation.

title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear, in a thick and suboptimally spread area, shows two large atypical cells among residual hematopoietic elements. The cells have eccentric round nuclei with fine chromatin and small nucleoli, and abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing sparse fine azurophilic granules. Their appearance is plasmablast-like, and lineage cannot be assigned on morphology alone. Immunophenotyping (cytoplasmic CD3, CD56, cytotoxic markers, CD138) and EBER in situ hybridization are required. Findings are suggestive of marrow involvement by lymphoma, compatible with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma in the clinical context.

title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma - 3.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows residual trilineage hematopoietic elements with several admixed large atypical cells. These cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm, which is finely vacuolated in one cell, and round to cleaved or bilobed nuclei with fine chromatin. Azurophilic granules are not readily identified in this field, and the morphology alone does not establish lineage. Correlation with immunophenotyping (cytoplasmic CD3, CD56, TIA-1/granzyme B) and EBER in situ hybridization is required. Findings are suggestive of marrow involvement by lymphoma and compatible with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma in the clinical context.

title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma - 4.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular marrow containing multiple enlarged histiocytes with abundant pale, vacuolated cytoplasm. Several histiocytes contain phagocytosed nucleated hematopoietic cells and nuclear debris, indicating hemophagocytosis. The background shows residual erythroid and granulocytic precursors; definite atypical lymphoma cells are not evident in this field. Findings are consistent with hemophagocytosis, which in a patient with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma supports lymphoma-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis; marrow involvement should be assessed with EBER in situ hybridization.

title: Plummer-Vinson syndrome and reactive thrombocytosis mask a JAK2-V617F positive myeloproliferative neoplasm
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows hypochromic, microcytic red cells with anisopoikilocytosis, including pencil cells and occasional target cells, and a conspicuously increased number of platelets. No nucleated red cells, teardrop cells, or immature myeloid cells are seen in this field. The endoscopic inset shows a thin esophageal web. Findings are consistent with iron deficiency anemia with thrombocytosis and Plummer-Vinson syndrome; because thrombocytosis may persist after iron repletion, testing for JAK2 V617F, CALR, and MPL mutations is warranted, as the morphology cannot distinguish reactive thrombocytosis from an underlying myeloproliferative neoplasm.

title: Basophilic stippling: a lead to the diagnosis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several red cells with coarse, evenly dispersed basophilic stippling, in a background of target cells, mild anisopoikilocytosis, and occasional hypochromic cells; a mature neutrophil is unremarkable. The accompanying radiograph and CT reconstructions show an intramedullary femoral rod with retained radiodense metallic fragments in the thigh soft tissues, consistent with a retained bullet. In a patient with chronic unexplained abdominal pain, findings are suggestive of lead poisoning from retained bullet fragments; blood lead level and zinc protoporphyrin should be measured. The image does not support the benzene/environmental toxin aplastic anemia category under which it is filed.

title: Myeloma: CNS - 1.
describe_en: Cerebrospinal fluid cytospin is paucicellular and contains scattered red cells, a few small lymphocytes, degenerated cells, and occasional medium-sized round cells with eccentric nuclei, coarse chromatin and moderate gray-blue cytoplasm resembling plasma cells. Given the low magnification, perinuclear hofs and nucleoli cannot be reliably assessed, and immunophenotypic confirmation (e.g., flow cytometry for CD138/CD38 with light chain restriction) is recommended. In a patient with plasma cell myeloma, the presence of plasma cells in CSF is suggestive of CNS involvement by myeloma.

title: Bone marrow germinal center - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows normocellular marrow with trilineage hematopoiesis and a single large, well-circumscribed intertrabecular lymphoid aggregate. The aggregate is composed mainly of small lymphocytes with a slightly paler central zone and small vessels, but a definite germinal center with centroblasts and tingible-body macrophages cannot be confirmed at this magnification. There is no paratrabecular or diffuse interstitial lymphoid infiltration. Findings are consistent with a reactive lymphoid aggregate, possibly with germinal center formation; immunohistochemistry is helpful to confirm.

title: Bone marrow germinal center - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at intermediate power shows a dense lymphoid aggregate composed predominantly of small, mature-appearing lymphocytes with round hyperchromatic nuclei. The central area is slightly looser with interspersed red cells and small vessels; distinct germinal center cells (centroblasts, tingible-body macrophages) are not clearly resolved at this magnification. No large atypical cells or sheets of blasts are identified. Findings are suggestive of a benign lymphoid aggregate/follicle; immunohistochemistry (CD20, CD3, CD10, BCL6, BCL2) would help confirm a reactive germinal center.

title: Acute megakaryocytic leukemia - 1.
describe_en: Low-power view of a smear, most consistent with peripheral blood or a hemodiluted aspirate, shows numerous nucleated cells that aggregate into small cohesive clusters distributed among red cells, with frequent smudged cells in the background. At this magnification the clustered cells appear to be blasts with dark round nuclei and scant cytoplasm, but cytoplasmic blebs, granules and nucleoli cannot be evaluated. Clumping of blasts is a recognized feature of megakaryoblasts; in a patient with Down syndrome, the findings are suggestive of myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome, pending high-power review and flow cytometry for CD41/CD61.

title: Amyloidosis: Acquired Factor X Deficiency - 1.
describe_en: Clinical photograph of hair-bearing skin shows multiple flat, irregular red-purple purpuric macules and ecchymoses with a streaky, linear arrangement and scattered petechiae. The lesions do not appear raised or necrotic. In systemic AL amyloidosis, cutaneous bleeding results from vascular fragility due to amyloid infiltration of vessel walls and can be aggravated by acquired factor X deficiency from adsorption of factor X onto amyloid fibrils. The photograph is not diagnostic by itself; confirmation requires tissue Congo red staining, a prolonged PT and aPTT with low factor X activity, and a monoclonal protein work-up.

title: ALCL with completed erythrophagocytosis
describe_en: Section (H&E) shows a cellular infiltrate with abundant red cells and small dark nucleated cells. Scattered large cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and round, vesicular nuclei with small nucleoli are present. Centrally, a large cell with a thick cytoplasmic rim contains a large vacuole filled with pale granular debris, consistent with digested phagocytosed red cells. The image alone cannot establish lineage of the phagocytic cell; in the given context, findings are consistent with anaplastic large cell lymphoma with tumor-cell erythrophagocytosis, which should be confirmed by CD30 and ALK immunohistochemistry.

title: Amyloidosis: Acquired Factor X Deficiency - 3.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells of fairly uniform size, many of which contain small, dense, dark inclusions most consistent with Howell-Jolly bodies; occasional target-like cells are also seen. Lymphocytes and scattered platelets are present, and no circulating plasma cells or schistocytes are identified in this field. The low image resolution limits distinction from Pappenheimer bodies or stain precipitate. In a patient with systemic AL amyloidosis, these findings suggest functional hyposplenism from splenic amyloid infiltration; the smear itself is not diagnostic of amyloidosis or factor X deficiency.

title: Amyloidosis: Acquired Factor X Deficiency - 4.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows trilineage hematopoiesis with a centrally placed megakaryocyte and scattered mature-appearing plasma cells (arrows) with eccentric nuclei, clumped chromatin, and perinuclear hofs. The plasma cells lack prominent nucleoli or atypical forms, and a precise percentage cannot be estimated from a single field. No extracellular amyloid is evident on the smear. In a patient with amyloidosis, these findings support an underlying plasma cell dyscrasia; clonality should be established by kappa/lambda immunohistochemistry or flow cytometry, and acquired factor X deficiency is a laboratory finding that cannot be assessed morphologically.

title: Lymphocytosis: T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with mild anisocytosis and no significant polychromasia. A large lymphocyte with abundant cytoplasm containing coarse azurophilic granules is present, alongside two small mature lymphocytes without visible granules. Fine dark dots overlie many red cells and the background, favored to represent stain precipitate rather than basophilic stippling. In a patient with chronic anemia, large granular lymphocytes raise the possibility of T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia with associated pure red cell aplasia; a single field cannot establish lymphocytosis, and flow cytometry (CD3+, CD8+, CD57+, CD16+) with TCR gene rearrangement studies is required.

title: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura - 3.
describe_en: Low-power bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular specimen with numerous hematopoietic cells dispersed among red cells. Megakaryocytes are readily identified and appear normal to increased in number, without obvious clustering. Detailed evaluation of erythroid hyperplasia or megakaryocytic morphology requires higher magnification. Findings are consistent with adequate to increased megakaryopoiesis, supporting a peripheral consumptive cause of thrombocytopenia such as thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, but are not specific.

title: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura - 5.
describe_en: Bone marrow biopsy section shows a hypercellular marrow with increased megakaryocytes that are dispersed singly without tight clustering or marked atypia. There is a prominent population of small cells with round, dark nuclei consistent with erythroid hyperplasia, together with maturing granulocytic elements. No infiltrative process is identified in this field. Findings are consistent with reactive megakaryocytic and erythroid hyperplasia secondary to peripheral platelet consumption and hemolysis, as seen in thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, and are not specific for TTP.

title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: Thrombocytopenia - 13.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymphoid tissue, likely spleen given the title context of thrombocytopenia, shows diffuse effacement by a dense infiltrate of small round lymphocytes. Vague paler zones with slightly larger cells suggest proliferation centers, and sinusoidal/vascular spaces containing red cells are interspersed. No normal germinal centers are identified. The findings are consistent with involvement by chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma; thrombocytopenia in CLL may reflect immune-mediated destruction, hypersplenism or marrow infiltration, and confirmation of CD5/CD23 co-expression by immunohistochemistry is advised.

title: Follicular lymphoma - aspirate
describe_en: Low-power bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular particle containing maturing myeloid and erythroid precursors admixed with small lymphoid cells, one of which is indicated by the arrow. The lymphoid cells have dense nuclei and scant cytoplasm, but nuclear clefts cannot be confidently resolved at this magnification. No increase in blasts is evident. Findings are compatible with, but not in themselves diagnostic of, marrow involvement by follicular lymphoma; flow cytometry for a CD10-positive clonal B-cell population and trephine biopsy for paratrabecular aggregates are required.

title: HIV-Related Thrombocytopenia - 9.
describe_en: Section of lymph node shows an intact capsule and a markedly enlarged follicle with an irregular germinal center, attenuated mantle zone and scattered tingible-body macrophages. Aggregates of small mantle lymphocytes infiltrate and fragment the germinal center (arrow), a pattern termed follicle lysis. No neoplastic infiltrate is identified at this magnification. Findings are consistent with florid follicular hyperplasia with follicle lysis, characteristic of HIV-associated lymphadenopathy; the image does not directly demonstrate thrombocytopenia but reflects the immune dysregulation underlying HIV-related immune thrombocytopenia.

title: Multiple Myeloma: Platelet Dysfunction - 5.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows sheets of plasmacytoid cells with eccentric nuclei and abundant cytoplasm displaying strong cytoplasmic and membranous positivity, with perinuclear clearing in some cells. Nuclei have vesicular chromatin with occasional small nucleoli. The antibody is not identified in the image; if this represents a single immunoglobulin light chain, the sheet-like positivity would indicate a clonal plasma cell population. The image itself does not demonstrate platelet dysfunction, which in myeloma results from paraprotein coating of platelets and is assessed by functional assays. Findings are consistent with a plasma cell neoplasm (multiple myeloma).

title: Precursor T-Lymphoblastic Leukemia/Lymphoma - 5.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low power shows a hypercellular, packed marrow in which the intertrabecular spaces are diffusely replaced by a monotonous infiltrate of small to medium hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios. The cells show prominent streaming, likely related to crush artifact, and residual fat and normal hematopoietic elements are not identified. Cytologic detail and lineage cannot be assessed at this magnification. In the appropriate immunophenotypic context (TdT, CD34, cytoplasmic CD3 positive), findings are consistent with involvement by T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.

title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome: Refractory Anemia with Ringed Sideroblasts (RARS) - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a hypercellular marrow with trabecular bone and reduced fat. At high power there is erythroid predominance, with clusters of precursors bearing round, hyperchromatic nuclei, together with coarse brown hemosiderin deposits and occasional megakaryocytes. No increase in blasts is evident on this field. Ring sideroblasts cannot be evaluated on H&E sections; an iron stain on the aspirate and SF3B1 mutation testing are required. Findings are suggestive of erythroid hyperplasia with increased storage iron, in keeping with the provided diagnosis of MDS with ring sideroblasts.

title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome: Refractory Anemia with Ringed Sideroblasts (RARS) - 3.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy section shows a hypercellular marrow with prominent erythroid precursors, including arrowed large early erythroid cells with round nuclei, open chromatin and single prominent nucleoli, suggestive of megaloblastoid maturation. Occasional mitoses and admixed granulocytic precursors are present. Ring sideroblasts cannot be assessed on H&E; a Prussian blue stain on the aspirate is needed to document the ring sideroblasts required for MDS with ring sideroblasts, and exclusion of an acute erythroid leukemia requires quantitative assessment.

title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome: Refractory Anemia with Ringed Sideroblasts (RARS) - 4.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate composite shows a cellular specimen with trilineage hematopoiesis, including granulocytic precursors at all stages, erythroid precursors and a large megakaryocyte. Arrows highlight precursor cells with irregular nuclear contours or asynchronous nuclear-cytoplasmic maturation, suggesting mild dysplasia, although resolution limits detailed assessment. Blasts are not obviously increased. Ring sideroblasts cannot be evaluated on this Romanowsky stain; a Prussian blue stain showing at least 15% ring sideroblasts (or at least 5% with SF3B1 mutation) is required for MDS with ring sideroblasts.

title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome: Refractory Anemia with Ringed Sideroblasts (RARS) - 5.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate composite shows erythroid predominance with numerous proerythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts containing deeply basophilic cytoplasm and round nuclei with finely granular, somewhat open chromatin, suggesting megaloblastoid maturation. Polychromatophilic erythroblasts and granulocytic cells, including band forms, are also present. These findings indicate erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoiesis. Classification as MDS with ring sideroblasts requires a Prussian blue stain demonstrating ring sideroblasts, which is not shown.

title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome: Refractory Anemia with Ringed Sideroblasts (RARS) - 6.
describe_en: Composite of bone marrow aspirate fields shows erythroid precursors with megaloblastoid maturation, including large erythroblasts with fine chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm. Several erythroid cells show dyserythropoietic changes such as irregular, multilobated or budding nuclei, and a mitotic figure is present. Granulocytic precursors are also seen. These dyserythropoietic features are compatible with a myelodysplastic neoplasm; demonstration of ring sideroblasts (at least 15%, or at least 5% with SF3B1 mutation) requires an iron stain, which is not shown.

title: Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia - 8.
describe_en: Smear stained with what appears to be a cytochemical method shows numerous maturing granulocytic cells, including metamyelocytes, bands and segmented forms, most of which lack distinct red reaction product in the cytoplasm. Magenta-red deposits are present at the periphery of the field but cannot be confidently assigned to individual cells. The specific stain is not labeled; if this is a leukocyte alkaline phosphatase stain, the predominance of non-reactive neutrophils would indicate a low LAP score, consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia. Because the stain type and scoring cannot be verified from this image, BCR::ABL1 testing remains the definitive study.

title: Pure Red Cell Aplasia (PRCA) –  parvovirus infection - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low power shows preserved architecture with bony trabeculae and hematopoietic marrow admixed with fat, with an estimated cellularity of approximately 40-50%. No focal lesions, fibrosis, or infiltrative process are identified. Lineage composition cannot be evaluated at this magnification. Assessment for pure red cell aplasia requires higher-power review and aspirate correlation to document markedly reduced erythroid precursors and the presence of giant pronormoblasts with viral inclusions; parvovirus B19 immunohistochemistry or PCR would support the diagnosis.

title: Red Blood Cell Diseases (RBC) 1 - 4.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, suboptimally stained with poor contrast, shows mild anisocytosis with a subset of smaller, dense red cells lacking central pallor. Occasional red cells contain small dark punctate inclusions that could represent Howell-Jolly bodies or Pappenheimer bodies, although overlying platelets or stain precipitate cannot be excluded at this quality. No leukocytes are present for assessment. The findings are nonspecific; correlation with red cell indices, reticulocyte count and an iron stain is required to support an underproduction anemia.

title: Follicular Lymphoma, Grade 1/3 - 8.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen) of a lymphoid infiltrate shows a dense population of small cells with round to slightly irregular nuclei, a large proportion of which show strong membranous/cytoplasmic positivity arranged in vague nodular aggregates and sheets, with interspersed negative cells and vessels. The antigen is not indicated and the follicular architecture is not clearly evaluable in this field, so the image alone does not establish the diagnosis. In the stated context, findings may represent a B-cell or BCL2 stain in follicular lymphoma, grade 1-2, but correlation with H&E and a full panel (CD20, CD10, BCL6, BCL2, CD21) is required.

title: An unusual case of bone marrow involvement in a patient with Primary Mediastinal Germ Cell Tumor
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smears show clusters of large atypical cells with abundant gray-blue, finely vacuolated cytoplasm, large round-oval nuclei with fine chromatin and small nucleoli, forming cohesive aggregates with smaller hematopoietic cells closely apposed. These cells do not resemble normal marrow elements. On morphology alone, metastatic germ cell tumor cells cannot be separated from megakaryoblasts or malignant histiocytes, both of which occur in association with primary mediastinal nonseminomatous germ cell tumors. Findings are suggestive of marrow involvement by a non-hematopoietic or GCT-associated neoplasm; immunophenotyping (SALL4, OCT3/4, CD30, AFP, keratin versus CD41/CD61, CD163) and i(12p) testing are required.

title: Normal Lymphoid Tissues: Part 3 - 10.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain with a red chromogen on lymphoid tissue shows a diffuse sheet of medium-to-large cells with round to oval nuclei, most of which show membranous and granular cytoplasmic positivity. No clear follicular or zonal pattern is evident in this high-power field. Because the antibody is not specified, the lineage of the positive cells cannot be determined from the image, and a uniformly positive population of larger cells would need to be correlated with the H&E and additional markers before interpreting it as normal (for example, a germinal center) versus a neoplastic infiltrate.

title: Normal Lymphoid Tissues: Part 3 - 3.
describe_en: Section at high power shows an aggregate of large cells with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, indistinct cell borders and irregular, folded to grooved or lobulated nuclei with vesicular chromatin and small nucleoli. Small lymphocytes are sparse, and fibrous stroma is present at the right edge. Significant mitotic activity or marked pleomorphism is not seen. The cells have a histiocytic/dendritic cell appearance, as seen with sinus histiocytes, interdigitating dendritic cells or Langerhans cells in lymphoid tissue; precise identification requires immunohistochemistry (CD68/CD163, S100, CD1a, langerin).

title: Normal Lymphoid Tissues: Part 4 - 2.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (antigen not specified) on normal lymphoid tissue shows a secondary follicle with a pale germinal center and a dense mantle zone that are largely unstained, whereas faint brown positivity is concentrated in the interfollicular and paracortical regions, with a vessel crossing the field. The chromogen signal is weak and the counterstain heavy, so the intensity and subcellular pattern cannot be reliably assessed. The compartmental distribution most closely fits a T-zone marker, but the specific antigen cannot be determined from this image. The findings illustrate preserved normal lymphoid compartmentalization.

title: Plasma cell - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a group of cells including forms with eccentric round nuclei, coarse clumped chromatin, and grey-blue to basophilic cytoplasm consistent with plasma cells. A large cell at the lower left has abundant vacuolated cytoplasm with an eccentric nucleus, and a central cell with pale vacuolated cytoplasm is overlapped by several nuclei, which limits confident assignment of individual cells. A well-defined perinuclear hof is not clearly seen in every cell. Findings are consistent with plasma cells in a marrow aspirate; quantitation and light chain studies would be required to assess for a plasma cell neoplasm.

title: Acute Biphenotypic Leukemia - 7.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a mixed population of hematopoietic cells, including maturing granulocytes (bands and segmented forms), abundant erythroid precursors with dense round nuclei, and scattered larger immature cells with fine chromatin. Fat vacuoles and red cells are present in the background. A monotonous population of blasts is not seen in this field, so the image does not by itself demonstrate acute leukemia as the title implies; it may represent a regenerating or post-treatment marrow or a less-involved area. A formal blast count and flow cytometric assessment for residual disease are required.

title: Plasmacytoid lymphocyte - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small-to-medium lymphocyte with a round nucleus, clumped chromatin and a rim of moderately basophilic cytoplasm. The nucleus is nearly central and a perinuclear hof is not appreciated, so plasmacytoid features (eccentric nucleus, abundant deep-blue cytoplasm) are only subtle in this cell. Surrounding red cells are unremarkable apart from occasional small dot-like inclusions. Findings are compatible with a reactive lymphocyte with mild plasmacytoid differentiation; a single cell cannot establish a clonal process.

title: Aneuploid cell - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a binucleate cell with two separate, similarly sized nuclei containing coarsely clumped chromatin and a moderate rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm with peripheral accentuation. No nucleoli, granules, or vacuoles are seen. The appearance resembles a binucleate reactive (plasmacytoid) lymphocyte, a cell that may result from abnormal mitosis or failed cytokinesis. Ploidy cannot be determined from morphology; the designation 'aneuploid cell' requires cytogenetic or DNA content correlation, so the image only partially supports the title.

title: Touch imprint matters…
describe_en: Panel A shows a bone marrow touch imprint containing clusters of medium-to-large mononuclear cells with round nuclei, moderate grey-blue cytoplasm and occasional perinuclear or peripheral cytoplasmic clearing, admixed with a few small lymphocytes. Panel B shows the corresponding trephine biopsy, which is diffusely packed with a monotonous cellular infiltrate replacing normal fat and hematopoiesis, with cells separated by clear cytoplasmic spaces. Image resolution precludes assessment of fine nuclear detail and definitive lineage assignment. The figure illustrates that when a packed or fibrotic marrow yields a dry tap, a touch imprint of the core provides cytologic material; findings indicate a diffuse marrow-replacing infiltrate requiring immunophenotyping for classification.

title: Neuroblastoma - pleural fluid - 4.
describe_en: Cytospin preparation of pleural fluid shows low cellularity, with a small group of large cells having abundant vacuolated cytoplasm with ruffled borders and round central nuclei with small nucleoli, accompanied by vacuolated macrophages, a neutrophil and scattered red cells. The morphology in this field favors reactive mesothelial cells and histiocytes. No cohesive clusters of small round cells characteristic of metastatic neuroblastoma are present in this field; the image therefore only partially supports the stated diagnosis, and review of additional fields and immunocytochemistry would be required.

title: Gaucher's Disease - 4.
describe_en: Cytochemically stained smear (reaction likely PAS or acid phosphatase; exact stain not specified) shows a single large cell with abundant cytoplasm displaying strong, diffuse magenta-purple granular to fibrillary positivity, with surrounding yellow-counterstained erythrocytes. The nucleus is largely obscured, and the striated cytoplasmic texture seen on Romanowsky stains cannot be evaluated here. Strong cytoplasmic positivity in a large histiocyte is consistent with a Gaucher cell in the given context; the diagnosis should be confirmed by glucocerebrosidase assay or GBA1 testing.

title: Paraneoplastic hypercalcemia in Diffuse Large B-Cell NHL - 10.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of a bone biopsy shows bony trabeculae with an intertrabecular marrow space that is replaced by a dense cellular infiltrate, with loss of normal fat and hematopoietic elements. Dense parallel fibrocollagenous tissue is present at the left, and crushed spindled cells are seen at the lower interface. Cytologic detail is limited at this magnification, so the cell type cannot be determined from this field alone. In the clinical context, findings are compatible with marrow and bone involvement by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which requires high-power morphology and immunohistochemistry for confirmation.

title: Paraneoplastic hypercalcemia in Diffuse Large B-Cell NHL - 6.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (antigen not specified) shows sheets of discohesive medium to large round cells with strong, diffuse membranous and cytoplasmic positivity in nearly all neoplastic cells, with occasional interspersed negative cells and small vessels. The nuclei are round to oval and larger than those of small lymphocytes. The diffuse, uniform staining of a sheet-like large-cell population is typical of a lineage marker such as CD20 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, but the specific antigen cannot be confirmed from the image. Findings are supportive of the reported diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

title: Hairy Cell Leukemia - 11.
describe_en: Smear shows a single pale mononuclear cell with purple granular deposits concentrated at the periphery of the cytoplasm and a poorly delineated nucleus. Distinct hairy cytoplasmic projections are not evident, and the staining pattern raises the possibility of a cytochemical preparation rather than a routine Romanowsky stain. The surrounding red cells show slit-like central pallor, likely artifactual. Morphology in this single field is not diagnostic on its own; correlation with TRAP cytochemistry and flow cytometry (CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123) is required to support hairy cell leukemia.

title: Concomitant microfilaria and malaria infection
describe_en: Peripheral blood films show microfilariae: panel A contains a coiled larva with a column of densely packed nuclei enclosed by a pale sheath, and panel B shows an undulating larva in a thinner area of the film. The tail region and cephalic space cannot be evaluated at this magnification, so species identification (e.g., Wuchereria bancrofti versus Brugia malayi) is not possible from this image. Malaria parasites are not clearly identified in these panels, so the concomitant Plasmodium infection must be documented on separate fields or by antigen testing. Findings are consistent with sheathed microfilaremia, most likely lymphatic filariasis in this clinical setting.

title: Acute Basophilic Leukemia - 2.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several granulated cells with abundant coarse, dark basophilic granules that overlie the nucleus. Nuclei range from round to lobulated, and nuclear detail is largely obscured by the granules. Most cells at this field resemble basophils rather than unequivocal blasts, so blast enumeration and immunophenotyping (CD123, CD203c, CD13/CD33 with CD117 negativity) are needed. In the appropriate clinical and immunophenotypic context, findings are suggestive of acute basophilic leukemia, after exclusion of BCR-ABL1-positive CML.

title: Angioimmunoblastic T Cell Lymphoma - 12.
describe_en: Very low-power immunohistochemical stain (antibody not labeled) of a lymph node shows multiple irregular, geographic tan-staining zones of variable size separated by paler areas with scattered hematoxylin-stained nuclei. The stained zones are irregular rather than round and discrete. Owing to low contrast and resolution, the cellular localization of staining cannot be assessed and the antibody cannot be inferred with confidence. If this represents a follicular dendritic cell marker such as CD21 or CD23, the irregular expanded pattern would support angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.

title: Angioimmunoblastic T Cell Lymphoma - 13.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain (antibody not labeled) of a lymph node shows positive small lymphoid cells arranged in irregular, geographic aggregates and sheets, including around thick-walled hyalinized vessels, with scattered positive cells in intervening large pale areas that are largely negative. Normal compartmentalization of follicles and paracortex is not evident. Because the antibody is not identified, the lineage of the positive population cannot be determined from this image alone; in context it most likely highlights a lymphoid subset in the disrupted architecture of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.

title: Angioimmunoblastic T Cell Lymphoma - 9.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an atypical lymphoid cell with an irregular, folded and lobulated nucleus, coarsely clumped chromatin, and a moderate amount of deeply basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm. The red cells are normochromic and a small platelet clump is present. This cell has plasmacytoid or immunoblastic features; such circulating atypical lymphoid cells and plasmacytoid cells may be seen in angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, but the morphology is not specific and requires flow cytometry (for example CD10-positive, surface CD3-negative T cells) for interpretation.

title: Light chain deposition
describe_en: Kidney biopsy stained with H&E shows proximal tubules with epithelial cells distended by abundant bright eosinophilic, fractured-appearing cytoplasmic material, with focal vacuolization and cell sloughing and mild interstitial edema. Electron microscopy demonstrates numerous electron-dense rhomboid and polygonal crystalline inclusions filling the cytoplasm of the tubular epithelial cells. The powdery, non-crystalline linear deposits along tubular and glomerular basement membranes that define light chain deposition disease are not shown in these panels, so the image is only partially concordant with the title. Findings are consistent with a monoclonal light chain-related tubulopathy with intracellular crystals (light chain proximal tubulopathy/crystal-storing pattern) in the setting of an IgG monoclonal gammopathy; immunofluorescence for kappa and lambda is required to confirm light chain restriction.

title: Aplastic Crisis in a Patient with Sickle Cell Disease - 3.
describe_en: Section shows large rounded empty spaces separated by thin septa that contain sparse nucleated cells and abundant sickled erythrocytes. Vascular channels are distended and packed with aggregates of elongated sickle-shaped red cells (thick arrow), and individual sickle forms are scattered in the stroma (thin arrow). Active hematopoietic precursors, including the giant pronormoblasts of parvovirus B19 infection, are not evident in this field; tissue site cannot be determined with certainty from this image. Findings are consistent with sickle cell disease with in situ sickling and vaso-occlusion, compatible with a hypocellular marrow in the setting of aplastic crisis.

title: Toxoplasmosis - 5.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (antibody not specified) shows a band-like zone of cells with abundant pale cytoplasm displaying membranous and reticular cytoplasmic positivity, with largely negative adjacent tissue. The counterstain is faint and nuclear morphology cannot be assessed. The distribution suggests highlighting of a sinusoidal population such as monocytoid B cells or histiocytes in toxoplasma lymphadenitis, but the specific marker and cell type cannot be determined from this image alone; no organisms are identifiable.

title: Gaucher Disease - 3.
describe_en: Smear (probably bone marrow aspirate) shows a large aggregate of cells with abundant pale blue cytoplasm and indistinct borders, containing numerous small, eccentric, irregular nuclei, with scattered vacuoles and stretched crush artifact. The distinctive fibrillary, crumpled tissue paper texture of Gaucher cell cytoplasm is not clearly resolved at this resolution, so the morphology alone is only suggestive. In the proper clinical context the findings are consistent with clusters of Gaucher cells; confirmation by glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay or GBA1 genotyping is recommended.

title: Visceral leishmaniasis involving the bone marrow
describe_en: The smear shows a disrupted macrophage with numerous small round-to-oval intracellular and extruded organisms measuring roughly 2-4 µm, and a second cell containing several similar bodies; adjacent mononuclear cells lack organisms. At this resolution the characteristic nucleus and rod-shaped kinetoplast of each organism are not clearly resolved. The field has sparse nucleated cells in a red cell monolayer, resembling a peripheral blood film or a thin area of an aspirate smear rather than a cellular marrow particle. Findings are consistent with Leishmania amastigotes and support visceral leishmaniasis; confirmation by PCR, culture, or serology is recommended.

title: AML and Hgb E
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked leukocytosis composed predominantly of medium-to-large blasts with fine chromatin, visible nucleoli and basophilic cytoplasm, some forming clusters. The background red cells are microcytic with anisopoikilocytosis and occasional target cells. The bone marrow aspirate shows sheets of similar blasts, and a cytochemical stain highlights granular positivity in a subset of blasts, supporting myeloid lineage. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia; the microcytic target cell picture could reflect hemoglobin E, which must be confirmed by hemoglobin HPLC or electrophoresis.

title: Follicular Lymphoma - 10.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a lymph node shows effacement of architecture by numerous closely packed, relatively uniform follicles that stain more intensely than the internodular areas. The specific antibody is not indicated, and diffuse background staining reduces contrast; cytologic detail cannot be assessed. If this represents BCL2, positivity within germinal center-like nodules supports neoplastic follicles, as reactive germinal centers are BCL2-negative. Findings are consistent with a follicular growth pattern in keeping with follicular lymphoma.

title: Burkitt Lymphoma - 6.
describe_en: Cytologic preparation shows a population of medium to large atypical lymphoid cells with round to irregular nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, small nucleoli and scant basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with numerous neutrophils. The classic deeply basophilic cytoplasm with sharply punched-out lipid vacuoles is not convincingly demonstrated, and cell preservation is suboptimal. The atypical cells are compatible with a high-grade lymphoma, but the morphology in this field is not specific for Burkitt lymphoma; confirmation requires immunophenotyping (CD10+, BCL2-, Ki-67 near 100%) and MYC rearrangement studies.

title: Dohle Bodies - 5.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at oil immersion shows a hyposegmented neutrophil with coarse chromatin and fine purple cytoplasmic granules on a faintly grayish-blue cytoplasm. A discrete Döhle body is not clearly identifiable in this image, although subtle cytoplasmic basophilia may be present. Red cells show refractile drying artifact. Findings are only partially consistent with the labeled Döhle body; mild reactive neutrophil changes of this type are common in normal pregnancy.

title: Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Syndrome - 1.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymph node shows diffuse expansion of the nodal parenchyma, with a mottled pattern of paler zones rich in small vascular channels consistent with paracortical expansion. Well-formed secondary follicles are not apparent in this field, and a fibrous trabecula is present. Cellular composition, including the double-negative T cells characteristic of ALPS, cannot be judged at this magnification and would require high-power review and immunophenotyping (CD3+, CD4-, CD8-, TCR alpha/beta+). Findings are compatible with paracortical hyperplasia as seen in autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, but are not specific.

title: Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Syndrome - 4.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a lymph node shows preserved architecture with multiple strongly positive nodules corresponding to follicles, separated by broad, expanded interfollicular/paracortical zones that contain only scattered positive cells. The antibody is not specified in the image; the follicular distribution suggests a B-cell marker such as CD20, which would indicate that the expanded paracortex is composed of non-B cells. The architecture is not effaced. In the appropriate clinical context, the pattern of follicular hyperplasia with marked paracortical expansion is consistent with autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, pending demonstration of CD4-/CD8- TCRαβ+ double-negative T cells.

title: Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Syndrome - 6.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of lymph node shows negative follicles separated by an expanded interfollicular compartment containing a prominent positive meshwork of linear and ring-like profiles, suggestive of a rich vascular or stromal network, along with scattered positive single cells. The antibody is not labeled, which precludes precise interpretation. This pattern highlights paracortical expansion with vascular proliferation, which can accompany the florid reactive changes of autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, but it is not specific; diagnosis depends on demonstration of TCRαβ+ CD4-/CD8- double-negative T cells.

title: Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Syndrome - 7.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a lymph node (antibody not specified in the image) shows numerous positive small cells concentrated in expanded interfollicular and paracortical regions, with focal dense aggregates, while multiple round follicle-like areas are largely negative. The distribution indicates an expanded T-zone or interfollicular population rather than follicular involvement. In autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, paracortical T cells are increased and a large fraction are CD4- CD8- double-negative T cells; interpretation requires the corresponding CD3, CD4 and CD8 stains and flow cytometry.

title: Autoimmune Lymphoproliferative Syndrome - 9.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of lymphoid tissue shows a preserved, vaguely nodular architecture, with nodules containing aggregates of positive cells and scattered positive cells in the intervening compartments. The antibody is not specified, and the weak staining intensity and low magnification limit interpretation of which compartment is expanded. In the appropriate clinical setting, a reactive-appearing pattern like this is compatible with autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, but diagnosis requires demonstration of expanded TCRαβ+ CD4-/CD8- double-negative T cells and supportive genetic or biomarker studies.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Multilineage Dysplasia - 1.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows several blasts with round nuclei, fine chromatin, and moderate deeply basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with a hypogranular myeloid cell with abnormal nuclear lobation and erythroid precursors showing irregular nuclear contours. Small lymphocytes and late normoblasts are also present. The degree of multilineage dysplasia cannot be quantified from this single field. Findings are suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia with dysplastic features, compatible with AML with myelodysplasia-related changes when blast count and lineage dysplasia criteria are met.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Multilineage Dysplasia - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at medium power is cellular, with numerous blasts with fine chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm admixed with many erythroid precursors, including small dense late normoblasts, and scattered granulated myeloid precursors. A few cells show irregular nuclear contours suggestive of dysplasia, but detailed dysplastic features cannot be fully assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with a prominent erythroid component; classification as AML with myelodysplasia-related changes depends on blast count and multilineage dysplasia quantification.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Multilineage Dysplasia - 3.
describe_en: Hemodilute smear at low-to-medium power shows scattered large blasts with round nuclei and basophilic cytoplasm, monocytoid cells with folded nuclei, occasional late erythroid precursors, and small lymphocytes. A neutrophil with hypogranular cytoplasm and abnormal nuclear segmentation is present. The magnification and hemodilution limit reliable assessment of multilineage dysplasia and blast percentage. Findings are suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia with dysplastic features and should be correlated with a cellular aspirate and genetic studies for classification as AML with myelodysplasia-related changes.

title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Multilineage Dysplasia - 4.
describe_en: Thin smear area shows several blasts with round to oval nuclei, fine chromatin, and moderate basophilic cytoplasm, together with a coarsely granulated promyelocyte-like cell, a monocytoid cell with abundant pale vacuolated cytoplasm, and a small lymphocyte. The red cells are in a monolayer with mild anisocytosis. Definite multilineage dysplasia is not demonstrable in this limited field. Findings support an acute myeloid leukemia; the subclassification as AML with multilineage dysplasia requires evaluation of dysplasia across the whole aspirate.

title: Enteropathy Type T Cell Lymphoma - 3.
describe_en: Low-power section of small intestine shows mucosa with finger-like villi of mildly variable height, crypts with goblet cells, and a moderate lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the lamina propria. Submucosal adipose tissue and glands are present at the top of the field. No ulceration, mass lesion or transmural atypical lymphoid infiltrate is identified, and intraepithelial lymphocytes cannot be assessed at this magnification. The image is not diagnostic of enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma on its own and likely represents non-tumoral mucosa; correlation with the tumor sections and CD3/CD8 immunostains is needed.

title: Enteropathy Type T Cell Lymphoma - 4.
describe_en: High-power section of small-intestinal mucosa shows a villus lined by columnar enterocytes with goblet cells and scattered intraepithelial lymphocytes. The lamina propria is edematous and contains scattered lymphocytes, plasma cells and occasional eosinophils. No sheets of atypical lymphoid cells or mucosal destruction are identified in this field, and villous architecture of the illustrated villus is relatively preserved. These findings may represent mucosa adjacent to enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, but are not diagnostic by themselves; quantification of intraepithelial lymphocytes with CD3/CD8 and evaluation of the tumor are required.

title: Toxoplasmosis - 1.
describe_en: Smear (likely marrow or body fluid) shows a single histiocyte-like cell with an irregular, crumpled nucleus and pale foamy cytoplasm. A band-like basophilic structure overlies the nucleus and could represent intracellular organisms; however, the staining is faint and individual crescent-shaped tachyzoites with discrete nuclei cannot be clearly resolved at this resolution. No free extracellular organisms are identified. The image is of limited diagnostic value on its own and is only suggestive of Toxoplasma infection; confirmation by serology, PCR or immunohistochemistry is required.

title: Toxoplasmosis - 2.
describe_en: Smear at oil immersion shows a single small leukocyte, approximately the size of an adjacent red cell, with an irregular lobulated nucleus, coarse clumped chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine pinkish-purple granules and a small dark punctate inclusion. The appearance is most in keeping with a granulocyte. No crescent-shaped tachyzoites with discrete nuclei are identified, so the image does not itself demonstrate Toxoplasma organisms. The diagnosis of toxoplasmosis must rest on serology, PCR or tissue immunohistochemistry.

title: Toxoplasmosis - 3.
describe_en: Smear at high magnification shows a mononuclear cell containing two irregular, dense nucleus-like masses in pale finely granular cytoplasm, with a small dark cytoplasmic inclusion. An adjacent disrupted cell releases fine granular material, and nearby monocytoid cells have folded nuclei. Although the clustered chromatin-rich material may represent intracellular organisms, discrete crescent-shaped tachyzoites with single central nuclei cannot be confidently identified. The image is suggestive at most of Toxoplasma infection and requires confirmation by serology, PCR or immunostaining.

title: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and its complications
describe_en: Serial bone marrow aspirates and trephine biopsies are shown. The 2002 aspirate and biopsy show preserved cellularity with erythroid precursor clusters and trilineage hematopoiesis. The 2013 aspirate contains more fat and fewer hematopoietic elements, and the corresponding biopsy is markedly hypocellular, consisting predominantly of adipose tissue between bony trabeculae with only scant residual hematopoiesis. No blast increase or infiltrative process is seen at this magnification. In a patient with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, findings are consistent with progression to marrow hypoplasia (aplastic anemia/PNH overlap); the PNH clone itself must be documented by flow cytometry.

title: Plasmodium Vivax - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-to-medium power shows a single red cell containing a small ring-form parasite (arrow) with a delicate blue cytoplasmic ring and chromatin dot. The infected cell is not distinctly enlarged and no stippling, trophozoites, schizonts or gametocytes are visible in this field; red cells and neutrophils are otherwise unremarkable. Findings indicate Plasmodium infection; a single ring form does not permit speciation, so the diagnosis of P. vivax requires additional forms on thin film review, rapid antigen testing or PCR, and parasitemia should be quantified.

title: Plasmodium Vivax - 4.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a compact round body, smaller than an adjacent red cell, containing numerous punctate purple chromatin dots and associated with a pale, ghost-like host cell outline. The appearance is suggestive of a Plasmodium schizont with multiple merozoites or a parasite released from a lysed red cell. Malarial pigment, Schüffner stippling and host cell enlargement cannot be confidently assessed, and no other parasitized cells are present in this field. Findings are suggestive of, but not by themselves diagnostic of, Plasmodium vivax infection; species confirmation requires review of additional parasite stages on thick and thin films or PCR.

title: Melanin inclusions in the neutrophils of a patient  with metastatic melanoma.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a phagocytic leukocyte with an indented, non-segmented nucleus and pale, finely granular cytoplasm containing multiple coarse, irregular blue-black inclusions of variable size. The inclusions are distinctly larger and darker than toxic granulation or normal azurophilic granules.
