describe_en: Section shows diffuse sheets of large atypical cells with a somewhat cohesive growth pattern. The cells have round to oval vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli and moderate amphophilic cytoplasm; mitotic figures and apoptotic bodies are readily identified. Marked bizarre pleomorphism or hallmark horseshoe-shaped nuclei are not conspicuous in this field. The morphology is that of a high-grade large-cell lymphoma; with B-cell lineage confirmed (CD20/PAX5+), findings are consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, anaplastic variant, which may be CD30-positive and mimic ALCL or carcinoma.

title: Nucleated red blood cell - 1.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows moderate anisopoikilocytosis with numerous macro-ovalocytes, occasional teardrop-like and irregular red cells, and sparse platelets. A nucleated red blood cell with a dense, coarsely clumped nucleus and grayish-pink cytoplasm is present, with a small pale round body at its margin whose nature cannot be determined with certainty. No leukocytes, blasts or intraerythrocytic inclusions are identified in this field. In a pregnant patient with suspected acquired aplastic anemia, circulating nucleated red cells with macrocytosis and thrombocytopenia are nonspecific; bone marrow biopsy is required to establish marrow hypocellularity and exclude infiltrative or dysplastic processes.

title: Castleman lymphadenopathy - 5.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain (DAB; marker not specified, distribution typical of a B-cell marker such as CD20) on a lymph node shows numerous follicles with expanded, strongly positive mantle zones surrounding small, regressed germinal centers, while the interfollicular zones are negative. One follicle contains two germinal centers within a shared mantle, and penetrating vessels are seen within germinal centers. The preserved follicular architecture with expanded mantles and atretic centers is consistent with hyaline-vascular Castleman disease, and the absence of sheets of positive cells in interfollicular areas argues against a B-cell lymphoma effacing the node.

title: Castleman lymphadenopathy - 6.
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain (DAB; marker not specified, distribution typical of a T-cell marker such as CD3) on a lymph node shows positivity predominantly in the interfollicular zones, with only scattered positive cells within a small regressed germinal center. The surrounding broad, concentrically layered mantle zone is negative, and a vessel penetrates the germinal center. The preserved compartmentalization with expanded onion-skin mantles and an atretic, vascularized germinal center is consistent with hyaline-vascular Castleman disease.

title: Mantle cell lymphoma - 3.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows a diffuse, monotonous population of medium-sized lymphoid cells with strong, uniform membranous staining. Nuclear features are partially obscured, and the specific antigen is not identified in the image. A diffuse membranous-positive neoplastic infiltrate of this type supports a mature lymphoid neoplasm, and in combination with cyclin D1 or SOX11 nuclear positivity, CD5 co-expression, and t(11;14), it is consistent with mantle cell lymphoma.

title: Mantle cell lymphoma - 4.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (DAB; marker not specified) on a lymph node involved by a diffuse monotonous small-to-medium lymphoid proliferation shows that the neoplastic cells are negative. Scattered individual background cells show membranous to dendritic positivity without a zonal pattern. This pattern is most compatible with a marker of the non-neoplastic compartment (for example reactive T cells or histiocytes) in mantle cell lymphoma. Diagnostic confirmation rests on CD20, CD5 and cyclin D1/SOX11 staining.

title: Mantle cell lymphoma - 5.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (DAB; marker not specified) shows nuclear positivity in nearly all cells of a diffuse proliferation of medium-sized lymphoid cells with irregular nuclear contours, with variable staining intensity and rare negative background cells. If this is cyclin D1, diffuse nuclear expression in a CD5+ B-cell lymphoma is consistent with mantle cell lymphoma. If this is Ki-67, a proliferation index approaching 90% or more would indicate a highly proliferative (blastoid or pleomorphic) variant with an adverse prognosis. The marker should be confirmed before interpretation.

title: Reactive marrow: infection post-chemotherapy - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a thick marrow particle composed largely of fat vacuoles and a stromal network with clustered, poorly spread cells. Individually identifiable hematopoietic precursors are sparse, and scattered lymphocytes and occasional neutrophils are present at the particle periphery. No microorganisms, granulomas, or blast population can be identified, although the thickness of the preparation limits cytologic assessment. Findings suggest a hypocellular, stroma-rich post-chemotherapy marrow; specific features of infection are not demonstrable in this image and would require stains, cultures, and biopsy correlation.

title: Multiple myeloma and acute myeloid leukemia - 2.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is highly cellular and dominated by a population of medium to large blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, finely dispersed chromatin, occasional nucleoli, and scant agranular basophilic cytoplasm. Residual maturing neutrophils and small lymphocytes are present, while erythroid and megakaryocytic elements are sparse. A distinct neoplastic plasma cell population is not evident in this particular field, so the plasma cell myeloma component must be documented on other fields, flow cytometry, or biopsy. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia in the given clinical setting of multiple myeloma (possibly therapy-related).

title: Systemic mastocystosis - 1.
describe_en: Low-power bone marrow aspirate smear shows marrow particles with abundant fat spaces and associated hematopoietic cells. A dense, dark purple, granular cluster at the upper left may represent an aggregate of mast cells within a particle, but individual cellular detail cannot be resolved at this magnification. Neoplastic mast cells in systemic mastocytosis are typically spindled, hypogranular or with eccentric nuclei and tend to be trapped in particles; high-power evaluation and flow cytometry for CD117+/CD25+ mast cells are required. The image is only partially informative for the stated diagnosis.

title: Systemic mastocystosis - 4.
describe_en: H&E section of bone marrow biopsy shows a hypercellular marrow with decreased fat, composed predominantly of granulocytic precursors with numerous eosinophils, scattered megakaryocytes and erythroid elements. Occasional cells with oval nuclei and pale cytoplasm are present, but discrete compact aggregates of spindled mast cells are not definitely identified in this field. The findings are compatible with a myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and, in context, may represent systemic mastocytosis; immunohistochemistry for tryptase, CD117 and CD25 and KIT D816V testing are needed to document the mast cell infiltrate.

title: Systemic mastocystosis - 5.
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a sheet-like infiltrate of medium-sized round to polygonal cells with moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm, distinct borders and round central nuclei, adjacent to a bony trabecula. Spindle-shaped mast cells and a perivascular or paratrabecular fibrotic pattern are not evident in this field, so the lineage cannot be established on H&E alone. Findings are compatible with a dense mast cell infiltrate in systemic mastocytosis, but confirmation with tryptase, CD117 and CD25 immunostains is required.

title: Ruptured spleen due to infectious mononucleosis - 10.
describe_en: Immunostained section of spleen at low power shows strong positivity concentrated in the white pulp follicles, with only scattered positive cells in the red pulp. The pattern suggests a B-cell marker (e.g., CD20) highlighting preserved follicles, while the expanded red pulp infiltrate is largely negative. The specific antibody is not stated, so interpretation is limited. In the context of ruptured spleen from infectious mononucleosis, this pattern would support a polymorphous, predominantly non-B red pulp expansion rather than a diffuse B-cell lymphoma.

title: Ruptured spleen due to infectious mononucleosis - 5.
describe_en: Low-power section of spleen shows diffusely hypercellular parenchyma with effacement of the usual white pulp/red pulp distinction by a dense lymphoid infiltrate. Several pale, hypocellular amorphous areas are present, which may represent edema, fibrin deposition or hemorrhage but cannot be characterized at this magnification. Individual cell morphology, including immunoblasts, is not assessable. In the appropriate clinical setting these findings are consistent with the red pulp expansion of infectious mononucleosis predisposing to splenic rupture, but they are not specific on their own.

title: Ruptured spleen due to infectious mononucleosis - 6.
describe_en: Immunostained splenic section at medium power shows a diffuse infiltrate of small to medium lymphoid cells with membranous staining throughout the red pulp, sparing scattered pale zones that likely represent white pulp. The pattern suggests expansion of a T-cell population (e.g., CD3 or CD8), although the antibody is not labeled. In the context of infectious mononucleosis, this would be consistent with the reactive cytotoxic T-cell expansion that infiltrates the red pulp and predisposes to rupture.

title: Ruptured spleen due to infectious mononucleosis - 7.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (antigen not specified) on the splenic lesion shows a dense population of medium to large lymphoid cells with vesicular oval nuclei. A substantial subset shows granular, dot-like cytoplasmic positivity, a pattern characteristic of cytotoxic granule proteins such as TIA-1 or granzyme B, while other cells are negative. Because the marker is not stated, the exact lineage cannot be confirmed from this image alone. In context, the findings are suggestive of an expanded activated cytotoxic T-cell population, as seen in infectious mononucleosis.

title: Ruptured spleen due to infectious mononucleosis - 8.
describe_en: Immunostained splenic section at low-medium power shows many positive medium to large cells distributed diffusely through the red pulp, with relative sparing of the white pulp areas. The morphology of the positive cells suggests an activated or immunoblastic population. The specific marker is not labeled, which limits interpretation. In the context of infectious mononucleosis, a red pulp distribution of activated lymphoid cells (e.g., EBV-infected or cytotoxic T-cells) is expected and contributes to capsular infiltration and rupture.

title: Nodal involvement by adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma - 4.
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain of a lymph node (antibody not labeled) shows diffuse effacement by medium-sized lymphoid cells, the majority of which display predominantly nuclear staining of variable intensity, while high endothelial venules and stromal elements are negative. No residual follicles are appreciated. The image documents a diffuse, immunoreactive lymphoid population but does not by itself establish lineage; in the context of HTLV-1 infection and a CD4+/CD25+ T-cell phenotype, findings are consistent with nodal involvement by adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

title: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma involving the skin - 1.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of skin shows patchy superficial and mid-dermal perivascular lymphoid infiltrates, with a denser infiltrate surrounding an adnexal structure and focal extension into the lower epidermis. The epidermis shows compact orthokeratosis without prominent spongiosis. Cytologic atypia cannot be assessed at this power. In conjunction with higher-power morphology, immunophenotype and HTLV-1 status, the findings are compatible with cutaneous involvement by adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; the pattern alone is nonspecific.

title: Falciparum malarial parasite in bone marrow aspirate - 8.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of maturing erythroblasts and a larger erythroid precursor, with a large cell with pink-purple cytoplasm at the upper right. A few small purple dot-like structures overlie scattered red cells and are possibly early ring forms, but they cannot be confidently distinguished from platelets or stain precipitate at this resolution, and no pigmented trophozoites or crescent gametocytes are seen. The image therefore only partially supports the diagnosis of falciparum malaria; correlation with other fields and peripheral blood thick and thin films is required.

title: RhD Hemolytic disease of newborn
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a nucleated red blood cell with a round, dense nucleus. The red cells show anisocytosis, including larger pale polychromatophilic cells and occasional small round cells with reduced central pallor. Irregular deep-blue clumped material lies over several red cells, including one with a small dark dot; its nature is uncertain in this image and may represent overlying platelets or stain precipitate. The findings of circulating nucleated red cells and polychromasia can be seen in hemolytic disease of the newborn, but the field alone is limited and correlation with the direct antiglobulin test, maternal antibody screen and bilirubin is needed.

title: Acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia related changes PB 2
describe_en: The smear shows several large blasts with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and scant to moderate basophilic agranular cytoplasm; no Auer rods are seen. These are admixed with numerous erythroid precursors at polychromatic and orthochromatic stages, including a precursor with nuclear lobation suggestive of dyserythropoiesis. Although labeled as peripheral blood, the density of nucleated cells and clustering of erythroid precursors resemble a bone marrow aspirate, or at least a leukoerythroblastic smear; this discrepancy should be considered. Findings are consistent with increased blasts with background erythroid dysplasia, supporting acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes.

title: May-Hegglin anomaly
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, medium power, shows a single segmented neutrophil among red cells that are diffusely crenated (echinocytic), most consistent with a preparation artifact. A giant platelet approximately the size of a red cell is present in the lower right field, with only occasional normal-sized platelets, suggesting reduced platelet numbers. The characteristic large, pale blue, spindle-shaped Döhle-like cytoplasmic inclusions in the neutrophil cannot be clearly identified at this resolution, so the image only partially demonstrates the entity. In the appropriate context, findings are suggestive of an MYH9-related disorder (May-Hegglin anomaly); higher-power review of neutrophils and MYH9 immunofluorescence or genetic testing would confirm.

title: Atypical chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR-ABL1 negative 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a pair of closely apposed neutrophils, possibly a binucleate form, with hypolobated bilobed nuclei and markedly hypogranular cytoplasm. Red cells are largely unremarkable and platelets are present. This field does not capture the reported marked leukocytosis or circulating immature granulocytes. The dysgranulopoiesis shown is compatible with atypical chronic myeloid leukemia in the appropriate clinical and genetic setting, but it is not specific on its own.

title: Atypical chronic myeloid leukemia, BCR-ABL1 negative 4
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large megakaryocyte with abundant granular cytoplasm and a multilobated nucleus with connected lobes, without separated nuclear lobes or micromegakaryocytic features. Several neutrophils and bands cluster at its periphery, and a dark particle of debris or pigment overlies the cytoplasm. This field demonstrates a morphologically unremarkable megakaryocyte and is not in itself diagnostic; in the context of neutrophilic leukocytosis with dysgranulopoiesis and circulating precursors without basophilia, monocytosis or BCR::ABL1, the overall findings support atypical chronic myeloid leukemia.

title: Follicular lymphoma involving the bone marrow 1
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at scanning magnification shows a hypercellular marrow with scant fat between several bony trabeculae. Denser, more basophilic cellular bands appear to hug the surfaces of some trabeculae, raising the possibility of paratrabecular infiltrates. Cytologic detail cannot be evaluated at this power, so the nature of these infiltrates must be confirmed at higher magnification with CD20, CD10, BCL2 and BCL6 immunohistochemistry. In the given context, the paratrabecular distribution is suggestive of bone marrow involvement by follicular lymphoma.

title: Nodular lymphocyte Predominant Hodgkin lymphoma 4
describe_en: High-power H&E section of lymph node shows a dense population of small to intermediate lymphocytes. Scattered among them are larger cells with vesicular, pale chromatin, small nucleoli and folded nuclear contours, consistent with lymphocyte-predominant (LP) cells, although well-formed multilobated popcorn nuclei are not prominent in this field. There is no polymorphous inflammatory background with eosinophils or plasma cells, and no classic Reed-Sternberg cells are identified. In the context of a nodular architecture and appropriate immunophenotype (CD20+, OCT2+, CD30-, CD15-), the findings are suggestive of nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

title: Hairy cell leukemia 6
describe_en: Low-power view of a bone marrow core biopsy immunostain shows an extensive diffuse and interstitial infiltrate with strong positivity replacing much of the marrow space and extending between adipocytes. No nodular or paratrabecular architecture is evident. The specific antibody is not stated and cytologic detail cannot be assessed at this magnification. In the clinical context, findings are consistent with diffuse marrow involvement by hairy cell leukemia, highlighted by a lymphoid (likely B-cell) marker.

title: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma 3
describe_en: Low-power section shows extensive geographic coagulative necrosis composed of ghost cell outlines, eosinophilic debris, and scattered karyorrhectic nuclear fragments. A small vessel with a thickened wall and fibrin-containing lumen is present at the lower left, and a thin rim of residual viable lymphoid cells is seen at the right. Viable tumor cells are not evaluable in this field, so the image alone is not diagnostic. In a nasal/upper aerodigestive tract biopsy, such zonal necrosis with vascular injury is characteristic of extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, and additional sampling of viable tissue with CD3, CD56, cytotoxic markers, and EBER ISH is required.

title: Acanthocyte
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked poikilocytosis. Several small, dense red cells lacking central pallor carry irregular, unevenly distributed spicules of varying length, consistent with acanthocytes (spur cells). Numerous additional red cells show regular, short, evenly spaced crenations with preserved central pallor, resembling echinocytes; these may be partly artifactual (thick area/slow drying) and should be assessed in a well-spread area. Findings are consistent with acanthocytosis, as seen in liver disease, with admixed echinocyte-like forms.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows diffuse membranous and cytoplasmic positivity in the majority of small-to-medium lymphoid cells, some slightly enlarged with mildly irregular nuclei. Negative cells with larger oval pale nuclei and abundant cytoplasm, consistent with epithelioid histiocytes, are interspersed throughout. The antibody is not labeled, so the lineage marker cannot be named from the image, though the pattern fits a T-cell-associated antigen. In the context of the title, the findings support a T-cell-predominant infiltrate with abundant histiocytes, compatible with lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows diffuse membranous positivity in a dense population of small-to-medium lymphoid cells with mildly irregular nuclei. Interspersed negative cells with pale oval nuclei and abundant cytoplasm, consistent with epithelioid histiocytes, and small negative vessels are also present. The antibody is not labeled, so the specific lineage marker cannot be read from the image, although the membranous pattern in the predominant lymphoid population is typical of a pan-T-cell marker such as CD3 or CD2. In the context of the title, the findings are compatible with the T-cell-predominant infiltrate of lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS, which requires assessment for aberrant antigen loss and TCR clonality.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows crisp membranous positivity in numerous small-to-medium lymphoid cells with mildly irregular nuclei, arranged singly and in small clusters. They are intermixed with negative cells bearing oval to elongated pale nuclei and abundant cytoplasm, consistent with epithelioid histiocytes. The antibody is not labeled, so the marker cannot be identified from the image, although the membranous pattern in lymphoid cells is typical of a T-cell antigen. In the context of the title, the image illustrates the T-cell infiltrate admixed with numerous epithelioid histiocytes in lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows strong membranous and cytoplasmic staining in a subset of scattered, irregularly shaped small-to-medium lymphoid cells, evenly distributed through the infiltrate. The majority of the cells, including larger cells with pale oval nuclei resembling epithelioid histiocytes, are negative, with only faint background blush. The antibody is not labeled, so it cannot be determined from the image which lineage subset is highlighted; a pattern like this would be expected with a T-cell subset marker (such as CD8) or a cytotoxic marker. In the context of the title, this represents part of the immunophenotypic workup of lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain of a lymphoid lesion shows scattered large cells with abundant cytoplasm and oval pale nuclei displaying granular cytoplasmic and membranous positivity, distributed among a dense population of negative small-to-medium lymphoid cells. The morphology of the positive cells favors histiocytes, but the antibody is not specified and the stained population cannot be definitively assigned from the image. In the context of the title, the image highlights the numerous interspersed epithelioid histiocytes characteristic of lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Section at medium power shows a dense, diffuse infiltrate of small-to-medium lymphoid cells with irregular hyperchromatic nuclei, extending into surrounding fibrous tissue and adipose tissue where it encircles individual fat cells. Small, ill-defined clusters of pale epithelioid histiocytes are interspersed within the infiltrate, but they are not conspicuous at this magnification. No residual follicles or necrosis are seen. The image supports a diffuse atypical lymphoid infiltrate with extranodal/perinodal extension; in the context of the title it is compatible with lymphoepithelioid (Lennert) variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS, which requires high-power assessment and T-cell immunophenotyping with clonality studies.

title: Lymphoepitheliod cell ("Lennert's") lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain of a lymphoid lesion shows numerous scattered small-to-medium cells with coarse granular cytoplasmic positivity, distributed among a background of negative cells with pale oval to reniform nuclei and abundant cytoplasm resembling epithelioid histiocytes. The antibody is not specified, so the stained population cannot be definitively assigned; a granular cytoplasmic pattern of this kind is typical of cytotoxic granule proteins (TIA-1, granzyme B, perforin) or lysosomal markers such as CD68. In the context of the title, the image illustrates the mixed population of lymphoepithelioid cell (Lennert) lymphoma, a variant of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS, in which neoplastic T cells frequently show a cytotoxic phenotype amid abundant epithelioid histiocytes.

title: EATL Type I
describe_en: Composite immunohistochemical figure of small-intestinal tissue compares tumor areas with the adjacent mucosa. In the lymphoma areas, one marker stains a dense infiltrate diffusely, a second highlights only scattered cells with the tumor cells negative, and a third shows strong staining in sheets of medium-to-large atypical lymphoid cells. In the adjacent enteropathic mucosa, the same markers highlight markedly increased intraepithelial lymphocytes within surface and crypt epithelium. Because the antibodies are not labeled, the specific phenotype cannot be read from the image alone; in the context of the title, the pattern of a T-cell tumor with an adjacent intraepithelial lymphocytosis is consistent with enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (classic EATL, formerly type I), typically CD3+, CD4-, CD8-, CD56-, often CD30+.

title: Chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normochromic red cells, some with slit-like central pallor, and adequate scattered platelets. Two medium-sized lymphocytes are present with round to slightly irregular nuclei, coarse mature chromatin, no nucleoli, and a moderate rim of pale cytoplasm. Cytoplasmic azurophilic granules are not clearly resolved in this field, so large granular lymphocyte morphology is only suggested. In a patient with years of stable lymphocytosis and an NK-cell phenotype on flow cytometry, findings are consistent with chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells.

title: Plasma cell leukemia 3
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows marked rouleaux formation, with red cells stacked in long, branching chains across the field, suggesting a high concentration of serum immunoglobulin. A single cell with deeply basophilic cytoplasm is present centrally, but the magnification and resolution do not allow confident identification as a plasma cell. Leukocytosis is not appreciable in this field. The rouleaux supports a paraproteinemia, and in the given clinical context the findings are suggestive of a plasma cell neoplasm such as plasma cell leukemia; higher-power review and a quantitative plasma cell count are required.

title: Reed Sternberg Cells 2
describe_en: Lymph node section at high power shows a large atypical cell with abundant pale cytoplasm set in a retraction space, containing two apposed vesicular nuclei with thin nuclear membranes and a prominent inclusion-like eosinophilic macronucleolus. The background consists of small lymphocytes, histiocytes and scattered eosinophils. Although the image caption describes a mononuclear variant, the depicted cell appears bilobed/binucleate at this plane of section. Findings are consistent with a Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cell of classic Hodgkin lymphoma; confirmation with CD30, CD15, PAX5 (weak) and CD45 negativity is recommended.

title: Cloaked in a starry sky
describe_en: Low-power H&E section shows lymphoid tissue with multiple ill-defined nodules surrounded by small lymphocytes, without obvious diffuse effacement at this magnification. A nuclear immunostain highlights two sharply circumscribed nodules with near-uniform strong nuclear positivity, whereas the remaining nodules and interfollicular regions show only scattered positive nuclei. The starry-sky pattern cannot be assessed at this resolution, and the antibody is not labeled; high-power morphology, MYC FISH and a complete B-cell phenotype (CD10, BCL6, BCL2 negative) are required. In the stated context, findings are suggestive of Burkitt lymphoma with a follicular/nodular (in situ-like) distribution cloaked within otherwise preserved lymphoid tissue.

title: Revision of the diagnosis of a case of hereditary hemolytic anemia by supravital staining
describe_en: Supravitally stained peripheral blood smear shows that the large majority of red cells contain dark blue precipitated material, ranging from fine reticular networks to coarse clumped granular inclusions (arrow). The pattern indicates marked reticulocytosis with intraerythrocytic precipitates rather than the uniform golf-ball stippling of hemoglobin H. At this magnification reticulocyte RNA cannot be reliably distinguished from membrane-bound Heinz bodies, which should be confirmed with crystal violet staining, heat/isopropanol stability testing and globin gene sequencing. Findings are suggestive of hereditary hemolytic anemia due to an unstable hemoglobin.

title: Chance identification of synchronous hairy cell leukemia and plasma cell myeloma in a potential HSC donor
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous medium-sized lymphoid cells with oval to bean-shaped nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm with irregular margins, consistent with hairy cells. Admixed is a large atypical plasma cell with an eccentric nucleus, prominent perinuclear hof and basophilic cytoplasm. A dual-color immunohistochemical stain on the core biopsy highlights two distinct populations (red cytoplasmic/membranous and brown nuclear staining); the specific markers are not labeled in this figure. In conjunction with flow cytometry (CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123) and plasma cell clonality studies, findings are consistent with concurrent hairy cell leukemia and plasma cell neoplasm.

title: Graft-versus-leukemia in the bone marrow
describe_en: The post-transplant bone marrow biopsy (H&E) shows a cellular infiltrate composed of intermediate to large atypical cells intermixed with numerous small lymphocytes and histiocytes. A panel of immunohistochemical stains demonstrates a dense population of positively staining lymphoid cells with membranous and cytoplasmic patterns, closely apposed to negative larger residual cells, while another stain shows granular dot-like positivity in a subset of cells. Because the antibodies are not identified in the figure, lineage cannot be assigned from the image alone. In the appropriate post-transplant context, findings are suggestive of a donor T-cell infiltrate targeting residual leukemia (graft-versus-leukemia effect), which should be supported by chimerism studies and immunophenotyping.

title: FISH: negative. Morphology: positive.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows sheets of abnormal promyelocytes with round to folded nuclei, fine chromatin, and abundant cytoplasm filled with coarse azurophilic granules. Several cells contain bundles of numerous needle-like Auer rods (faggot cells), and occasional cells show bilobed nuclei with less granular cytoplasm. Normal granulocytic maturation beyond the promyelocyte stage is markedly reduced. The morphology is characteristic of acute promyelocytic leukemia; a negative PML::RARA FISH result should prompt RT-PCR or sequencing for a cryptic/submicroscopic PML::RARA insertion or a variant RARA fusion. Note that the assigned category (EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder) does not correspond to this image.

title: EBV-driven HIV-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma causing profound lactic acidosis
describe_en: Tissue section (panel A) shows squamous mucosa with an underlying hemorrhagic stroma infiltrated by atypical, hyperchromatic large lymphoid cells; the yellow color cast of the image limits cytologic detail. The marrow biopsy (panel B) shows a fatty marrow in which numerous large cells display dark nuclear signal, consistent with EBER in situ hybridization highlighting EBV-infected tumor cells (the stain is not labeled in the image). No specific B-cell marker staining is shown. In an HIV-positive patient, findings are consistent with EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving mucosa and bone marrow, a setting in which a high tumor burden can cause type B lactic acidosis (Warburg effect).

title: Pancytopenia in a patient with methylmalonic acidemia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (inset) shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with macro-ovalocytes, fragmented forms, and circulating nucleated red cells with nuclear irregularity. The bone marrow aspirate shows erythroid precursors with enlarged nuclei and finely dispersed, sieve-like chromatin and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, consistent with megaloblastoid erythropoiesis; granulocytic and megakaryocytic lineages cannot be adequately assessed in this field. Several dark-rimmed refractile ring-shaped objects over red cells are most likely preparation artifact. In a patient with methylmalonic acidemia, findings are consistent with megaloblastic-type ineffective hematopoiesis due to impaired cobalamin-dependent metabolism rather than true marrow aplasia.

title: Rapid evolution of intracranial myeloid sarcoma in 4 weeks: images in blood
describe_en: Serial axial MRI images (panels A-C) show a right temporal lesion that progresses from a subtle area of hyperintensity to a large contrast-enhancing mass with mass effect over approximately four weeks. Biopsy (H&E, panel D) shows a diffuse, sheet-like infiltrate of monotonous immature mononuclear cells with fine chromatin and scant cytoplasm, without cohesive epithelial architecture. The accompanying immunostains (panels E and F) show diffuse tumor-cell positivity, but the antigens are not labeled and the image color quality limits interpretation. In the appropriate context with myeloid marker expression (e.g., MPO, CD33, CD117), findings are consistent with intracranial myeloid sarcoma.

title: An unusual cause of ascites
describe_en: Axial contrast-enhanced CT shows hepatosplenomegaly without a discrete hepatic mass. The liver biopsy shows preserved hepatocyte plates with fine pigment and numerous dark purple-black cell clusters distributed within the sinusoids and portal areas; the stain is not labeled, but the appearance suggests a chromogenic in situ hybridization or immunostain highlighting an infiltrating cell population. In the context of a plasma cell neoplasm, findings are suggestive of diffuse sinusoidal hepatic infiltration by neoplastic plasma cells as the cause of portal hypertension and ascites; the marker identity and light chain restriction should be confirmed from the original report.

title: T-cell primary effusion lymphoma with pseudo-monoclonal rearrangements for immunoglobulin heavy chain
describe_en: Cytologic preparation of the effusion shows large atypical lymphoid cells with irregular nuclei, coarse chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm. Flow cytometry plots and immunostains (markers not labeled/legible in the figure) characterize the population, with one marker diffusely positive, one showing nuclear positivity in most cells and one negative. Fragment analysis demonstrates a dominant TRG peak as well as a dominant IGH FR3 peak. In context, findings are consistent with a T-cell lymphoma presenting as a primary effusion-based lymphoma, with the IGH peak representing a pseudo-monoclonal result (limited template or cross-lineage rearrangement) that should not override the immunophenotype.

title: Rare and strange invader
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular and contains, in addition to trilineage hematopoiesis, a population of large atypical epithelioid cells with abundant pale cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. An immunostain (marker not labeled in the figure) highlights scattered, partly elongated cells. The findings are suggestive of marrow infiltration by a non-hematopoietic malignancy; the specific tumor type cannot be established from this image alone and requires a full IHC panel (cytokeratin, S100/SOX10, melanocytic and lineage-specific markers) with clinical correlation.

title: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma involving bone marrow
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a focal lesion that replaces normal hematopoietic elements and is composed of fibrous stroma with spindled fibroblasts and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate of small lymphocytes, histiocytes and occasional eosinophils. Scattered larger cells with vesicular nuclei are present, although unequivocal Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells are not clearly identified at this magnification. In a patient with classical Hodgkin lymphoma, the fibrotic mixed-cell lesion is consistent with marrow involvement; immunostains for CD30, CD15, PAX5 (weak) and CD45 are recommended to highlight the neoplastic cells.

title: Cabot ring
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with macro-ovalocytes, teardrop cells and small fragmented red cells. Two red cells with diffuse purple staining and fine stippling are present; within the upper central cell a faint curvilinear inclusion is barely perceptible, which may represent a Cabot ring, although a well-formed ring or figure-eight loop cannot be confidently resolved at this image resolution. Platelets are sparse and no leukocytes are present in the field. The red cell changes are suggestive of megaloblastic anemia, in keeping with the stated vitamin B12 deficiency; the Cabot ring itself is only equivocally demonstrated.

title: A rare histologic variant of a common lymphoma
describe_en: Lymph node sections show effacement of architecture by numerous back-to-back neoplastic follicles. The follicles are expanded by pale eosinophilic, acellular amorphous material in which neoplastic follicle center cells are dispersed, while interfollicular areas contain small dark lymphocytes. Immunostains show intense staining of the intrafollicular deposits in one panel, nuclear positivity of intrafollicular cells in another, and diffuse strong lymphoid staining in a third; antigens are not labeled in the figure. In the context of the stated diagnosis, findings are consistent with follicular lymphoma with intrafollicular extracellular eosinophilic (proteinaceous) deposits, a rare histologic variant; Congo red and immunoglobulin stains help characterize the material.

title: Auer rod-like inclusions in multiple myeloma 1
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows an isolated elongated plasma cell with an eccentric nucleus, clumped chromatin and deeply basophilic cytoplasm with slightly frayed borders. Faint pink-purple linear striations are seen over the cytoplasm and nucleus, possibly representing azurophilic rod-like inclusions, although they are not sharply resolved at this magnification. Scattered red cells show crenation artifact. The image is compatible with a plasma cell containing Auer rod-like inclusions as described in the myeloma case, but the inclusions are only partially demonstrated.

title: Auer rod-like inclusions in multiple myeloma 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows two closely apposed plasma cells, possibly a binucleate form, with round eccentric nuclei, clumped chromatin and abundant intensely basophilic cytoplasm with a fibrillary, frayed border. Faint pink-purple filamentous material is present within the cytoplasm, but discrete rod-shaped azurophilic inclusions are not clearly resolved at this resolution. The red cells in the background show drying artifact. The plasma cells are compatible with the reported myeloma, but the Auer rod-like inclusions in the title are only partially demonstrated in this field.

title: Free and intracellular bacteria on peripheral blood smear
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous small, darkly basophilic bacteria forming two aggregates, one lying free on disrupted cytoplasmic debris and one packed within a neutrophil. Adjacent neutrophils show marked cytoplasmic vacuolization with fine granular debris, in keeping with phagocytosis and cell degeneration. On Wright-Giemsa stain the organisms appear as short rods or paired coccoid forms; morphology on a Romanowsky-stained smear cannot reliably distinguish cocci from coccobacilli or identify species, so correlation with Gram stain and blood culture (reported as Staphylococcus capitis) is essential. Findings are consistent with overwhelming bacteremia with both free and phagocytosed organisms.

title: A case of bad Carma!
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymphoid tissue shows numerous pale follicle-like nodules of variable size within a densely cellular background. An immunostain (antibody not specified) highlights the rims surrounding the nodules and the interfollicular areas, whereas the nodule centers are largely negative with only scattered positive cells (arrows). The architecture is altered but the findings are nonspecific at this magnification, and a CARD11/CARMA1-related immunodeficiency cannot be diagnosed on morphology alone; correlation with lineage-specific immunostains, flow cytometry of lymphocyte subsets and genetic testing is required. The image is only partially informative for the stated entity.

title: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma with EBV-infected “anaplastic” B-cell proliferation confined to sinuses
describe_en: Lymph node sections show architectural effacement by a diffuse atypical lymphoid infiltrate, with immunostains highlighting an extensive T-cell population. In addition, large pleomorphic cells with abundant cytoplasm and bizarre nuclei are present, distributed within and confined to lymph node sinuses, where they are highlighted by further immunostains and a nuclear stain pattern suggestive of EBER in situ hybridization. The specific markers are not labeled in the figure and cytology is limited by resolution. Findings are consistent with peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS, accompanied by an EBV-driven large B-cell proliferation with anaplastic morphology restricted to sinuses, which should not be mistaken for anaplastic large cell lymphoma or a composite B-cell lymphoma.

title: A man with low back pain and anemia
describe_en: Note: the record description refers to MRI STIR signal changes of the lumbar spine, but the image provided is a bone marrow aspirate smear rather than a radiologic study. The smear shows a mixed hematopoietic population with granulocytic precursors, an eosinophil and small lymphocytes, together with several plasma cells showing eccentric nuclei, coarse chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm. A large cell at the lower right contains multiple round nuclei within abundant blue cytoplasm, favoring a multinucleated plasma cell over an osteoclast. The yellow color cast limits evaluation of subtle cytoplasmic features. Plasma cell quantification on a well-stained smear and CD138/light-chain studies are required; findings are suggestive of a plasma cell neoplasm in the appropriate clinical context.

title: aCML marrow
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is thick and heavily overstained, with nucleated cells appearing as dark blue masses lacking discernible chromatin or cytoplasmic detail, crenated red cells and abundant granular background debris. A large oval cell in the center with homogeneous pale blue staining may represent a mononuclear or hypolobated megakaryocyte, but this cannot be confirmed. A cellular particle is present at the right edge, suggesting a cellular specimen. Owing to staining and thickness artifacts, lineage assignment and dysplasia assessment are not possible from this image, and the findings are only nonspecifically compatible with the stated diagnosis of atypical CML.

title: Hematogones
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear from a child shows a cellular particle-adjacent field containing a cluster of medium-sized immature mononuclear cells with round nuclei, fine homogeneous chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and a variable rim of basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with maturing granulocytic precursors and occasional small mature lymphocytes. The cells lack overt nuclear atypia or prominent nucleoli. Although submitted as hematogones, several cells in this cluster have more abundant, deeply basophilic cytoplasm than classic hematogones and overlap morphologically with early erythroid precursors or blasts. Morphology alone cannot reliably separate hematogones from lymphoblasts; flow cytometry demonstrating a normal, continuous B-cell maturation pattern (CD34/CD10/CD20/CD19) is required for confirmation.

title: Leishmania bodies
describe_en: Smear from the provided bone marrow aspirate shows sparse cellularity with scattered red cells and a mononuclear cell containing a few azurophilic granules. The arrow highlights a small extracellular oval body, much smaller than a red cell, with a nucleus and an adjacent dark punctate structure suggestive of a kinetoplast, compatible with a Leishmania amastigote. A second dark inclusion overlying a red cell is of uncertain significance. Intracellular amastigotes within macrophages are not seen in this field, and a single organism at this resolution is not definitive. Findings are suggestive of Leishmania bodies; review of additional fields for parasitized macrophages, culture, or PCR is recommended.

title: Leishmania bodies
describe_en: Smear field composed mainly of red cells with scattered small debris. A single small oval body overlying a red cell contains a dense purple chromatin dot and could represent a free amastigote, but a distinct nucleus plus rod-shaped kinetoplast cannot be resolved at this magnification. No macrophages containing organisms are seen in this particular field. Therefore the image only partially supports the stated diagnosis of leishmaniasis; examination of histiocyte-rich areas for clusters of amastigotes with a nucleus and kinetoplast, or PCR/culture, is needed for confirmation.

title: Giant granule and platelets...
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, two fields with an inset. Red cells are largely normocytic and normochromic. A giant platelet approaching the size of a red cell, with abundant azurophilic granules and no nucleus, is present next to a lymphocyte. Arrows mark small granular purple bodies lying on or beside red cells, which on close inspection have the appearance of platelets rather than true intraerythrocytic inclusions. The image alone does not establish the specific underlying disorder referenced by the title; findings should be interpreted with platelet count and clinical history.

title: AIHA
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows anisocytosis with many enlarged round red cells and occasional smaller dense cells lacking central pallor, suggestive of spherocytes. No agglutinates, schistocytes or nucleated red cells are seen in this field; platelets appear adequate. The color cast of the photograph limits recognition of polychromasia, and spherocytes are not prominent in this image. In the context of a positive direct antiglobulin test with a warm IgG antibody, findings are consistent with warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

title: Gaucher disease 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large histiocyte with a small eccentric nucleus and abundant pale blue-gray cytoplasm containing fine granules and a faint fibrillary texture approaching a wrinkled tissue-paper appearance. The cytoplasm is not vacuolated or foamy. The background is crowded and poorly stained, and the characteristic striations are less distinct than in classic examples. In an infant with anemia and massive hepatosplenomegaly, findings are consistent with a Gaucher cell, and diagnosis should be confirmed by glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay and GBA1 genotyping.

title: Helmet cell
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear is weakly stained and shows red cells with frequent crenation and abundant intracellular refractile dots attributable to drying/water artifact. A few fragmented red cells with straight cut edges and pointed projections resembling helmet cells, as well as small irregular fragments, are present, and platelets appear decreased in the field. The artifact limits quantification of schistocytes and assessment of polychromasia. In the clinical context of SLE with seizure and thrombocytopenia, the fragmented cells are compatible with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (TTP), but a well-stained smear is needed for a reliable schistocyte count.

title: plasma cell leukemia 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large cell with an eccentric round nucleus containing a distinct nucleolus and abundant homogeneous deep blue cytoplasm, consistent with an immature circulating plasma cell. Background red cells show rouleaux-like stacking and refractile artifacts limit evaluation. Because only one cell is shown, the proportion of circulating plasma cells cannot be determined from this image. In a myeloma patient with leukocytosis, a differential count showing ≥5% circulating clonal plasma cells supports plasma cell leukemia; flow cytometry (CD38/CD138, light-chain restriction) is recommended.

title: plasma cell leukemia 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single circulating plasma cell with an eccentric round nucleus, coarse chromatin, and deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a perinuclear hof. Background red cells show rouleaux-like stacking, and refractile debris artifacts are present. Only one plasma cell is shown, so the proportion of circulating plasma cells cannot be assessed from this image. In a patient with myeloma and leukocytosis, a manual differential showing ≥5% circulating plasma cells (current WHO/IMWG threshold; historically ≥20%) would support plasma cell leukemia.

title: Cystic splenomegaly: ectopic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary
describe_en: Contrast CT shows marked splenic enlargement due to a large, thin-walled cystic lesion with fine septations. Histologic sections show a cyst wall lined by an epithelial layer overlying compressed splenic parenchyma, and immunostains highlight the lining epithelium. The antibodies are not labeled and cytologic atypia cannot be judged at the available resolution. In context, findings are consistent with a cystic splenic lesion lined by epithelium; correlation with keratin/CK7/CK20/CDX2/TTF-1 profile and exclusion of a mesothelial or true epithelial cyst is needed to support metastatic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary.

title: CART attack
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a hypercellular marrow containing a discrete, densely cellular nodule (outlined) composed of small to intermediate cells with high N:C ratios. An immunostain shows diffuse positivity within the nodule, whereas a second immunostain highlights a population of cells largely surrounding the nodule with only scattered small clusters within it. The antibodies are not labeled in the figure and cytologic detail is limited by image resolution. In a patient with B-lymphoblastic leukemia treated with CAR T cells, the pattern suggests a residual/relapsing blast focus with peripheral T-cell infiltration; correlation with CD19, CD22, TdT and CD3 stains and flow cytometry for antigen loss is required.

title: CD25 IHC
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD25 on a densely cellular infiltrate composed of medium to large cells with oval to reniform nuclei and moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm. Only scattered cells show weak, fine granular cytoplasmic staining; the majority of the infiltrate lacks definite reactivity, and the dot-like pattern should be distinguished from pigment or nonspecific deposits. Interpretation requires correlation with CD117 and tryptase stains on the same infiltrate; aberrant CD25 expression by mast cells, if confirmed, supports systemic mastocytosis, here in the context of mast cell leukemia.

title: Mast cell Leukemia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low power shows normochromic red cells with several segmented neutrophils and small lymphocytes. One cell contains abundant coarse, dark purple metachromatic granules that spill beyond an indistinct cytoplasmic border and obscure the nucleus, consistent with a circulating mast cell rather than a basophil, although distinction is limited at this magnification. A single such cell is insufficient to quantify leukemic involvement; a manual differential and marrow evaluation (mast cells ≥20% in the aspirate) are required. Findings are suggestive of circulating mast cells in the setting of mast cell leukemia.

title: Microfilaria entangled within marrow particles
describe_en: Low-power view of a bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular marrow particle containing fat vacuoles and cellular trails extending from it. At this magnification and image quality, the microfilaria described as entangled within the particle cannot be distinctly identified; high-power examination of the particle edges is required. In the stated clinical context of pancytopenia with microfilariae seen in blood and marrow, the image documents the particle in which the parasite was found, but it is not independently diagnostic of filariasis.

title: Peripheral blood film shows normal RBC density with normocytic normochromic cells, few acanthocytes and fewer target cells.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells of normal density that are largely normocytic and normochromic. Scattered spiculated red cells are present, most with regular short projections more in keeping with echinocytes, and a few with irregular spicules resembling acanthocytes; target cells are not convincingly seen in this field. A small lymphocyte and adequate platelets are present. The morphology is nonspecific and does not by itself indicate a hemoglobinopathy; correlation with the HPLC finding of a large peak in the HbA2 window is required.

title: Giant platelets 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a giant platelet approaching red cell size with preserved purple granulation, contrasting with a normal-sized platelet nearby. Two neutrophils show normal granulation without obvious Döhle-like cytoplasmic inclusions, and red cells are unremarkable. Only a single giant platelet is present in this low-resolution field, so the degree of macrothrombocytopenia cannot be assessed. The finding is compatible with an inherited macrothrombocytopenia such as Bernard-Soulier syndrome, which requires absent ristocetin-induced agglutination and reduced GPIb-IX-V expression by flow cytometry for confirmation.

title: Low power: H&E
describe_en: H&E section of lymph node at intermediate power shows a dense mixed infiltrate of small lymphocytes and plasma cells with scattered aggregates of large histiocytes having abundant pale cytoplasm and round vesicular nuclei. A few histiocytes appear to harbor intracytoplasmic lymphocytes, although emperipolesis is not well resolved at this magnification. Dilated sinuses are not clearly demonstrated in this particular field. The findings are suggestive of Rosai-Dorfman disease, best confirmed by higher-power demonstration of emperipolesis and S100-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes.

title: Classical Reed-Sternberg cell
describe_en: Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large binucleate cell with two symmetric, round nuclei with fine chromatin and moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm, set in a mixed background of lymphocytes, plasma cells and maturing granulocytes. The prominent inclusion-like nucleoli typical of Reed-Sternberg cells are not clearly discernible at this image resolution. The appearance is suggestive of a Reed-Sternberg-type cell in classical Hodgkin lymphoma involving marrow, but aspirate findings alone are not diagnostic; trephine biopsy with CD30, CD15 and PAX5 (weak) immunohistochemistry is required.

title: Metastatic breast cancer cells
describe_en: Low-power view of a Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular spread with scattered fat vacuoles. An aggregate of larger, darker-staining cells (arrow) stands out from the dispersed hematopoietic cells, suggesting a cohesive cell cluster. Nuclear and cytoplasmic detail cannot be evaluated at this magnification, and dense thick areas limit interpretation. The finding is suggestive of metastatic tumor clusters but requires high-power examination and immunohistochemical confirmation on the trephine biopsy.

title: Wright stain 4
describe_en: Low-power view of a Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cellular spread with scattered fat vacuoles and hematopoietic elements. Several discrete, cohesive clusters of larger cells stand out from the dispersed marrow cells. Cytologic detail cannot be assessed at this magnification, and a thick particle at the upper right is not interpretable. In the appropriate clinical context, cohesive clusters are suggestive of metastatic non-hematopoietic tumor; high-power review and correlation with the core biopsy and immunohistochemistry are required.

title: Neuroblastoma in BM 3
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows scattered pink fibrillary aggregates with a lacy texture, overlapped by red cells, together with scattered small round cells with dense nuclei and scant cytoplasm and occasional maturing granulocytes. Cohesive tumor clusters or Homer Wright rosettes are not clearly seen in this field, and the color cast and focus limit assessment of chromatin and cytoplasmic detail. The fibrillary material may represent neuropil or crushed tumor cells, but this is not definitive on this image alone. Findings are suggestive of, but not diagnostic for, marrow involvement by neuroblastoma; correlation with other fields, biopsy and immunohistochemistry (PHOX2B, synaptophysin, CD56) is required.

title: Lymphocyte morphology
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two lymphocytes against a background of normocytic red cells and adequate platelets with occasional clumps. The lower-left cell is a small lymphocyte with a dense round nucleus and a narrow rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm, consistent with a reactive, plasmacytoid lymphocyte. The upper-right cell is larger with an eccentric nucleus and more abundant pale cytoplasm, consistent with a large granular lymphocyte, although cytoplasmic azurophilic granules are not well resolved at this magnification. These findings illustrate normal lymphocyte morphologic variants.

title: Hemophagocytosis
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows several large macrophages with abundant foamy, vacuolated cytoplasm. Multiple hematopoietic cells, including neutrophils and immature myeloid precursors, are situated within the macrophage cytoplasm, consistent with phagocytosis of hematopoietic elements. Preparation quality is suboptimal with poorly spread red cells and streak artifact, and overlap cannot be fully excluded for every cell. Findings are suggestive of hemophagocytosis; correlation with clinical and laboratory HLH criteria (ferritin, soluble CD25, cytopenias, fever, splenomegaly) is recommended.

title: AML - Auer Rod
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single intermediate-sized blast with a round, slightly eccentric nucleus, finely dispersed chromatin, and a moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm lacking obvious granules. A thin, dark, needle-shaped linear inclusion is present along the right nuclear border, most suggestive of an Auer rod, although it is subtle and partly overlies the nucleus at this magnification. Red cells and platelets are unremarkable. If the inclusion is confirmed as an Auer rod (e.g., by MPO staining), the finding establishes myeloid lineage and is consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.

title: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (PDC)
describe_en: Section shows a dense, cohesive-appearing aggregate of monotonous intermediate-sized cells with oval to indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a moderate amount of pale eosinophilic cytoplasm. Normal hematopoietic elements and fat are not appreciated in this field. The morphology is compatible with a cluster of plasmacytoid dendritic cells, but H&E alone cannot establish lineage; confirmation with CD123, TCF4, and CD303 and assessment of CD56 expression is required to distinguish reactive/clonal PDC nodules from blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

title: SMZL (CD20)
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy immunostained for CD20 shows strongly positive B cells located predominantly within dilated sinusoids, forming linear and branching intravascular cords, with CD20-negative hematopoietic elements in the intervening marrow. The positive cells appear medium to large with vesicular nuclei. An intrasinusoidal B-cell infiltrate is characteristic of splenic marginal zone lymphoma; however, the relatively large cell size in this field also raises intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, which the case history indicates coexisted. Correlation with H&E cytology, Ki-67, CD5, and clinical findings is required.

title: Low magnification, H&E
describe_en: Low-power examination shows a dense, band-like lymphohistiocytic infiltrate extending from the ulcerated surface deep into smooth muscle bundles and the adjacent adipose tissue, with a relatively sharp deep interface. Pale eosinophilic areas at the lower left likely correspond to fibrinoid necrosis or ulcer bed, although a distinct necrotic surface slough is not clearly identified in this field. Cytologic detail cannot be assessed at this magnification. The architecture of a deep, well-circumscribed ulcer-associated infiltrate is compatible with EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer in the appropriate clinical and immunophenotypic context.

title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with strong aberrant expression of CD31
describe_en: Needle core biopsy shows diffuse effacement by sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells with pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei (A, B). Immunohistochemistry panels show diffuse strong membranous/cytoplasmic reactivity in the tumor cells (C-F) and nuclear staining of variable extent (G-I); the individual antibodies are not labeled in this figure. Per the provided history, the tumor shows strong aberrant CD31 expression with an activated B-cell (non-germinal center) profile. Findings are consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, with aberrant CD31 expression.

title: Disseminated histoplasmosis with bone marrow infiltration and secondary HLH 2
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows an increase in large histiocytes with abundant pale cytoplasm admixed with small lymphocytes and hematopoietic precursors. Several histiocytes contain small round intracytoplasmic bodies with surrounding clear halos, compatible with Histoplasma yeast forms, and some appear to contain engulfed cells suggestive of hemophagocytosis. At this magnification, yeasts cannot be reliably separated from ingested red cells. Findings are suggestive of marrow histoplasmosis with associated hemophagocytosis; GMS/PAS stains and CD163 immunostain are recommended, and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis remains a clinical diagnosis.

title: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D-1α-hydroxylase– and multiple cytokine–producing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
describe_en: Composite figure. Coronal CT (A) demonstrates a large sinonasal soft-tissue mass that has largely resolved on follow-up imaging (F). Biopsy (B) shows diffuse sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells with vesicular chromatin, and immunostains (C-E) show diffuse strong positivity in the neoplastic cells, including infiltration around muscle fibers; the specific antibodies are not labeled and cannot be identified from the image. The morphology is compatible with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The claimed 25-hydroxyvitamin D-1α-hydroxylase and cytokine production cannot be confirmed from these panels and requires clinical correlation (hypercalcemia with elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) and specific immunostains.

title: Acute  Undifferentiated  Leukemia  myeloperoxidase  (MPO)  reaction
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained for myeloperoxidase shows a mature neutrophil (arrow) with strong granular cytoplasmic positivity, serving as an internal positive control, and a second positive granulocyte at lower left. The remainder of this cropped field consists mainly of red cells and fat spaces, and MPO-negative blasts are not well demonstrated in the image. In a case of acute undifferentiated leukemia, blasts are expected to be MPO-negative (<3% positive) with no lineage-specific markers by flow cytometry. The stain is technically adequate given the positive internal control.

title: hepatosplenic T cell lymphoma 1
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows clusters of medium-sized atypical lymphoid cells with fine chromatin, round to indented nuclei, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a moderate rim of pale agranular cytoplasm, admixed with basophilic erythroid precursors and a mitotic figure. The atypical cells lack granules and Auer rods. These features are non-specific on the smear alone; distinguishing them from blasts or monocytes requires flow cytometry. In conjunction with an intrasinusoidal infiltrate on biopsy and a CD3+ CD4-/CD8- gamma-delta T-cell phenotype, the findings are consistent with involvement by hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma.

title: hepatosplenic T cell lymphoma 2
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E) shows a markedly hypercellular marrow with persistent trilineage hematopoiesis. There is an increased population of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with dark nuclei, some aligned in linear arrays suggestive of an intrasinusoidal distribution, without discrete nodular aggregates. The infiltrate is subtle and cannot be confidently characterized on H&E alone at this magnification. Immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD8, TIA-1 and TCR delta would be required; in that context the findings are consistent with marrow involvement by hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma.

title: Auer Rod-like inclusion in Lymphoma
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked lymphocytosis composed of a fairly monotonous population of intermediate-sized lymphoid cells with round to slightly irregular nuclei, clumped chromatin, occasional small nucleoli and a moderate rim of pale basophilic cytoplasm. The fine eosinophilic, Auer rod-like crystalline inclusions described for this case are not clearly discernible at the resolution of this image and would need confirmation at higher magnification. No blasts or smudge cells are identified. With the reported monoclonal B-cell population on flow cytometry, findings are consistent with a mature B-cell lymphoma in leukemic phase; immunoglobulin crystal inclusions of this type favor lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma or another low-grade B-cell neoplasm.

title: Lymphoma with Auer Rods
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows lymphocytosis composed of monotonous intermediate-sized lymphoid cells with round to slightly indented nuclei, coarsely clumped chromatin and a moderate amount of pale basophilic cytoplasm; a single segmented neutrophil provides a size reference. The eosinophilic, needle-like Auer rod-like inclusions reported in this case cannot be convincingly identified at this image resolution. There are no blasts or smudge cells. Together with the monoclonal B-cell population on flow cytometry, the findings are consistent with a low-grade B-cell lymphoma in leukemic phase, with crystalline immunoglobulin inclusions raising lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma in the differential.

title: HHV8-associated lymphoproliferative disorder in the peripheral blood
describe_en: This composite figure shows peripheral blood smears (A-C), a bone marrow aspirate (D), and two immunohistochemical stains (E-F). The blood smears contain increased circulating plasmablast-like cells with eccentric nuclei, dispersed chromatin, and abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm, some with a perinuclear hof. The marrow aspirate shows mixed hematopoietic elements with plasmacytoid cells and a histiocyte, while the immunostains show clusters of positive cells (E) and a rare nuclear-positive cell (F), although the antibodies are not labeled and resolution is limited. In the appropriate context, and with confirmation by HHV8 LANA staining, light-chain restriction studies, and EBV status, the findings are suggestive of an HHV8-associated lymphoproliferative disorder with circulating plasmablasts, such as HHV8-positive multicentric Castleman disease.

title: Bone Marrow Fibrosis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows moderate anisopoikilocytosis with several teardrop-shaped red cells (dacrocytes) and scattered elliptocytes. A large atypical platelet with irregular cytoplasmic projections is present, along with normal-sized platelets. Nucleated red cells and immature myeloid cells, which would complete a leukoerythroblastic picture, are not seen in this field. Although the title refers to marrow fibrosis, this image shows only blood findings; in conjunction with a marrow biopsy with clustered atypical megakaryocytes and reticulin fibrosis, these findings are consistent with primary myelofibrosis, fibrotic stage.

title: Post-transplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder: H&E
describe_en: Section of lymph node shows effacement by extensive geographic necrosis with a preserved perivascular cuff of viable atypical lymphoid cells around a small hyalinized vessel. At high power the cells are predominantly large with irregular, angulated nuclei, vesicular chromatin, small nucleoli and scant cytoplasm, admixed with a few small lymphocytes. In the post-transplant setting with PAX5/CD20 and CD30 positivity, CD15 negativity and diffuse EBER positivity, findings are consistent with EBV-positive post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, monomorphic type (diffuse large B-cell lymphoma).

title: Growth factor (GCSF) therapy effect 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single intermediate-to-large immature myeloid cell with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin and a thin rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing scattered fine azurophilic granules. A pale crescent is seen at one edge of the cytoplasm; definite Döhle bodies cannot be resolved with confidence in this cell. No neutrophils are present in this field, so the toxic granulation and Döhle bodies described in the neutrophils cannot be evaluated here, and platelets are markedly decreased. In a post-transplant patient recently given G-CSF, a rare circulating granulated blast is suggestive of growth factor effect, but correlation with blast percentage trend and marrow/MRD studies is required to exclude relapse.

title: EBV+Plasmablastic lymphoma
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows nuclear positivity in the majority of the neoplastic cells, with variable intensity, and a minor population of negative nuclei. The specific antibody is not stated in the record; the nuclear pattern and high proportion of positive cells would fit MUM1/IRF4, a high Ki-67 proliferation index, or MYC, each of which is typical of plasmablastic lymphoma. Interpretation should be tied to the labelled marker on the original slide. Findings are supportive of, but not by themselves diagnostic of, EBV-positive plasmablastic lymphoma.

title: AML-CEBPA
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low power shows a moderately cellular marrow with adipose tissue interspersed between thin bony trabeculae. Hematopoietic cells are distributed interstitially without nodular aggregates, fibrosis, or granulomas, and scattered megakaryocytes are identifiable. Cytologic detail is insufficient at this magnification to assess blast percentage or lineage. Correlation with higher-power sections, aspirate differential, immunohistochemistry (CD34), and molecular studies is required to support acute myeloid leukemia with mutated CEBPA.

title: AML-CEBPA-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two neutrophils with hypolobated, bilobed nuclei and coarsely condensed chromatin, one bearing small nuclear appendages, consistent with pseudo-Pelger-Huët-like change. Cytoplasmic granulation appears preserved. Red cells show crenation, likely a drying artifact, and platelets are present. No circulating blasts are identified in this field; the image demonstrates neutrophil nuclear abnormalities only and is not by itself diagnostic of AML with mutated CEBPA.

title: AML-CEBPA-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single granulated myeloid cell with an irregular, folded to bilobed nucleus, moderately condensed chromatin, and cytoplasm filled with fine purple granules; the cell likely represents an immature or atypical granulocytic element. No blasts or Auer rods are present in this field. The red cells are mostly normocytic, with rare fragmented forms. This single field is non-diagnostic on its own; the diagnosis of AML with mutated CEBPA rests on blast enumeration in blood and marrow and demonstration of an in-frame bZIP CEBPA mutation.

title: MDS-RS-SLD-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with mild anisocytosis, including scattered larger and paler cells that suggest a subtle dimorphic population, along with occasional elliptocytes and a teardrop form. The single neutrophil present shows normal lobation and granulation, and platelets are adequate. No blasts are seen. These findings are nonspecific; in the setting of anemia with an elevated RDW, they are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, MDS with ring sideroblasts, which requires bone marrow iron staining and SF3B1 testing.

title: MDS-RS-SLD-HE
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at high power shows a normocellular to mildly hypercellular marrow with interspersed fat. Erythroid precursors are increased and form clusters of cells with round, dark nuclei and perinuclear clearing, while granulocytic maturation is present and megakaryocytes are scattered with largely unremarkable lobation. Blasts are not conspicuously increased. The erythroid-predominant picture is compatible with MDS with ring sideroblasts and single-lineage dysplasia, which must be confirmed by iron stain for ring sideroblasts and SF3B1 mutation analysis.

title: MDS-RS
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a mixed population of maturing granulocytic cells, including myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and band forms, together with erythroid precursors ranging from a large basophilic pronormoblast-like cell to polychromatophilic and orthochromatic normoblasts. Dysplastic changes are subtle in this field, and blasts are not increased. Ring sideroblasts cannot be identified on a Romanowsky stain; an iron stain and SF3B1 mutation analysis are required to support MDS with ring sideroblasts and single-lineage (erythroid) dysplasia.

title: MDS-RS
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows increased erythroid precursors, including large pronormoblasts and basophilic normoblasts with finely stippled, somewhat megaloblastoid chromatin, admixed with maturing granulocytic elements. Mild nuclear irregularity is seen, but definitive dysplasia is limited in this field and many cells are smeared. Blasts are not increased. Ring sideroblasts cannot be evaluated on a Romanowsky stain; correlation with a Prussian blue iron stain (≥15% ring sideroblasts, or ≥5% with SF3B1 mutation) is required to support MDS with ring sideroblasts.

title: MDS-RS
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis, including target cells, elliptocytes, teardrop cells, and occasional echinocytes, with a suggestion of a dimorphic population in which some red cells appear paler than others. The few leukocytes in the field are mature lymphocytes without obvious blasts, and platelets appear adequate. These red cell changes are nonspecific; ring sideroblasts must be demonstrated on an iron-stained bone marrow aspirate. In the appropriate clinical context, the findings are compatible with the peripheral blood picture of myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts.

title: MDS-RS
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at high power shows a mixed hematopoietic population with abundant erythroid precursors and granulocytic cells in a loose, edematous stroma containing small vessels. Several megakaryocytes have small round, non-lobated or hypolobated nuclei, a feature suggestive of megakaryocytic dysplasia. Blasts are not conspicuously increased. Ring sideroblasts cannot be assessed on H&E; correlation with an iron-stained aspirate and SF3B1 status is required, and dysplasia in more than one lineage would favor MDS-RS with multilineage dysplasia over single-lineage dysplasia.

title: Intravascular DLBCL-Biopsy HE
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at high power shows a hypercellular marrow containing numerous large atypical lymphoid-appearing cells with vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli, irregular nuclear contours, and moderate amphophilic cytoplasm, admixed with residual hematopoietic elements and small lymphocytes. A predominantly intrasinusoidal distribution is not clearly evident on this H&E field. Immunohistochemistry for CD20/PAX5 together with an endothelial marker (CD34 or ERG) is required to demonstrate intravascular/intrasinusoidal localization; with such confirmation, findings would be consistent with involvement by intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

title: Intravascular DLBCL-Blood
describe_en: Low-power view of a Wright-stained peripheral blood smear shows a paucicellular field with only a few scattered nucleated cells, several of which are mononuclear cells with dark nuclei. Red cells are largely unremarkable at this magnification, and platelets appear sparse. Nuclear and cytoplasmic detail cannot be assessed at this power, so circulating large atypical lymphoid cells cannot be confirmed or excluded from this image alone. Correlation with high-power examination, flow cytometry and tissue biopsy (e.g., random skin or marrow) is required; findings are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, peripheral blood involvement by intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

title: Intravascular DLBCL-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normochromic red cells with scattered crenated forms, which may be artifactual, and a short rouleaux-like stack. A single small mononuclear cell with a dense round nucleus is present and is most consistent with a small lymphocyte. Platelets are present as small clumps. No circulating large atypical lymphoid cells are identified in this field. The peripheral blood is nonspecific; intravascular large B-cell lymphoma frequently lacks circulating tumor cells, and the diagnosis requires tissue (e.g., marrow or skin) biopsy.

title: Intravascular DLBCL-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large atypical mononuclear cell with an irregular folded to lobulated nucleus, moderately open chromatin and moderate gray-blue cytoplasm with irregular borders. A small dense naked nucleus lies nearby, and the background red cells include scattered crenated forms with sparse platelets. The large cell may represent a circulating neoplastic lymphoid cell, but its features overlap with a monocyte and it cannot be classified with certainty on morphology alone. In the clinical context of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, flow cytometry or tissue correlation is needed to confirm circulating lymphoma cells.

title: MPN-Polycythemia Vera
