describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normochromic, normocytic red cells with several platelets, including occasional large forms. A single mononuclear cell with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, moderately condensed chromatin, and scant agranular, pale-blue cytoplasm with an irregular outline is present; it most likely represents a lymphocyte, although a circulating immature cell cannot be excluded on a single cell. No specific morphologic features of polycythemia vera are evident in this field; red cell mass and crowding cannot be assessed from a thin-area field. The diagnosis of polycythemia vera requires correlation with hemoglobin/hematocrit, JAK2 mutation status, and bone marrow morphology.

title: H+E 1000x
describe_en: At high power, the section shows numerous large histiocytes with abundant pale granular to foamy cytoplasm and vesicular oval nuclei, admixed with lymphocytes and occasional granulocytes. Within the histiocyte cytoplasm are faint tiny dot-like structures and small vacuoles corresponding to intracellular yeast forms, although individual organisms and their halos are not sharply resolved in this photograph. No well-formed granulomas or necrosis are seen. Findings are suggestive of a histiocytic infiltrate harbouring intracellular yeasts, consistent with histoplasmosis in context; special stains are required for confirmation.

title: Myeloma
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E, low-to-medium power) shows a markedly hypercellular intertrabecular space with near-complete loss of fat. The marrow is replaced by diffuse sheets of monotonous cells with round, eccentrically placed nuclei and moderate cytoplasm, with marked reduction of normal hematopoietic elements. Cytologic detail is limited at this magnification, and plasma cell lineage should be confirmed with CD138 and kappa/lambda staining. Findings are consistent with extensive marrow involvement by plasma cell myeloma in the appropriate context.

title: BPDCN
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows a single small-to-intermediate mononuclear cell with a slightly irregular nucleus, moderately condensed chromatin without a conspicuous nucleolus, and a moderate rim of pale cytoplasm with fine granular or microvacuolated texture. Background red cells are unremarkable. The morphology of this isolated cell is nonspecific and could represent a circulating neoplastic cell, a large granular lymphocyte or a reactive lymphocyte. In the context of known blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm it may represent a circulating tumor cell, but confirmation requires flow cytometry (CD4, CD56, CD123-bright, HLA-DR).

title: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma-CD79a
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemistry for CD79a shows a few small aggregates of positive B cells, some related to vascular structures, with scattered single positive cells in a largely negative background. This field does not demonstrate the expanded, confluent white pulp nodules or diffuse red pulp B-cell infiltration usually expected in splenic marginal zone lymphoma. The image may represent a limited area of involvement or residual B cells, so findings are only partially supportive and should be correlated with CD20 and H&E sections from the same case.

title: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma-HE
describe_en: High-power section of spleen shows red pulp diffusely infiltrated by medium to large lymphoid cells with oval vesicular nuclei, small distinct nucleoli and moderate pale amphophilic cytoplasm, admixed with red blood cells, sinus-lining cells and scattered hemosiderin. The cells in this field are larger than the typical small-to-medium marginal zone cells of splenic marginal zone lymphoma. No overt necrosis is seen. The appearance is compatible with splenic marginal zone lymphoma involving red pulp, but the proportion of large cells raises the possibility of large-cell transformation, which should be evaluated with Ki-67 and review of sheets of large cells across the specimen.

title: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma-HE
describe_en: Sections show a diffuse infiltrate of intermediate to large lymphoid cells with vesicular chromatin, distinct nucleoli, and moderate pale cytoplasm, traversed by thin-walled vessels. Small lymphocytes are few, and the cells are larger and more open than the small marginal zone cells typical of splenic marginal zone lymphoma. Mitotic figures are not prominent in this field. The image is only partially typical of SMZL and raises the question of increased large cells or large cell transformation, which should be assessed with Ki-67 and correlation with other areas.

title: Mantle cell lymphoma-Cyclin-D1
describe_en: Immunohistochemistry for cyclin D1 shows that the diffuse population of medium-sized tumor cells lacks nuclear staining, while rare scattered non-neoplastic cells are positive, indicating adequate staining. The image therefore does not demonstrate the cyclin D1 overexpression expected in most mantle cell lymphomas. A cyclin D1-negative mantle cell lymphoma is still possible and would be supported by SOX11 positivity (as in the companion image) and CCND2 rearrangement; otherwise alternative blastoid B-cell neoplasms should be excluded.

title: Aberrant T-cell antigen expression in a plasma cell neoplasm
describe_en: The H&E section shows a sheet of atypical plasmacytoid cells with eccentric nuclei, coarse to vesicular chromatin and moderate amphophilic to eosinophilic cytoplasm. The accompanying immunostains show diffuse membranous positivity (B, D), strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positivity (C), cytoplasmic staining in one light-chain preparation with a negative counterpart (E, F), consistent with monotypic light-chain expression, and strong (G) and weak (H) membranous staining in the tumor cells. Because the antibodies are not labeled, the specific aberrant T-cell antigens (e.g. CD3, CD4, CD7 or CD56) cannot be verified directly from the figure. The findings are consistent with a clonal plasma cell neoplasm with an aberrant immunophenotype, and the T-cell marker expression should not be mistaken for a T-cell lymphoma.

title: NUT midline carcinoma with leukemic presentation mimicking CD34-positive acute leukemia
describe_en: This composite figure shows peripheral blood with clusters of large, cohesive blast-like cells (A), flow cytometry identifying a CD45-dim/negative, low side-scatter population that is CD34 positive but lacks CD33, CD19 and CD7 (B-D), and a bone marrow biopsy diffusely replaced by sheets of monotonous tumor cells (E) with several immunohistochemical stains (F-H). The absence of any hematopoietic lineage marker on a CD34-positive population, CD45 negativity and cohesive clustering on the smear are red flags for a non-hematopoietic neoplasm. The IHC panels are unlabeled, so the NUT (speckled nuclear) and cytokeratin results cannot be verified in this image. Findings are suggestive of metastatic carcinoma mimicking CD34-positive acute leukemia, consistent with the stated NUT carcinoma when confirmed by NUT IHC or NUTM1 rearrangement.

title: Myeloid Neoplasm-GATA2-proband
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain on a hypercellular marrow core (marker not labeled; pattern most consistent with CD34) highlights scattered small-to-intermediate round cells with membranous and cytoplasmic staining, present singly and in small clusters, together with positive capillary endothelium as an internal control. The majority of hematopoietic cells, including larger cells with vesicular nuclei, are negative. The positive cells should be quantified and checked for clustering or abnormal localization; the findings support an increase in CD34-positive precursors in this GATA2-associated myeloid neoplasm rather than sheets of blasts.

title: Myeloid Neoplasm-GATA2-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small mononuclear cell with a dense, coarsely clumped hyperchromatic nucleus and scant cytoplasm, accompanied by fine purple granules scattered beside it. Its identity cannot be established with certainty from this single field; a degranulated or disrupted basophil and a micromegakaryocyte are the main considerations, and a small lymphocyte with nearby platelet debris is also possible. Background red cells show mild anisocytosis with an occasional teardrop form and a polychromatic macrocyte. The image does not by itself demonstrate a specific diagnostic abnormality and should be interpreted with the full smear in the context of the GATA2-associated myeloid neoplasm.

title: Erdheim-Chester Disease
describe_en: Scanning-magnification sections of two skin biopsies show an intact epidermis overlying a dermis that is expanded by a diffuse, pale-staining infiltrate which effaces the normal reticular dermal collagen and surrounds adnexal structures, extending to the deep margin. Cytologic detail cannot be assessed at this magnification; higher power is required to confirm foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells. In the clinical and radiologic context, the pattern is compatible with cutaneous involvement by Erdheim-Chester disease.

title: Circulating prolymphocytes cell in peripheral blood sample 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single medium-to-large lymphoid cell with a round to slightly indented nucleus, relatively open chromatin and a moderate rim of pale basophilic, agranular cytoplasm. A single prominent nucleolus, the hallmark of a prolymphocyte, is not clearly resolved at this resolution. The background red cells show widespread crenation consistent with drying or delayed-processing artifact, and there is blue stain precipitate. A single cell cannot establish a monomorphic prolymphocytic population; the morphology is only partially consistent with a circulating prolymphocyte, and correlation with the full smear, lymphocyte count and flow cytometry is required.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-H&E
describe_en: Skin biopsy shows an epidermis with marked intracellular edema and reticular degeneration, with keratinocytes stretched into thin strands forming intraepidermal vesicles beneath an intact basket-weave stratum corneum. Scattered lymphocytes are present within the epidermis, and the papillary dermis shows edema, a lymphocytic infiltrate and extravasated red cells. Multinucleated keratinocytes with viral inclusions are not identified. These changes represent an early vesiculating lesion; in the appropriate clinical setting with a dermal EBV (EBER)-positive cytotoxic T/NK-cell infiltrate, they are consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: Low-power sections of skin show a dense lymphoid infiltrate diffusely involving the reticular dermis, dissecting between collagen bundles with accentuation around vessels and adnexal structures. The infiltrate extends deep into the dermis. The infiltrating cells appear small to medium-sized, but cytologic atypia cannot be assessed at this magnification. In the setting of vesiculopapular lesions on sun-exposed skin and an EBER-positive cytotoxic T/NK-cell infiltrate, the findings are consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: Low-power sections of deep dermis and subcutis show a lymphoid infiltrate permeating subcutaneous fat lobules in a lobular panniculitis-like pattern, with cuffing around a small neurovascular bundle and a hair follicle. The infiltrating cells are small to medium-sized at this magnification, and definite adipocyte rimming, fat necrosis or granulomas are not evident. Extension of the infiltrate into the subcutis in a patient with photodistributed vesiculopapular lesions and an EBER-positive cytotoxic infiltrate is consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: High-power examination of the dermis shows a small vessel surrounded and infiltrated by small to medium-sized lymphocytes with slightly irregular hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, with red cells and fibrinoid material in the lumen. Lymphocytes also extend interstitially between collagen bundles. Cytologic atypia is mild, and large pleomorphic cells are not identified. The angiocentric infiltrate of mildly atypical lymphocytes, in conjunction with EBER positivity and a cytotoxic phenotype, is consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: Sections of dermis show a dense perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with irregular, angulated hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, permeating the wall of a dilated vessel and dissecting between collagen bundles. Occasional larger cells are present, but sheets of large atypical cells and necrosis are not seen. An adjacent eccrine duct is intact. The mildly to moderately atypical angiocentric infiltrate, together with EBER positivity and a cytotoxic T/NK phenotype, is consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: Sections of deep dermis and subcutis show a dense infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with irregular, indented hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, admixed with scattered larger cells with vesicular chromatin. The infiltrate shows perivascular accentuation and extends into subcutaneous fat. Necrosis is not seen in this field. These cytologic features indicate a mildly to moderately atypical lymphoid infiltrate; with an EBER-positive cytotoxic T/NK phenotype and the clinical picture of photodistributed vesiculopapular lesions, they are consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Hydroa Vacciniforme-like Lymphoproliferative Disorder-HE
describe_en: Low-power sections of deep dermis and subcutis show a dense lymphoid infiltrate cuffing an obliquely sectioned hair follicle and extending into the surrounding dermis and between adipocytes of the subcutaneous fat lobules. The follicular epithelium is largely intact without obvious folliculotropism or follicular mucinosis, and no necrosis or granulomas are seen. Cytologic detail is limited at this magnification. The deep periadnexal and subcutaneous distribution, with an EBER-positive cytotoxic infiltrate, is consistent with hydroa vacciniforme lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: NK-cell enteropathy-HE
describe_en: Low-power sections of gastrointestinal mucosal biopsies show the lamina propria diffusely expanded by a dense cellular infiltrate that separates and displaces glands. The glands and surface epithelium are largely preserved, and there is no ulceration, necrosis or mass-forming destructive growth in this field. An adjacent fragment shows less involved mucosa. Cytologic features cannot be evaluated at this magnification; in conjunction with higher-power morphology and an NK-cell immunophenotype (CD56+, cytoplasmic CD3+, surface CD3-, CD5-, EBER-), these findings are compatible with NK-cell enteropathy.

title: NK-cell enteropathy-CD56
describe_en: Scanning-power CD56 immunohistochemistry of multiple gastrointestinal mucosal biopsy fragments shows extensive CD56-positive infiltration, diffuse and intense in one fragment and patchy in the others, with negative gland profiles discernible within the stained lamina propria. The low resolution of the image does not permit evaluation of cytologic features, depth of involvement or angiodestruction. The distribution indicates a large mucosal NK-cell population; in conjunction with EBER negativity and a non-destructive histology, this is compatible with NK-cell enteropathy.

title: NK-cell enteropathy-HE
describe_en: Sections of colonic-type mucosa show preserved crypt architecture with crypts separated by a lamina propria expanded by a moderately dense mononuclear infiltrate accompanied by conspicuous interstitial hemorrhage. There is no crypt destruction, cryptitis, crypt abscess or ulceration, and the surface epithelium is intact. Cytologic features of the infiltrate are not well assessed at this magnification. In conjunction with an NK-cell immunophenotype and EBER negativity, the superficial non-destructive infiltrate is compatible with NK-cell enteropathy.

title: NK-cell enteropathy
describe_en: An immunohistochemical stain (antibody not specified) on colonic-type mucosa highlights a dense infiltrate of positive cells expanding the lamina propria and surrounding negative crypts. Intraepithelial positive cells are sparse, and crypt architecture is preserved. The specific marker cannot be determined from the image, so lineage cannot be assigned on this stain alone. When the infiltrate is CD56-positive with cytoplasmic CD3 and negative for CD5 and EBER, the findings support NK-cell enteropathy.

title: Beta-thalassemia trait-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells of fairly uniform size with mild hypochromia and mild poikilocytosis, including scattered teardrop and pear-shaped cells, occasional target cells and a few stomatocyte-like forms. Basophilic stippling, nucleated red cells and schistocytes are not seen. No leukocyte is present in the field to gauge red cell size, so microcytosis must be confirmed by the MCV. The findings are nonspecific but compatible with thalassemia trait; beta-thalassemia trait is supported by a high RBC count with low MCV and increased HbA2 on HPLC.

title: Beta-thalassemia trait-Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells that appear microcytic relative to a small lymphocyte, with relatively uniform size and mild poikilocytosis including occasional elliptocytes and teardrop-like forms. Hypochromia is mild, and target cells and basophilic stippling are not conspicuous in this field. White cells and platelets are unremarkable in this limited view. The findings are nonspecific but compatible with thalassemia trait; correlation with red cell indices (low MCV with high RBC count) and hemoglobin HPLC showing increased HbA2 is needed for a diagnosis of beta-thalassemia trait.

title: EBV reactivation
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (antibody not specified) shows numerous intermediate-to-large cells with strong membranous and cytoplasmic staining, scattered and in loose clusters among negative small lymphocytes. The positive population varies in size and does not form cohesive sheets. Because the marker is not identified, the image cannot be interpreted in isolation; within the EBV reactivation case it likely represents one of the lymphocyte subset markers highlighting activated cells in a reactive process.

title: ALCL-H&E
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymph node shows a dense lymphoid area abutting a pale, hypocellular fibrotic to edematous zone containing scattered cells, with loss of recognizable follicular architecture in the field. Cytologic detail of the large cells is not resolvable at this magnification. The low-power appearance is nonspecific; in this case the diagnosis of ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma rests on the high-power hallmark cells and uniform strong CD30 expression.

title: Cutaneous intralymphatic CD30 pseudolymphoma: a reactive condition mimicking lymphoma
describe_en: Composite of skin sections. H&E sections show a dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate beneath an intact epidermis, with dilated thin-walled channels containing intraluminal aggregates of larger mononuclear cells. The accompanying immunostains (markers not labeled) highlight positive cells within the dermis and a dense cluster within a vascular lumen, with other panels showing sparser staining. Because the markers are not identified, the lymphatic nature of the vessels (e.g., D2-40) and the CD30 status of the intraluminal cells cannot be confirmed from the image alone. Findings are compatible with intralymphatic aggregates of activated lymphoid cells, as in cutaneous intralymphatic CD30-positive pseudolymphoma, but the benign nature depends on clinical correlation, lack of a clonal T-cell population and clinical regression.

title: Myeloma with Cyclin D1
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (marker not labeled on the image) shows a diffuse, sheet-like infiltrate of uniform round cells with strong membranous staining in essentially all cells, replacing the normal architecture in this field. Only scattered unstained stromal elements are present. In the context of this case, the pattern is compatible with a membranous marker such as CD138 (plasma cells) or aberrant CD20, which is enriched in myeloma with t(11;14). Findings support extensive involvement by a plasma cell neoplasm; the specific marker should be confirmed from the source case.

title: Myeloma with Cyclin D1
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (DAB; antigen not labeled) shows diffuse sheets of uniform cells with strong circumferential membranous staining, replacing nearly the entire field, with a rare negative large cell and small stromal spaces. In the context of plasma cell myeloma with t(11;14), the membranous pattern is compatible with CD138 highlighting a diffuse plasma cell infiltrate, or CD20, which is frequently expressed in t(11;14) myeloma. Cyclin D1 expression (nuclear) is not demonstrated in this image; the antigen should be confirmed with the case materials.

title: Myeloma with Cyclin D1
describe_en: H&E section of bone marrow shows diffuse sheets of monotonous small to medium-sized cells with round, slightly eccentric nuclei, condensed chromatin and scant to modest cytoplasm, replacing normal hematopoiesis with only residual megakaryocytes and stroma. Definitive plasmacytic features are not clearly resolved at this magnification, and the cells have a lymphoid-like appearance. In the context of CD138-positive, cyclin D1-positive plasma cells with t(11;14), the findings are consistent with extensive involvement by plasma cell myeloma with small, lymphoplasmacytoid morphology, a recognized mimic of small B-cell lymphoma.

title: Myeloma with Cyclin D1
describe_en: Section of bone marrow shows a dense sheet of cells stained with a chromogenic in situ hybridization or immunostain (dark blue chromogen with pink nuclear counterstain; probe not labeled). Nearly all cells in the field show fine granular cytoplasmic signal, indicating a diffuse, monotonous population. In the context of plasma cell myeloma, this pattern is most consistent with light chain mRNA in situ hybridization demonstrating light-chain restriction in a plasma cell infiltrate; the image itself does not demonstrate cyclin D1 expression, which would be nuclear, and the specific probe should be verified in the referenced case.

title: Myeloma with Cyclin D1
describe_en: Section of bone marrow stained with a chromogenic in situ hybridization or immunostain (dark blue chromogen, pink counterstain; probe not labeled) shows positive cytoplasmic signal in a subset of cells, while most cells in the field are negative. The positive cells are scattered and in small groups. When compared with the companion stain showing diffuse positivity, this pattern is consistent with the non-restricted light chain in a light-chain-restricted plasma cell neoplasm; the image does not demonstrate cyclin D1 itself, and probe identity should be verified in the referenced case.

title: B & B: basophils and bleeding, an atypical case of acute promyelocytic leukemia
describe_en: This composite figure combines smear morphology with flow cytometry and karyotype. The smears (panels A and B) show large abnormal granular cells with irregular folded nuclei and abundant granular cytoplasm, admixed with cells bearing coarse, dark purple granules consistent with basophils (red arrows). Faggot cells and Auer rods cannot be confirmed at this resolution. Panel C shows flow cytometric dot plots with distinct colored populations and panel D a G-banded karyotype, but axis labels and chromosomal breakpoints are not legible in this image. Findings are compatible with an atypical acute promyelocytic leukemia with basophilic differentiation, as indicated in the title; the diagnosis rests on demonstration of PML::RARA by FISH, RT-PCR, or karyotype, and coagulopathy (DIC/bleeding) should be urgently evaluated.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain with a red chromogen (marker not specified on the image) shows a sharply demarcated, confluent sheet of medium to large cells with strong membranous positivity occupying most of the field, adjacent to an area composed of negative small cells containing only scattered positive cells. The sheet-like, diffuse distribution of positive larger cells differs from the scattered single LP cells expected in classic nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. If this marker represents a B-cell antigen such as CD20, the pattern supports a diffuse large B-cell component; in the reported context, the findings are suggestive of NLPHL with progression to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, pending correlation with H&E and the full panel.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen, antibody not specified in the image) of lymph node at high power shows a predominantly nuclear staining pattern, with strong positivity in scattered large cells and variable positivity in a subset of small-to-intermediate cells. Most background small lymphocytes are negative, and some large vesicular cells are weak or unstained. The positive large cells are dispersed and do not form sheets. The pattern could correspond to a nuclear marker such as MUM1/IRF4, OCT2, or Ki-67; findings are compatible with the large-cell component of nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma but require correlation with the labeled immunopanel for specific interpretation.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: High-power immunohistochemical stain with a red chromogen (marker not specified on the image) shows a dense lymphoid background containing several large atypical cells with vesicular, lobulated nuclei (arrows), morphologically consistent with lymphocyte-predominant (LP) cells. The LP cells are negative for this marker, while a single large cell elsewhere in the field is strongly positive and the small background lymphocytes are largely negative. Because the marker is not identified, the stain is best interpreted as a negative result in LP cells (for example, CD30 or CD15 negativity, which would argue against classic Hodgkin lymphoma) and must be correlated with the full panel. Findings are consistent with nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma in the reported context of variant patterns with progression.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen, antibody not specified in the image) of lymph node at high power shows a background of small to intermediate lymphocytes and scattered large vesicular cells that are negative for the marker. Only a single intermediate-to-large cell shows strong cytoplasmic and membranous staining, and there is faint granular background deposition. Because the antibody is not identified, the pattern cannot be definitively interpreted; if this is CD30 or CD15, the lack of staining in the large cells would support LP cells of nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, with the single positive cell likely a reactive immunoblast or granulocyte. Correlation with the case's labeled immunopanel is required.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen; antigen not labeled) of a lymph node shows an irregular, poorly delineated aggregate of positive small to medium-sized cells with numerous positive cells scattered in the surrounding lymphoid tissue. Distinct, well-formed nodules are not apparent in this field. In the context of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, the ill-defined, expansile distribution may reflect a variant growth pattern; cytologic detail is not resolvable at this magnification, and interpretation depends on the antigen and the companion stains of the referenced case.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen; antigen not labeled) shows numerous scattered large cells with weak-to-moderate membranous staining in a dense background of negative small lymphocytes. The positive cells are individually dispersed and do not form sheets. The staining intensity is relatively weak, limiting evaluation. In the context of the referenced case, the scattered positive large cells are consistent with LP cells of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma with a variant pattern; the marker identity should be verified with the case materials.

title: NLPHL with progression
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain (red chromogen, antibody not specified in the image) of lymph node at medium power shows numerous large cells with strong membranous staining and irregular outlines, set in a background of uniformly negative small lymphocytes. The positive large cells increase in density toward the upper right, where they approach but do not form confluent sheets. Some positive profiles have granular or process-like extensions, so a histiocytic marker cannot be fully excluded without the antibody label. If this represents a B-cell marker such as CD20, the numerous large positive cells in a B-cell-poor background raise concern for a T-cell-rich variant pattern or evolution toward T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma in this nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma; correlation with the labeled panel is required.

title: peripheral blood smear with spherocytic view 3
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous small, densely staining round red cells lacking central pallor, with anisocytosis and scattered larger pale cells. Crenation with regular short spicules affects a large proportion of the red cells and, together with the thick, poorly spread field, makes reliable distinction between true spherocytes and artifactual loss of central pallor difficult. A single larger, intensely stained round cell is present but cannot be characterized at this resolution. Findings are suggestive of, but not diagnostic for, a spherocytic red cell population; review of a thin, well-prepared fresh smear is recommended.

title: Identifying Concomitant Parasitism in an Individual Host
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single long, slender, coiled microfilaria at the upper left with a column of densely stained nuclei and a pale sheath extending beyond the body. The surrounding red cells appear largely unremarkable, and definite Plasmodium vivax trophozoites are not clearly resolved in this field at this resolution. The tail nuclear pattern cannot be evaluated, so species identification is limited, although a sheathed microfilaria in an Indian patient most likely represents Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia malayi. Findings confirm microfilaremia; the reported concomitant P. vivax infection is not demonstrated in this particular image.

title: Pure Erythroid Leukemia 3
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a hypercellular field dominated by erythroid precursors across a spectrum of maturation, from proerythroblasts with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and round nuclei to later erythroblasts with condensed chromatin. Many erythroid cells show nuclear irregularities, including lobulation, budding and elongated forms. Granulocytic elements are sparse. Although the erythroid proliferation is striking, a differential count is needed to document >80% erythroid cells with ≥30% proerythroblasts; in that context, the findings would be consistent with pure erythroid leukemia.

title: Dyserythropoesis in CDA
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows clusters of erythroid precursors that predominate among the nucleated cells. Several erythroblasts show irregular, lobulated or paired nuclear profiles suggesting binuclearity and nuclear fragmentation, with some nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony. Granulocytic precursors are present without increased blasts. Image resolution limits confident assessment of multinuclearity and internuclear chromatin bridges. Findings are compatible with dyserythropoiesis and, in the appropriate congenital clinical setting, suggestive of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia.

title: Multiple Myeloma-bone marrow 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows trilineage hematopoietic elements with predominance of maturing granulocytic precursors. Two plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, clock-face chromatin, deeply basophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear hofs are present in the center of the field. The plasma cells in this single field are not numerous, so their proportion cannot be estimated from this image. Findings show plasma cells; correlation with a full differential count, clonality studies and serum/urine protein studies is required to support plasma cell myeloma.

title: Multiple Myloma 5
describe_en: The image is a gross photograph of a centrifuged glass tube showing a dark red packed red cell layer and an overlying clear amber-yellow plasma layer, with a few small red flecks at the plasma interface that may represent aggregated red cells. The plasma is not visibly hemolyzed. Rouleaux formation is a microscopic finding and cannot be confirmed from this macroscopic image; it requires a peripheral smear or wet preparation, where rouleaux disperse with saline dilution whereas true agglutination persists. The image is therefore only partially illustrative of the stated rouleaux in multiple myeloma and should be correlated with the blood film, ESR and serum protein electrophoresis.

title: Prominent large eosinophilic abscess
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymph node shows a large, ill-defined pale eosinophilic area set within densely cellular lymphoid parenchyma with vague nodular contours suggestive of follicles. At this magnification the cellular composition of the pink zone cannot be confirmed; higher power would be needed to document sheets of eosinophils and necrosis. In context, the appearance is compatible with an eosinophilic abscess in a background of follicular hyperplasia; parasitic infection, Kimura disease, and IgG4-related disease should be considered clinically.

title: paracortical tissue showing thick vessels containing waxy, homogenous, pale eosinophilic extracellular material
describe_en: Sections show fibroadipose tissue containing several thick-walled blood vessels whose walls are expanded by homogeneous, waxy, pale eosinophilic acellular material. The deposits are relatively hypocellular and extend into the perivascular stroma. Adjacent areas of fresh hemorrhage and mature adipose tissue are present; lymph node parenchyma (paracortex) is not clearly identifiable in this particular field. The findings are suggestive of vascular amyloid deposition, which should be confirmed with Congo red staining and polarization.

title: Paracortical tissue with thick blood vessels due to amyloid deposition.
describe_en: Low-power H&E section shows a nodular aggregate of numerous thick-walled vessels whose walls are expanded by pale, homogeneous, acellular eosinophilic material, with intervening adipose tissue and fibrous stroma and hemorrhage at the left edge. Bony trabeculae with fatty hematopoietic marrow are present at the top and right of the fragment, and no lymph node architecture (capsule, sinuses, follicles) is recognizable, so the tissue appears to be bone/marrow rather than paracortical lymph node as captioned. The vascular wall thickening is suggestive of amyloid deposition, which must be confirmed by Congo red with apple-green birefringence and typed (e.g., AL light chain). In a patient with plasma cell myeloma, findings are suggestive of AL amyloid angiopathy.

title: Peripheral smear  showing cocci in pairs within the cytoplasm of a monocyte.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a thick area with overlapping crenated red cells and two leukocytes. The arrowed cell has an eccentric dense nucleus and pale granular cytoplasm containing a few tiny dark dots; at this magnification and in this thick field they cannot be confidently resolved as paired cocci. The second leukocyte shows an indented nucleus with finely granular, vacuolated cytoplasm. Intracellular bacteria in circulating phagocytes would indicate high-grade bacteremia, but confirmation requires oil-immersion review in a thin area, Gram stain and blood cultures.

title: Circulating megakaryocytes in a case of Visceral Leishmaniasis 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (May-Grünwald-Giemsa) shows numerous small oval organisms, approximately 2-4 um, each containing a purple nucleus and a smaller rod-shaped kinetoplast, lying predominantly extracellularly around large pale nuclei of disrupted macrophages. A few erythroid precursors and a small lymphocyte are present. The image shows amastigotes in the marrow rather than the circulating megakaryocyte referred to in the title, which corresponds to the companion peripheral blood image. Findings are diagnostic of visceral leishmaniasis (Leishman-Donovan bodies).

title: Burkitt Lymphoma CD10
describe_en: CD10 immunostain shows a diffuse, monotonous population of medium-sized tumor cells that are negative for CD10. Only faint staining of scattered vascular/stromal elements is present, serving as an internal control. Of note, classic Burkitt lymphoma is characteristically CD10-positive; CD10 negativity is uncommon and should prompt careful exclusion of other high-grade B-cell lymphomas. The stain is interpreted as negative, which is partially concordant with the stated diagnosis and requires correlation with BCL6, BCL2, TdT, Ki-67 and MYC/BCL2/BCL6 FISH.

title: Lymph node with starry sky pattern
describe_en: Low-power H&E section shows small intestinal mucosa with villi at the upper left, beneath which the bowel wall is effaced by a diffuse, monotonous, sheet-like lymphoid infiltrate with scattered foci of hemorrhage. No nodular or follicular architecture is present. At this magnification the characteristic starry-sky pattern of interspersed tingible-body macrophages is only faintly appreciable, and cytologic features cannot be assessed; the tissue is intestine rather than lymph node as the title states. In the ileocecal region of a young patient, this diffuse transmural lymphoid infiltrate is suggestive of Burkitt lymphoma, pending high-power cytology, Ki-67, CD10/BCL2 and MYC studies.

title: Mastocytosis High Power
describe_en: High-power view of colonic mucosa (H&E) shows a lamina propria densely infiltrated by eosinophils, with focal extension of eosinophils into the crypt epithelium. Admixed lymphocytes, plasma cells and occasional pale oval mononuclear cells are present, while crypts remain intact without distortion or crypt abscesses. The eosinophil-rich infiltrate is nonspecific on its own; spindled mast cells are not clearly discernible in this field. Findings are compatible with the eosinophil-rich component of mucosal mastocytosis when correlated with CD117, tryptase and CD25 immunostains.

title: Mycosis Fungoides Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and dense chromatin, one with an irregular, indented nuclear contour and a cytoplasmic tail and the other with a round nucleus showing a faint folded chromatin texture. No nucleoli are apparent. A refractile fragment of debris is present in the center of the field as an artifact. The atypical nuclear contours are suggestive but not diagnostic of Sezary cells; in the context of mycosis fungoides, blood involvement should be confirmed by flow cytometry and clonality studies.

title: Mycosis Fungoides Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small lymphocyte with dense, clumped chromatin, a slightly irregular nuclear outline, and scant cytoplasm, and a separate large mononuclear cell with an oval nucleus and abundant pale blue cytoplasm with irregular borders molding around adjacent red cells. Neither cell shows an unequivocal cerebriform nuclear configuration at this magnification. The large cell has the appearance of a reactive lymphocyte or monocyte, and the small cell may represent a small Sezary-type cell but is not diagnostic by morphology alone. In the context of mycosis fungoides, blood involvement should be established by flow cytometry (CD4:CD8 ratio, CD7 and CD26 loss) and T-cell clonality studies rather than morphology.

title: Cat Scratch Disease-H&E High Power
describe_en: High-power H&E shows predominantly amorphous, finely granular and vacuolated necrotic material containing wavy residual collagen bundles and scattered degenerated nuclei and nuclear debris. No viable epithelioid histiocytes, giant cells or organisms are identified in this field. The appearance represents the central necrotic zone of a necrotizing granulomatous process; in isolation it is nonspecific, and correlation with the palisading histiocytic rim, special stains for organisms and clinical history is needed to support cat scratch disease.

title: Cat Scratch Disease-Steiner
describe_en: Steiner silver stain of the necrotic area shows a yellow-brown background of granular debris with rare tiny dark rod-like and punctate particles. Definite clusters or chains of pleomorphic bacilli are not convincingly resolved at this magnification and focus, and nonspecific silver deposition on debris cannot be excluded. In cat scratch disease, Bartonella henselae appears as small black, pleomorphic, curved bacilli in clusters, often in necrotic areas and vessel walls, best evaluated under oil immersion; a negative or equivocal silver stain does not exclude the diagnosis, and serology or PCR is more sensitive.

title: Refractory Cytopenia of Childhood
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low-to-medium power shows marrow spaces between bony trabeculae with interspersed adipocytes and trilineage hematopoiesis. Erythroid clusters and maturing granulocytes are present, whereas megakaryocytes are sparse. Cellularity in this field is not markedly decreased, which may occur in a minority of refractory cytopenia of childhood cases, but hypocellularity elsewhere cannot be excluded from a single field. No abnormal infiltrate is identified. Findings are nonspecific in isolation and must be integrated with aspirate dysplasia, blast count and cytogenetics.

title: Refractory Cytopenia of Childhood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-to-medium power shows reduced numbers of leukocytes, with only two small lymphocytes and one monocytoid cell in the field and no neutrophils. Platelets are markedly decreased. Red cells are predominantly normocytic and normochromic with mild anisocytosis. No blasts or dysplastic forms are identified. Findings suggest pancytopenia, which is nonspecific but compatible with refractory cytopenia of childhood in the appropriate clinical and marrow context.

title: Refractory Cytopenia of Childhood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single segmented neutrophil with normal lobation and granulation. Red cells show mild anisocytosis with occasional macrocytes, without significant poikilocytosis. Leukocytes and platelets appear sparse in this field, although counts cannot be judged from a single high-power field. No blasts or dysplastic granulocytes are identified. Findings are nonspecific; macrocytosis and cytopenias may accompany refractory cytopenia of childhood but require correlation with blood counts and marrow examination.

title: Germinotropic Lymphoproliferative Disorder-H&E
describe_en: Lymph node section shows a follicle with a small, regressed germinal center containing pale eosinophilic material and dendritic cells, surrounded by concentrically layered small mantle zone lymphocytes in an onion-skin pattern, with a vessel penetrating toward the follicle. The interfollicular areas contain prominent high endothelial venules and a dilated vascular space. Clusters of large plasmablastic cells are not evident in this particular field. These Castleman-like changes may be seen in the background of HHV8-positive germinotropic lymphoproliferative disorder, but the diagnostic germinal-center plasmablast aggregates must be identified elsewhere and confirmed with HHV8 LANA-1 and EBER.

title: Follicular Lymphoma Grade 3a-H&E
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymph node shows architectural effacement by numerous closely packed, back-to-back neoplastic follicles of relatively uniform size with attenuated mantle zones and compressed interfollicular regions. The follicles lack polarization and a starry-sky pattern of tingible-body macrophages. Cytologic detail is insufficient at this magnification to count centroblasts, so grading requires high-power evaluation (grade 3A: >15 centroblasts per HPF with centrocytes still present). The architecture is consistent with follicular lymphoma, reported in this case as grade 3A.

title: Plasmacytoma-Like PTLD, EBV+ EBER
describe_en: Low-power whole-section image of EBER in situ hybridization shows a solid, densely cellular nodule that is diffusely darker than the adjacent pale soft tissue, suggesting widespread signal within the lesional cells. However, at this scanning magnification discrete nuclear staining cannot be confirmed and interpretation depends on higher-power fields. In conjunction with high-power EBER images from the same case, the findings support an EBV-associated lesion, consistent with EBV-positive plasmacytoma-like post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Primary Effusion Lymphoma-Clinical
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the scalp shows multiple violaceous to dark brown macules, papules and small plaques of variable size, some coalescing, without ulceration. The appearance is most suggestive of cutaneous Kaposi sarcoma. The photograph itself does not demonstrate the effusion lymphoma; its relevance is that Kaposi sarcoma indicates KSHV/HHV8 infection, which frequently coexists with primary effusion lymphoma, particularly in HIV-positive patients. Biopsy with HHV8 LANA-1 immunostaining is required for confirmation.

title: Primary Effusion Lymphoma-H&E
describe_en: Skin biopsy at low power shows an intact epidermis overlying a dermis diffusely expanded by a proliferation of spindle cells arranged between collagen bundles. Numerous irregular, jagged and slit-like vascular spaces dissect the dermis, and there are scattered perivascular lymphoplasmacytic aggregates; a preexisting hair follicle is surrounded by the proliferation. No sheets of large lymphoma cells are seen. The findings are most consistent with Kaposi sarcoma (plaque stage) in a patient with KSHV/HHV8-associated primary effusion lymphoma; HHV8 LANA-1 immunostaining would confirm.

title: Primary Effusion Lymphoma-H&E High Power
describe_en: Skin biopsy at high power shows a dermal proliferation of plump spindle and epithelioid cells infiltrating between collagen bundles. The lesional cells have oval vesicular nuclei with mild atypia and form slit-like vascular channels containing extravasated erythrocytes, with scattered eosinophilic globules. Sheets of large immunoblastic or plasmablastic lymphoma cells are not seen in this field. In the context of a KSHV-associated primary effusion lymphoma case, the morphology is most suggestive of a coexisting Kaposi sarcoma; confirmation with HHV8 LANA-1 plus vascular markers (CD31/ERG) versus CD45/CD138 is recommended.

title: Primary Effusion Lymphoma-H&E
describe_en: Section of tissue at low-to-intermediate power shows an infiltrate of intermediate-to-large atypical cells arranged in cords, nests and sheets that dissect a dense collagenous stroma, with a small lymphoid aggregate. The cells have moderate amphophilic cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei, but nucleolar and plasmablastic detail cannot be resolved at this magnification, and the nested pattern could mimic carcinoma or melanoma. Immunostains on this case show HHV8/LANA nuclear positivity with CD45 and MUM1 expression and lack of immunoglobulin light chains, supporting extracavitary (solid) primary effusion lymphoma.

title: Primary Effusion Lymphoma-HHV8
describe_en: HHV8 (LANA-1) immunohistochemistry at low power shows an unremarkable surface squamous epithelium overlying edematous stroma that contains numerous scattered cells with nuclear HHV8 positivity. The positive cells are distributed diffusely as single cells through the stroma. At this magnification cytologic detail is limited and a vasoformative lesion cannot be entirely excluded on this image alone. In the context of a large-cell lymphoma lacking B-cell markers, the findings support tissue (extracavitary) involvement by HHV8-positive primary effusion lymphoma.

title: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria-Blood
describe_en: Low-power peripheral blood smear shows a monolayer of normochromic red cells with very few leukocytes and scarce platelets in the field, raising the possibility of cytopenias. The arrows highlight pale, poorly outlined red cell structures and a small cluster of red cells, which may represent lysed red cell ghosts reflecting intravascular hemolysis, although detail is not resolvable at this magnification. No schistocytes or spherocytes can be assessed reliably. The findings are nonspecific but compatible with an intravascular hemolytic process such as paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, which requires flow cytometric confirmation.

title: Presence of LE cells in Bone Marrow
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of cells surrounded by red cells. At the top of the cluster are smooth, rounded, homogeneous purple masses without chromatin structure, and the adjacent cells show vacuolated cytoplasm and indented nuclei, an arrangement reminiscent of phagocytes aggregating around free denatured nuclear material. Image resolution and focus are limited, and a classic LE cell with a peripheral crescentic host nucleus is not clearly resolved in this field. Findings are suggestive of LE phenomenon (rosette formation) in the given clinical context of systemic lupus erythematosus, though a cell clump cannot be fully excluded.

title: Presence of LE cells in Bone Marrow
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of crowded, overlapping cells with dark, partly smudged nuclei, admixed with homogeneous purple material and granular debris. A few rounded pale nuclear masses without chromatin texture are present within the cluster, and an isolated degenerated cell is seen at the lower left. Cell preservation is poor and no discrete LE cell with a crescentic displaced nucleus can be confidently identified in this field. The findings may represent aggregation of phagocytes around denatured nuclear material in the clinical setting of systemic lupus erythematosus, but they are not diagnostic on their own.

title: Extracavitary Primary Effusion Lymphoma-H&E Low Power
describe_en: Scanning-power H&E section shows an entire lymph node with an intact fibrous capsule and perinodal fat. The nodal architecture is largely preserved, with numerous small follicles, some with small or regressed germinal centers, and no mass-forming effacement. Sinusoidal involvement by large neoplastic cells is not resolvable at this magnification, and linear sectioning artifacts are present. This field alone would not suggest lymphoma; the diagnosis of extracavitary primary effusion lymphoma relies on higher-power identification of large cells within sinuses and HHV8 immunostaining.

title: Chronic Lymphoproliferative Disorder of NK Cells - Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single lymphoid cell with moderate pale blue cytoplasm containing a few fine azurophilic granules. The nucleus is atypical, with a deeply indented, multilobated flower-like contour and condensed chromatin without nucleoli. The red cells show rouleaux-like stacking and scattered ovalocytes; platelets are present. The granular cytoplasm supports a large granular lymphocyte, which fits chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells, but the lobated nucleus is not the typical round LGL morphology and a single cell cannot establish clonality or NK lineage. Findings are partially consistent with an NK-cell LGL; flow cytometry is required.

title: Abnormal plasma cell with multiple nucleoli
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows increased atypical plasma cells of variable size with eccentric nuclei and deeply basophilic cytoplasm. In the center is a large abnormal plasma cell with abundant basophilic cytoplasm containing multiple nuclei or nuclear lobes with relatively open chromatin; distinct nucleoli are not clearly resolved in this thick, partially out-of-focus field, so the multinucleation is the more evident abnormality. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma with atypical, multinucleated plasma cells.

title: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia, B/myeloid: Blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear stained with a cytochemical stain (likely myeloperoxidase with a blue-black chromogen) shows a mature granulocyte with strong, coarse granular positivity serving as an internal control. Two large cells with pale cytoplasm and folded contours, presumed blasts, are essentially negative, with only rare focal granules in one cell. Nuclear detail is not well seen with the counterstain, and fine dots over red cells are likely artifact. Cytochemistry therefore shows at most a minor MPO-positive blast subset; in the context of mixed phenotype acute leukemia, B/myeloid, myeloid lineage assignment rests on flow cytometric MPO expression in a defined blast population together with B-lineage markers.

title: endomitosis in malignant plasma cell
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a very large atypical cell with abundant, deeply basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm. Within the cell there is a cluster of condensed, rod-like chromosomes in a metaphase-like configuration alongside a separate eccentric nuclear mass, indicating an abnormal mitosis with chromosome condensation not followed by normal nuclear division (endomitosis). The cytoplasmic basophilia supports plasmacytic differentiation, although discrete Russell bodies are not clearly seen in this field. In a patient with CLL, findings are consistent with a highly proliferative atypical plasmablastic cell, supporting Richter transformation to plasmablastic lymphoma.

title: Indolent T-cell Lymphoproliferative Disorder: CD20, CD3, CD8, & CD2
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical panel of colonic mucosa shows that the lamina propria infiltrate is diffusely positive for CD3 and CD2, with only rare CD20-positive B cells. CD5 stains only scattered cells, indicating aberrant loss of CD5 in the neoplastic T-cell population. The crypts are preserved. Note that the four panels are labeled CD20, CD3, CD5 and CD2, whereas the title lists CD8 instead of CD5. The findings support an immunophenotypically aberrant T-cell infiltrate consistent with indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract.

title: Diagnosing D Variant Serologically in the Laboratory
describe_en: Low-power microscopic view of a conventional tube test with monoclonal IgM anti-D shows large red cell agglutinates set against numerous free, unagglutinated red cells, a mixed-field reaction. The image itself demonstrates only the mixed-field pattern and does not by itself establish a D variant; this requires exclusion of recent transfusion or chimerism and supplementary testing such as weak D testing by indirect antiglobulin technique (positive in this case) and, ideally, RHD genotyping. In this transfusion-dependent patient with aplastic anemia, the finding supports reporting the D type as indeterminate (possible D variant) with transfusion of D-negative red cells.

title: Pigment in neutrophils and myeloid cells 6
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single granulocyte whose cytoplasm is packed with coarse, irregular dark purple-black granular material that overlies and partially obscures a lobulated nucleus. The surrounding red cells are normochromic with several echinocytes, and scattered platelets are present. In isolation, the cell closely resembles a basophil or a neutrophil with heavy toxic granulation; the reported history of blood drawn after iodinated contrast injection, with similar black material in other neutrophils and myeloid precursors, supports interpretation as ingested pigment. Findings are suggestive of contrast-associated pigment in a neutrophil, with toxic changes in a septic patient.

title: Blasts with pseudo-chediak-higashi granules.
describe_en: Smear shows several large blasts with fine chromatin, occasional nuclear indentation, and moderate basophilic cytoplasm, together with scattered small lymphocytes and a maturing granulated myeloid cell. One centrally placed blast contains coarse, enlarged cytoplasmic granules, compatible with the fused granules described as pseudo-Chédiak-Higashi granules, although truly giant inclusions are not clearly resolved at this magnification. No Auer rods are identified in this field. In the setting of RUNX1::RUNX1T1, findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with t(8;21) showing abnormal granule fusion.

title: Myeloblasts with AML with t(8;21)
describe_en: High-power view of a smear shows three large blasts with round nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, and high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. The left blast has a moderate rim of pale basophilic cytoplasm with a paler juxtanuclear zone and faint linear cytoplasmic streaking that may correspond to a slender Auer rod; however, a discrete Auer rod is not clearly demonstrated at this focus and resolution. No maturing granulocytes are present in this field for assessment of dysplasia. Findings are consistent with myeloblasts and, in conjunction with cytogenetic confirmation, with acute myeloid leukemia with t(8;21).

title: Chediak Higashi- Incidental Detection 4
describe_en: This digitally enlarged image of a single peripheral blood leukocyte is markedly pixelated and blurred. A dense, lobulated dark purple central mass is seen with a few discrete large dark granules at the periphery, but nuclear detail, cytoplasm, and granule size relative to normal cannot be reliably assessed. The image is non-diagnostic on its own; in the context of the other images from this case, it may represent a leukocyte with Chediak-Higashi giant granules.

title: Wuchereria Bancrofti with CML in Accelerated Phase 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked leukocytosis with a left-shifted granulocytic series spanning myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, and segmented neutrophils. Several basophils with coarse dark granules and a large immature cell with fine chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm are present. Red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis. No microfilariae are present in this field; the parasites were reported at the smear edges and tail. Together with the reported 12% blasts and 15% basophils, findings are consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia in accelerated phase (as defined by ELN/ICC criteria).

title: Niemann-Pick disease with isolated leukemic nonnodal mantle cell lymphoma of the spleen
describe_en: Composite figure. Splenic section shows red pulp diffusely expanded by pale foamy histiocytes, with a periarteriolar white pulp lymphoid aggregate that is not nodular or markedly expanded. An immunostain with nuclear staining highlights scattered small positive cells within the white pulp. The bone marrow biopsy shows fat and interstitial pale histiocytes without an obvious lymphoid aggregate. Findings are consistent with storage histiocytosis compatible with Niemann-Pick disease, with a subtle non-nodular lymphoma infiltrate (reported as leukemic non-nodal mantle cell lymphoma) requiring cyclin D1/SOX11 and flow cytometry for confirmation.

title: The fertile field of “isomopic” immune dysregulation as a nidus for lymphoproliferative disorders
describe_en: Composite figure: clinical photographs show erythematous, scaly and crusted papules coalescing into plaques on the trunk. Skin biopsy shows a dense dermal lymphoid infiltrate arranged in sheets and nodules beneath an intact epidermis. At high power the infiltrate consists of monotonous small to medium-sized lymphocytes with condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm; large transformed cells are not prominent at this magnification. Immunostains show diffuse strong positivity of the infiltrate with one marker and a nuclear-staining marker in many cells, while a further stain highlights only scattered cells. In the clinical context, findings are consistent with cutaneous involvement by CLL/SLL arising at a site of prior skin inflammation (isotopic immune response); the specific markers are not labeled in the image.

title: Refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained for iron (Prussian blue with nuclear fast red counterstain) shows a mixed population of nucleated cells, including erythroid precursors and segmented granulocytes, on a background of red cell debris. A few scattered blue siderotic granules are present, but a clear perinuclear ring of granules encircling erythroblast nuclei is not well resolved in this photomicrograph, likely owing to magnification and color balance. Ring sideroblasts should be counted at high power as erythroblasts with at least five granules covering at least one-third of the nuclear circumference. With the reported 40% ring sideroblasts and SF3B1 mutation, the case is consistent with MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation (formerly refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts).

title: EBV-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a boy with a history of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows circulating plasmacytoid lymphocytes and plasmablast-like cells with eccentric nuclei, abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm, and perinuclear hofs (panels A and B, arrows). Flow cytometry (panel C) demonstrates an expanded CD19-positive B-cell population (32% of lymphocytes), the majority of which co-express CD38 and surface IgM, consistent with an activated plasmablastic phenotype; a smaller CD19-positive subset is IgM+ CD38−. Light-chain analysis is not shown, so clonality cannot be assessed from this figure, and hemophagocytosis itself is not illustrated. In a patient with EBV-triggered HLH, these findings are best interpreted as a reactive EBV-driven plasmablastic B-cell response, but relapse of B-cell lymphoma should be excluded given the history.

title: Multiple myeloma - Bone marrow smear 1
describe_en: Low-power view of a Wright-Giemsa stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows a markedly cellular, particle-rich preparation with numerous fat vacuoles. The cellular trails are dominated by a relatively monotonous population of round mononuclear cells with basophilic cytoplasm, with apparent reduction of normal trilineage hematopoiesis and no megakaryocytes evident in this field. Cytologic features of individual cells cannot be assessed at this magnification. The low-power pattern is compatible with extensive marrow infiltration, which in this case was reported as mature plasma cells; high-power examination and plasma cell quantification are required to confirm multiple myeloma.

title: MCD - H&E - Fig 6
describe_en: Section shows a lesion extensively replaced by broad, anastomosing, eosinophilic trabeculae with intervening small lymphocytes, plasma cells and thin-walled vessels, and a focus of hemorrhage. The trabecular material is consistent with metaplastic ossification or osteoid, as described, but osteocytic lacunae, osteoblastic rimming and cement lines are not clearly evident at this magnification, so dense hyalinized collagen cannot be excluded from this image alone. No lymphoid follicles are present in this field. Findings are compatible with regressive stromal change (ossification/hyalinization) in long-standing Castleman disease, correlating with other fields showing regressed follicles.

title: Snapper-Schneid granules in plasma cell
describe_en: Blood smear shows a single mononuclear cell with an eccentric, dark, condensed nucleus and a rim of cytoplasm filled with numerous uniform round inclusions. The inclusions have a clear halo with a dark eccentric dot or crescent, rather than the fine azurophilic granules usually expected. The submitted interpretation is Snapper-Schneid granules (lysosomal azurophilic granules) in a plasma cell; however, the image resolution does not allow confident identification of the host cell as a plasma cell, and the halo-and-dot appearance overlaps with intracellular yeasts such as Histoplasma capsulatum or Talaromyces marneffei. Review of additional fields and, if doubt remains, GMS/PAS staining or culture is recommended before accepting this as a plasma cell with azurophilic granules.

title: Leukemia cutis in acute myeloid leukemia - 2
describe_en: Composite of six high-power fields from a peripheral blood smear shows circulating blasts. The blasts are medium to large with moderate to high N:C ratios, round to irregular or indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant to moderate pale gray-blue agranular cytoplasm, some with cytoplasmic blebs. No Auer rods, cytoplasmic granules or dysplastic neutrophils are identified in these fields. The image shows only the blood component; the cutaneous infiltrate referred to in the title is not depicted. Together with the reported immunophenotype (CD117+, CD33+, CD7+, HLA-DR+, cMPO-negative, CD19/CD20/CD14/CD64-negative), findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with minimal differentiation.

title: AML with myelodysplasia related changes- Peripheral blood smear
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low-to-medium power shows a paucicellular field with only two leukocytes, suggesting leukopenia. One is an atypical mononuclear cell with moderately fine chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm that may represent a circulating blast, and the other is a small mature lymphocyte. Red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional elliptocytes, and platelets appear decreased in this field. No neutrophils are present to evaluate for dysplasia. The findings are nonspecific and, while compatible with the clinical diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplasia-related changes, require correlation with bone marrow morphology, blast enumeration and cytogenetic/molecular studies.

title: AML with myelodysplasia related changes- Bone marrow biopsy Iron
describe_en: Iron stain (Prussian blue with nuclear fast red counterstain) of what appears to be a bone marrow aspirate smear, rather than a core biopsy section as labeled, shows scattered nucleated cells with only rare fine extracellular blue granules. No ring sideroblasts are identified among the nucleated cells in this field, and no marrow particle or macrophage is present to grade storage iron. Evaluation is limited by focus and the small number of cells. Findings do not demonstrate ring sideroblasts in this field; a full assessment of storage iron and sideroblasts on particle-containing aspirate smears is required.

title: Dapsone Induced Oxidative Haemolysis.
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows anisocytosis with numerous small, dense erythrocytes lacking central pallor, consistent with spherocytes and irregularly contracted cells, along with scattered crenated cells and occasional red cell fragments. Classic bite cells and blister cells with eccentric hemoglobin retraction are not clearly identified in this field, and Heinz bodies require a supravital stain for demonstration. Platelets appear adequate and no leukocytes are present in this field. In the setting of dapsone therapy, the findings are suggestive of oxidative hemolysis; confirmation with a Heinz body preparation, methemoglobin level and G6PD assay is recommended.

title: urine analysis in sickle cell disease 2
describe_en: Automated urine sediment digital imaging shows a single unstained particle measuring approximately 7-9 um with a crescentic shape and tapered ends, classified by the analyzer into a red cell-related class. The morphology resembles a sickled red cell, but the low resolution and absence of internal detail prevent definitive distinction from a folded or crenated red cell or other debris. Findings are suggestive of sickled red cells in urine in a patient with sickle cell disease and should be verified by manual microscopy of the sediment.

title: BONE MARROW BIOPSY 1
describe_en: The image is a bone marrow aspirate smear rather than a biopsy section. It shows histiocytes whose pale blue cytoplasm contains numerous small, uniform, round-to-oval yeast-like organisms with clear halos, with additional organisms free in the background. Surrounding cells include lymphocytes, plasma cells and myeloid precursors in a vacuolated background, and a cohesive epithelioid granuloma as described in the title is not appreciable. Findings are suggestive of disseminated fungal infection, most likely histoplasmosis; GMS/PAS stains, culture, antigen testing and correlation with the biopsy are recommended.

title: G-6-PD deficiency & eryptosis vs dyserythropoesis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows several nucleated red cells with small dense nuclei, one of which displays nuclear budding with a detached nuclear fragment. Red cells show anisopoikilocytosis with oval and teardrop-like forms, and platelets are numerous with large granular forms. Classic bite or blister cells are not convincingly seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a hemolytic picture with circulating nucleated red cells showing nuclear budding; these changes are not specific, and G6PD deficiency requires confirmation by enzyme assay and a Heinz body preparation.

title: ACANTHOCYTES IN PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous red cells with surface projections. Most of these cells retain central pallor and have short, relatively uniform, evenly distributed spicules, a pattern typical of echinocytes (burr cells); only a minority are smaller, dense cells with fewer irregular spiky projections resembling acanthocytes. A small lymphocyte and platelets are present, and schistocytes are not seen. In this patient with renal failure, the findings are most suggestive of echinocytosis (burr cells), with only a subset of cells meeting acanthocyte criteria; drying artifact from slow smear preparation should also be excluded. The title of acanthocytes is therefore only partly supported by this image.

title: Bone Marrow Necrosis 3
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain on a bone marrow biopsy shows a densely cellular infiltrate in which nearly all cells demonstrate strong, diffuse cytoplasmic/membranous brown staining with sparing of the nuclei. The uniformity of staining indicates that the infiltrating population expresses the antigen tested. The antibody is not specified, so the lineage implication cannot be stated from the image alone. In the context of acute leukemia with focal coagulative necrosis, this pattern would support a lineage-defining marker expressed by the blast population, pending correlation with the full panel.

title: Bone Marrow Necrosis 4
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain on a bone marrow biopsy shows a dense population of small to intermediate round cells. A subset of cells shows granular cytoplasmic/membranous brown staining in a patchy distribution, while many cells are negative. The specific antibody is not indicated, so the lineage significance of this pattern cannot be determined from the image alone. In the provided context of acute leukemia with focal coagulative necrosis, this stain is part of the immunophenotypic workup and must be interpreted with the full IHC panel and flow cytometry.

title: Bone Marrow Necrosis 5
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain on a bone marrow biopsy shows a diffuse, densely cellular infiltrate of small to intermediate round cells. Most cells are negative or show only weak brownish nuclear staining, with rare cells containing small cytoplasmic brown dots. The antibody is not indicated and the staining is weak, so the result cannot be confidently interpreted as positive or negative from this image. Interpretation requires correlation with the stated diagnosis of acute leukemia with focal coagulative necrosis and the remainder of the immunophenotypic panel.

title: Mast cells in peripheral blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large cell with abundant pale grey-blue, finely vacuolated cytoplasm containing sparse faint granules, irregular angulated borders and an eccentric bilobed to folded nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin. The background red cells and platelets are unremarkable in this field. The cell lacks the dense metachromatic granulation of a typical mast cell, and on morphology alone a monocyte cannot be excluded. In a patient with systemic mastocytosis, this may represent a circulating hypogranular atypical (bilobed) mast cell; confirmation by tryptase or CD117/CD25 flow cytometry is recommended, and quantification is needed to assess for mast cell leukemia.

title: Therapy related myeloid neoplasm 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a hypercellular particle with a crowded population of immature mononuclear cells having high N:C ratios, fine chromatin and occasional nucleoli, suggesting increased blasts, which should be quantified on a differential count. A megakaryocyte in the center shows abundant pale granular cytoplasm with a single small, round, non-lobated nucleus, a dysplastic hypolobated (mononuclear) form. Micromegakaryocytes with widely separated nuclear lobes described for this case are not clearly identifiable in this particular field. In a patient with prior cytotoxic therapy, the dysmegakaryopoiesis and immature cell population are consistent with a therapy-related myeloid neoplasm.

title: VEXAS SYNDROME 4
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright-Giemsa) shows a cellular specimen with orderly-appearing granulocytic maturation. A large cell with dense, clumped, eccentric nuclear lobes and pale cytoplasm is present, possibly representing a dysplastic megakaryocyte, and another large cell with abundant granular cytoplasm is seen at left. Distinct cytoplasmic vacuolization of myeloid or erythroid precursors, the hallmark finding of VEXAS syndrome, is not convincingly demonstrated in this particular field. Blasts are not increased in this view. The image is only partially supportive of VEXAS syndrome and should be interpreted together with other fields and UBA1 mutation testing.

title: Dutcher Bodies in Lymphoplasmacytic Lymphoma 1
describe_en: Low-power H&E sections show fragments of tissue diffusely replaced by a dense, monotonous infiltrate of small lymphoid-appearing cells with scattered small vessels and eosinophilic stromal elements. Normal architecture is not identifiable in the fields shown. Cytologic details, including plasmacytoid differentiation and intranuclear inclusions, cannot be evaluated at this magnification. In the clinical context, the findings are compatible with involvement by a low-grade B-cell lymphoma such as lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, but high-power examination, immunohistochemistry (CD20, CD138, kappa/lambda), and MYD88 L265P testing are required.

title: T lymphoblastic leukemia with granulomas
describe_en: Composite figure of a tissue biopsy. The H&E panel shows a dense infiltrate of hyperchromatic blast-like lymphoid cells admixed with and surrounding aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes forming granulomas. The lymphoid cells are diffusely positive for nuclear TdT and for CD3, indicating an immature T-cell phenotype. In the CD34 panel the endothelium is strongly positive while the neoplastic cells show only weak or equivocal staining, so CD34 positivity described in the legend is not clearly evident in this field. Findings are consistent with T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma accompanied by an epithelioid granulomatous reaction.

title: Granulomas and T cell leukemia
describe_en: Composite figure of a tissue biopsy. The H&E panel shows sheets of small to medium hyperchromatic atypical lymphoid cells surrounding pale eosinophilic aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes forming non-necrotizing granulomas. Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse nuclear TdT and diffuse CD3 staining of the lymphoid infiltrate, establishing an immature T-cell phenotype. The CD34 panel shows strong endothelial staining, with the neoplastic cells largely negative or only faintly stained in this field, so CD34 positivity stated in the legend is not clearly demonstrated. Findings are consistent with T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with an associated epithelioid granulomatous reaction.

title: Image 3
describe_en: Four-panel low-power composite of a lymph node core biopsy with unlabeled panels. The upper panels are interpreted as kappa and lambda in situ hybridization, with scant staining in the left panel and abundant positive plasma cells in the right, indicating lambda light chain restriction. The lower panels show Congo red staining of extensive salmon-pink amorphous deposits with cracking artifact and, under polarized light, birefringence of the deposits, although the characteristic apple-green color is not clearly resolved at this magnification and image quality. Findings support a lambda-restricted plasma cell neoplasm with AL amyloid deposition; confirmation of apple-green birefringence on the glass slide and amyloid typing by mass spectrometry are recommended.

title: Mitosis in a bone marrow aspirate
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows maturing granulocytic precursors including myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and band neutrophils. The arrowed cell has abundant finely granular cytoplasm and discrete condensed chromosomes arranged in a radial rosette around a central clear zone, without a discernible nuclear membrane. This is a mitotic figure; however, the fully discrete chromosomes and rosette arrangement suggest late prophase/prometaphase or an end-on (polar) view of metaphase rather than early prophase as labeled. Findings are consistent with a normal mitotic figure in a granulocytic precursor.

title: Giant lymphomatous cell (in a patient with splenic marginal zone lymphoma
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (Leishman) shows increased small lymphoid cells with round nuclei, condensed chromatin, and scant cytoplasm. One larger lymphoid cell has an oval nucleus with bipolar attenuated cytoplasmic tails giving a fusiform shape, and occasional cells show a short polar cytoplasmic projection; distinct villous projections and a clearly giant cell are not well demonstrated in this image. Red cells show diffuse crenation, likely artifactual. In the setting of massive splenomegaly, the findings are compatible with circulating splenic marginal zone lymphoma cells, but fusiform stretching can be produced by smearing and the image alone is not diagnostic; flow cytometry and splenic or marrow histology are required.

title: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma - Peripheral blood
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, viewed at low magnification in a thin area, shows two small lymphoid cells with condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm, one of which has a slightly eccentric nucleus suggestive of plasmacytoid differentiation. Red cells are largely separated with central pallor, and definite rouleaux formation is not well demonstrated in this particular field, although it may be evident in thicker areas of the smear. Platelets are numerous and no blasts are seen.
