The low magnification limits cytologic detail; findings are nonspecific but compatible with circulating lymphoplasmacytic cells in the context of known lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.

title: Bone marrow biopsy -granulomatous inflammation
describe_en: Scanning-power view of a fragmented bone marrow core biopsy shows intertrabecular spaces diffusely occupied by a dense cellular infiltrate with near-complete loss of marrow fat. The cellular composition, the presence of discrete granulomas, and necrosis cannot be assessed at this magnification. Higher-power examination, together with special stains for microorganisms and immunohistochemistry, is required. In this case, higher-power views demonstrated granulomatous inflammation.

title: GZL CD-20
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD20 shows weak and heterogeneous granular staining in a subset of cells, while many large pleomorphic and multilobated tumor cells are negative or only faintly positive. Strong, uniform membranous positivity across sheets of cells is not seen. This variable CD20 expression, in the context of CD15 and CD30 positivity in the same large cells, supports B-cell lymphoma with features intermediate between DLBCL and classic Hodgkin lymphoma (mediastinal gray zone lymphoma); distinguishing positive small reactive B cells from tumor cells at this resolution is limited.

title: Von Willebrand disease with intestinal angiodysplasia
describe_en: Composite figure. Capsule endoscopy frames show a small bowel lumen filled with fresh blood, which obscures the underlying mucosa. The gross photograph shows an opened segment of small intestine with preserved plicae circulares and multiple dark red hemorrhagic foci and clots on the mucosal surface; no mass lesion is apparent. The images document active small bowel bleeding but cannot by themselves demonstrate the vascular lesion; the reported histology of dilated, congested, irregular thin-walled vascular channels beneath focally eroded mucosa supports intestinal angiodysplasia in a patient with von Willebrand disease.

title: autoagglutination in a case of auto immune hemolytic anemia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows markedly increased nucleated red cells, predominantly polychromatic and orthochromatic normoblasts, together with prominent polychromasia, macrocytic reticulocytes and scattered spherocytes. Several small irregular clumps of red cells are present, suggestive of autoagglutination, although agglutination is focal rather than marked in this particular field. Neutrophils appear morphologically unremarkable and platelets are present. In the setting of a strongly positive direct antiglobulin test and reticulocytosis, findings are consistent with autoimmune hemolytic anemia with brisk erythroid regeneration; red cell agglutination with spuriously high MCV and MCHC should prompt evaluation for a cold-reactive autoantibody.

title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia with Sanjad Sakati syndrome
describe_en: Composite figure. Peripheral blood smears show marked leukocytosis composed of granulocytes at all stages of maturation, with conspicuous myelocytes and metamyelocytes, and a basophil at high power; blasts are not increased in the fields shown. These blood findings are consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase, in keeping with the reported t(9;22) BCR::ABL1 detection. The accompanying chest radiograph shows a globular enlarged cardiac silhouette, and the clinical photographs show the patient and a subxiphoid pericardial drain, correlating with the reported pericardial effusion and tamponade during imatinib therapy.

title: Primary cutaneous CD8+ epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphomas, a rare and dramatic challenge still open
describe_en: Clinical photographs of the lower leg document disease evolution. Panel A shows multiple scattered erythematous papulonodules with central ulceration and black necrotic crusts; panel B shows progression to a large confluent necrotic, exudative ulcer with eschar; panel C shows healing after chemotherapy with hyperpigmentation and atrophic scarring. These appearances indicate a rapidly progressive ulceronecrotic cutaneous process but are not specific. Diagnosis of primary cutaneous CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma requires biopsy demonstrating pagetoid epidermotropic atypical CD8+ cytotoxic T cells.

title: Severe acute gastrointestinal GVHD in patients undergoing HSCT: an open challenge
describe_en: Gross photographs show an expelled elongated fragment of intestinal-type tissue, approximately 5 cm per history, that is dark red, edematous and hemorrhagic with irregular excavated edges, lying in bile- and blood-stained fecal material. These appearances indicate extensive mucosal sloughing. The gross image alone cannot establish the cause; in a recent allogeneic HSCT recipient the differential includes severe acute gastrointestinal GVHD and conditioning-related mucositis, and histologic examination for crypt apoptosis, crypt dropout and infection is required.

title: Bone marrow biopsy at low power
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at low power shows bony trabeculae with intervening marrow that contains preserved fat and focal hemorrhage. The hematopoietic areas are occupied by a dense interstitial to sheet-like infiltrate of mononuclear cells, with megakaryocytes not readily appreciated. Cytologic detail is insufficient at this magnification to characterize the infiltrate, and the pattern is not specific. Findings are compatible with marrow involvement by a blastic neoplasm; correlation with high-power morphology and immunohistochemistry (CD4, CD56, CD123, TCL1) is required to support blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

title: HLH 2
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at high power shows maturing granulocytic elements, including neutrophils, myelocytes and eosinophils, in a background of red cells and smudged cells. A large macrophage in the center has abundant, vacuolated cytoplasm containing pale cellular debris; clearly intact engulfed red cells, platelets or nucleated cells are not identified in this field. Findings indicate activated macrophages with phagocytosed debris, which can be seen in hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis but are not specific on their own. Correlation with HLH diagnostic criteria (fever, cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble CD25) is recommended.

title: Leishman Stain 100X ; Howell Jolly bodies , Basophilic stippling , Bite cells, Polychromatophils
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (Leishman stain, high power) shows red cells with anisopoikilocytosis and many crenated forms, which may partly reflect drying artifact. A red cell containing a single dense round inclusion consistent with a Howell-Jolly body is present, along with polychromatophilic cells and occasional cells with peripheral bites or eccentric clearing. Fine punctate inclusions are seen in a few cells, but definite basophilic stippling is not clearly resolved at this resolution. In the appropriate drug history, findings are suggestive of oxidative (drug-induced) hemolysis.

title: Schistocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (high power; suboptimal, greyish staining) shows red cells with mild anisocytosis, most of which are oval to elliptical with preserved central pallor. A single helmet-shaped fragment with a straight cut border is present at the upper left, consistent with a schistocyte. Only a few cells are in this field, so the schistocyte proportion cannot be estimated, and the predominance of ovalocytes is not explained by fragmentation. The image supports the presence of a schistocyte, but quantification over multiple fields (ICSH: >1% suggests microangiopathic hemolysis) and correlation with platelet count and hemolysis markers are required.

title: Imprint smear showing blast like lymphoid  cells with prominent nucleloli
describe_en: Touch imprint smear is cellular and shows a monotonous population of intermediate-to-large atypical lymphoid cells, roughly two to three times the size of an adjacent small lymphocyte. The cells have very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to slightly irregular nuclear contours and finely dispersed chromatin; nucleoli, although described, are not clearly resolvable in this image because of overstaining and limited focus. No maturing myeloid elements are evident in the field. Findings are consistent with infiltration by blastoid lymphoid cells of a high-grade lymphoma, with correlation to histology and immunophenotyping required.

title: cup shaped blasts with Auer rod
describe_en: Smear shows a single blast with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin and a prominent pale cup-shaped nuclear invagination giving a fish-mouth appearance. The surrounding cytoplasm is scant, and a definite Auer rod cannot be confidently identified at this focus and resolution, although a faint linear structure may be present within the invagination. No other nucleated cells are in the field. Findings are consistent with a cup-like blast, a morphology associated with AML with NPM1 mutation and/or FLT3-ITD; molecular testing is required for classification.

title: Hemophagocytosis and increased bone marrow iron stores
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a regenerating marrow with maturing granulocytic and erythroid precursors. There are increased macrophages with abundant cytoplasm containing coarse dark greenish-brown to black globular inclusions; some contain small dark bodies suspicious for ingested cellular material, although definite hemophagocytosis of intact cells is not unequivocal in this field. A Prussian blue stain of a marrow particle shows macrophages laden with coarse blue-green iron-positive granules admixed with golden-brown pigment, indicating increased storage iron. Findings are consistent with increased marrow iron stores in post-chemotherapy/transfusion setting with macrophage activation; residual pigmented globules that are not clearly iron-positive could reflect hemosiderin of variable staining or other ingested debris, and clinical correlation is recommended.

title: Metastatic gastric cancer cells 1
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a hemodilute background with scattered myeloid and erythroid precursors. There is a loose aggregate of large cells with round nuclei, fine chromatin and abundant pale blue cytoplasm with indistinct syncytial borders, as well as a large cell with abundant finely vacuolated cytoplasm; these cells are several times the size of adjacent granulocytes. Cohesion is less pronounced in this field than in classic tumor clusters, and distinction from macrophages or osteoblasts is limited on a single field. In the context of known gastric carcinoma, findings are suggestive of metastatic carcinoma, which should be confirmed on the trephine biopsy with cytokeratin immunohistochemistry.

title: Plasma Cell Myeloma in the Stomach
describe_en: Gastric polyp biopsy shows the lamina propria diffusely expanded by sheets of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and focal atypia, including Dutcher bodies, separating residual gastric glands. The infiltrate is positive for CD138 and MUM1 and negative for CD20 and PAX5, with monotypic cytoplasmic light chain expression. Note that the figure legend labels panel C as lambda (negative) and panel D as kappa (positive), which conflicts with the case description stating lambda restriction; the correct light chain should be confirmed against the original report. In a patient with known myeloma, findings are consistent with extramedullary involvement by plasma cell neoplasm.

title: Promyelocyte
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single medium-to-large immature cell with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a round nucleus with finely stippled chromatin, and a thin rim of pale cytoplasm. Heavy azurophilic granulation, bilobed nuclear folding, and Auer rods described for this case are not clearly resolved in this image, likely because of focus and resolution. The image alone therefore does not permit confident classification beyond a circulating immature myeloid-appearing cell. If abnormal promyelocytes with Auer rods are confirmed on the film, urgent evaluation for acute promyelocytic leukemia (coagulation studies, PML::RARA testing) is warranted.

title: Plasmodium vivax gametocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with prominent crenation artifact and scattered platelets. One enlarged, pale red cell contains dispersed fine brown granules and a small eccentric chromatin dot, compatible with a Plasmodium vivax-infected erythrocyte; the enlargement of the host cell and stippling favor P. vivax over P. falciparum. Because of the pale staining, a mature gametocyte (round parasite filling the cell with a single compact chromatin mass and dispersed pigment) cannot be confidently distinguished from a developing trophozoite in this field. Findings are suggestive of P. vivax malaria; correlation with a thick film and a well-stained thin film is recommended.

title: Panel A, 10X: Focal area of epithelioid cells in bone marrow core biopsy
describe_en: Low-power H&E section of the bone marrow core biopsy shows a bony trabecula with adjacent marrow composed of adipose tissue and trilineage-appearing hematopoietic elements, with scattered megakaryocytes and focal hemorrhage. Areas in the right half of the field contain paler, larger cells, but a discrete focus of epithelioid cells is not sharply defined at this magnification. High-power examination and immunohistochemistry (CD163 positive, CD34 negative, dot-like AE1/AE3) are needed to characterize the epithelioid population.

title: Panel-B, 40X, Cells are large with large pleomorphic nucleus, abundant clear to pink cytoplasm and inconspicuous nucleoli
describe_en: High-power view of an H&E-stained bone marrow core biopsy shows a hypercellular marrow with maturing erythroid and myeloid elements and abundant hemosiderin-laden macrophages. Interspersed are large epithelioid cells with pleomorphic vesicular nuclei, inconspicuous nucleoli, and pale to pink cytoplasm, which form a loose focal aggregate rather than cohesive glands. On H&E alone these cells raise concern for metastatic carcinoma; however, in this case they showed only dot-like cytoplasmic keratin staining with membranous CD163 positivity, supporting an epithelioid histiocytic aggregate in a marrow with MDS. The epithelioid focus is not sharply delineated at this magnification, so correlation with the lower-power and immunostained panels is required.

title: Chediak-Higashi syndrome- Platelet
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an enlarged platelet with an irregular outline and coarse, dense purple granules, alongside a few normal-sized platelets. Red cells are overlapping in this thicker area of the film with occasional crenated forms. No leukocytes are present in the field for assessment of giant cytoplasmic granules. This platelet finding is nonspecific on its own; in the setting of Chediak-Higashi syndrome it is compatible with the reported hypergranulated platelets, although the platelet dense-granule deficiency underlying the bleeding tendency is not visible by light microscopy.

title: Trephine biopsy
describe_en: Low-power immunohistochemical stain of a bone marrow trephine biopsy (antibody not specified) shows a hypercellular marrow with diffuse sheets of immature cells that are negative. Only scattered interstitial cells with irregular to dendritic shapes, and a few larger cells, show brown cytoplasmic/membranous staining, suggesting a residual non-neoplastic population such as macrophages, myeloid cells or megakaryocytes. Because the antigen is not identified, specific interpretation is limited; in the context of pure erythroid leukemia, the neoplastic infiltrate would be expected to be negative for myeloid/megakaryocytic markers and positive for E-cadherin, CD71 and glycophorin/hemoglobin.

title: Platelets satellitism
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of approximately seven mature neutrophils in tight apposition. Numerous platelets are adherent to the neutrophil membranes around the perimeter of the cluster and in the spaces between cells, while few free platelets are present in the surrounding field. The neutrophils themselves show normal nuclear segmentation without toxic change. Findings are consistent with EDTA-associated platelet satellitism, here accompanied by neutrophil aggregation, which can cause spurious thrombocytopenia; a platelet count on a citrate-anticoagulated sample is recommended.

title: Reactive clumping
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two small loose aggregates of platelets, consistent with platelet clumping, which can cause spurious thrombocytopenia on automated counts. The field is dominated by irregular, branching clumps of red cells resembling agglutination, with numerous small dark punctate bodies overlying the red cells and scattered stain precipitate; these dots cannot be characterized reliably and may be artifactual. No leukocytes are present in this field. Findings show platelet clumping as described, but the prominent red cell clumping suggests additional red cell agglutination (for example, cold agglutinins) or a thick, poorly spread area, and correlation with a repeat smear is advised.

title: Gaucher cell
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large histiocytic cell (arrow) with abundant pale lilac-gray cytoplasm containing numerous fine vacuoles and a poorly defined nucleus, surrounded by erythroid precursors, lymphocytes and granulocytic cells. The classic crumpled tissue-paper fibrillary cytoplasm of a Gaucher cell is not clearly demonstrated, and the image is out of focus. Findings suggest a storage-type histiocyte; in the stated clinical context this may represent a Gaucher cell, with confirmation by glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay and/or GBA1 genotyping.

title: Gaucher's disease
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smears show intact trilineage hematopoiesis with readily identified megakaryocytes. The upper panel contains a large histiocytic cell with a small eccentric nucleus and abundant pale, finely vacuolated to fibrillary cytoplasm, and nearby pale storage-type cytoplasm; the characteristic wrinkled tissue-paper appearance of Gaucher cells is not sharply resolved due to focus and image quality. Findings are suggestive of a storage histiocyte in the appropriate clinical context of Gaucher disease; confirmation requires glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay and/or GBA1 genotyping.

title: Hodgkin Cell
describe_en: Smear shows a single very large mononuclear cell with deeply basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm, set among maturing granulocytes and a small lymphocyte. The nucleus appears large but its chromatin detail and nucleoli are obscured by the overlying cytoplasmic vacuoles, so the characteristic inclusion-like macronucleolus of a Hodgkin cell cannot be confirmed on this image alone. In the appropriate clinical and histologic context this could represent a mononuclear Hodgkin cell; however, a vacuolated large cell of other lineage cannot be excluded morphologically, and correlation with biopsy and CD30/CD15/PAX5 immunostaining is recommended.

title: Reed-Sternberg Cell
describe_en: Smear shows a large binucleate cell with two round, similarly sized nuclei arranged in a mirror-image configuration, finely dispersed chromatin and a moderate amount of grey-blue cytoplasm with irregular borders. Distinct eosinophilic macronucleoli are not well visualized at this focus. Surrounding cells include an erythroid precursor and small lymphocytes. The cell has the configuration of a Reed-Sternberg cell and, in a patient with classic Hodgkin lymphoma, is suggestive of marrow involvement; however, binucleate cells of other lineages can appear similar on smears, and confirmation on trephine biopsy with CD30/CD15/PAX5 immunostaining is recommended.

title: Hypergranulated Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (composite of six fields) shows clusters of large immature myeloid cells with round to slightly irregular nuclei, fine chromatin, occasional nucleoli, and basophilic cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules that partly overlie the nucleus, consistent with abnormal promyelocytes. However, the cytoplasm is not densely packed with coarse granules, and bilobed nuclei, Auer rod bundles, and faggot cells are not evident in these fields; image focus also limits evaluation. The morphology is therefore only partly representative of classic hypergranular APL, and confirmation by PML::RARA FISH or RT-PCR (and strongly MPO-positive, CD34/HLA-DR-negative immunophenotype) is essential. Findings are suggestive of acute promyelocytic leukemia in the appropriate clinical context.

title: Goblet Cells
describe_en: Nasal smear stained with a Romanowsky-type stain shows scattered epithelial cells in a mucoid, granular background. The cells have a single round nucleus with speckled chromatin and pale, faintly foamy blue cytoplasm; in one cell the nucleus is displaced toward one pole. A classic chalice shape with a distended apical mucin vacuole is not clearly demonstrated at this resolution. Findings are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, goblet cells of respiratory mucosa.

title: Lamellar bodies 1
describe_en: Gross photograph shows bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in a test tube with a thick, white, foamy pellicle floating on the surface over a relatively clear to faintly opalescent fluid, with minimal sediment and no hemorrhagic or purulent appearance. This gross appearance reflects high surfactant/lipoproteinaceous content. Microscopic structures such as lamellar bodies cannot be evaluated on this image; correlation with the cytologic smear (PAS-positive granular material, foamy macrophages) is needed. Findings are suggestive of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis in the appropriate context.

title: Hemoglobin C Crystals
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous target cells with folded and irregularly contracted red cells. Scattered red cells contain dense, homogeneous, rectangular to rhomboid crystals with straight, parallel edges (arrows), consistent with hemoglobin C crystals. Occasional elongated forms with more tapered ends resembling sickle or boat-shaped cells are also present; the coexistence of HbC-type crystals and sickle-like forms raises the possibility of compound hemoglobin SC disease rather than homozygous HbC disease. Findings are consistent with a hemoglobin C-containing hemoglobinopathy; hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC is required to define the genotype.

title: lymphocyte ingulfing bacteria 5
describe_en: The smear shows a sparsely cellular, pale background with numerous extracellular short, plump rod-shaped bacteria and no red blood cells. A single leukocyte with a dense, eccentrically compressed crescentic nucleus contains several intracytoplasmic bacilli within pale vacuolated cytoplasm. The dense compacted nucleus and phagocytic activity favor a degenerating phagocyte (neutrophil or monocyte) over a true lymphocyte, as lymphocytes are not professionally phagocytic; exact lineage cannot be established on this single cell. Findings are consistent with bacterial infection with intracellular organisms (gram-negative bacilli such as Klebsiella/Pseudomonas per the case context); Gram stain and culture are required for identification.

title: CSF Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter cloacae
describe_en: Cytocentrifuge preparation of cerebrospinal fluid shows a cluster and scattered single short, straight bacilli with rounded ends, staining blue with a Romanowsky-type stain. No inflammatory cells are present in this field, and Gram reaction cannot be determined from this stain. The findings indicate bacterial organisms (bacilli) in the CSF, suggestive of bacterial meningitis or contamination; morphology cannot distinguish Pseudomonas aeruginosa from Enterobacter cloacae or other gram-negative rods, and identification requires Gram stain and culture with susceptibility testing.

title: Multiple bluish globules indicative of cryoglobulinemia visible at the tail end of the smear.
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of mature plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, clock-face chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid lymphocytes, with occasional granulocytic cells. The background contains pale, tan-to-pale-blue amorphous globular extracellular deposits. The image depicts a marrow aspirate rather than the tail of a peripheral smear stated in the title, so the match is partial. In the context of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, the lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with amorphous background deposits is suggestive of cryoglobulin precipitation; flow cytometry, MYD88 L265P testing and serum studies are needed for confirmation.

title: Plasma cell myeloma
describe_en: Composite of Wright-stained fields shows numerous plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, deeply basophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear clearing, including large, binucleate and multinucleate forms, some with finer chromatin and nucleoli, and occasional small clusters. The background contains abundant granulocytic precursors at various stages of maturation, which is more in keeping with a bone marrow aspirate than the peripheral blood smear stated in the title. Definite rouleaux formation is not clearly demonstrated in these fields, as red cells are mainly overlapping in thick areas. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma; if this is peripheral blood, the circulating plasma cell burden would raise concern for plasma cell leukemia.

title: Renal biopsy involved by follicular lymphoma, intermediate-power
describe_en: H&E-stained renal biopsy at intermediate power shows effacement of the renal parenchyma by a dense, diffuse infiltrate of small lymphoid cells with scant cytoplasm, with only residual interspersed blood vessels and no clearly preserved tubules or glomeruli. A follicular growth pattern is not evident in this field, and image quality limits assessment of centrocytes versus centroblasts. The infiltrate is monotonous without a prominent mixed inflammatory component. Findings are consistent with renal involvement by a low-grade B-cell lymphoma; immunohistochemistry (CD20, CD10, BCL6, BCL2) is needed to support follicular lymphoma.

title: Blasts in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered medium-to-large immature myeloid cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin and granular cytoplasm with irregular borders. Nucleoli and Auer rods cannot be confidently resolved at this magnification and resolution. Background red cells show target cells and minor poikilocytosis, and platelets appear decreased. In a patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia under treatment (e.g., ATRA/arsenic), the findings are compatible with circulating abnormal blasts/promyelocytes with therapy-related changes; the Auer rod described cannot be verified in this image.

title: Sezary Cell 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows two atypical lymphoid cells of medium size with scant cytoplasm and dense chromatin. The nuclei are markedly convoluted and lobulated, with a petal-like multilobated nucleus in the upper cell and a cleaved clover-like nucleus in the lower cell; fine cerebriform grooves are not clearly resolved at this resolution. No nucleoli or cytoplasmic granules are seen. In a patient with mycosis fungoides, these convoluted lymphocytes are consistent with circulating Sezary cells, although the coarse lobation resembles ATLL flower cells, and flow cytometry (CD4+, CD7-, CD26-) is needed to quantify the clone.

title: Lytic bone lesions with sclerosed margins 1
describe_en: Frontal radiograph of the right distal femur and knee, photographed from a display screen, shows subtle mottled lucency within the distal femoral shaft and metaphysis. Because of moire artifact and low contrast, the size, number and margins of any lytic lesions, including the reported sclerotic rims, cannot be reliably assessed on this image. No obvious pathologic fracture or aggressive periosteal reaction is seen. The image is only partially supportive of the reported lytic lesions and should be interpreted together with better-quality views; in the clinical context, the findings would be compatible with skeletal Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

title: Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis in a Case of Pulmonary Adenocarcinoma with Multiple Metastases and Concurrent Infection 1
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large multinucleated cell containing three oval nuclei with fine chromatin and abundant pale, finely vacuolated cytoplasm, set in a background of small mononuclear hematopoietic cells. No clearly engulfed hematopoietic elements are identified within this cell at this focal plane, so hemophagocytosis cannot be confirmed from this image alone. The cell may represent an activated multinucleated histiocyte or a metastatic tumor cell; correlation with the other fields of this case, which show hemophagocytes and metastatic adenocarcinoma, is required. Findings are suggestive of, but not diagnostic for, secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

title: Richter transformation, DLBCL cell with erythrophagocytosis
describe_en: The May-Grunwald-Giemsa-stained smear shows a small cluster of large atypical mononuclear cells with eccentric nuclei, dispersed chromatin and abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm, in a background of mature neutrophils, small lymphocytes and platelets. Red cells lie closely adjacent to the large cells, but unequivocal intracytoplasmic erythrophagocytosis cannot be confirmed at this image resolution. In the clinical context of CLL, the large basophilic cells are suggestive of large B-cell lymphoma (Richter transformation); tissue biopsy and immunophenotyping are required for confirmation.

title: Richter transformation, DLBCL cells with erythrophagocytosis  2
describe_en: H&E-stained section including a bone trabecula shows the marrow space replaced by a diffuse infiltrate of large atypical cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and moderate cytoplasm, admixed with spindle-shaped stromal cells in a fibrotic background. The arrowed cell contains a small round intracytoplasmic body that may represent an engulfed red cell, although erythrophagocytosis is difficult to confirm at this magnification. Normal trilineage hematopoiesis is not evident in this field. In a patient with CLL, findings are suggestive of involvement by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Richter transformation), to be confirmed by immunohistochemistry.

title: Burkitt Lymphoma
describe_en: Smear preparation (composite of several fields) shows medium-sized, monomorphic lymphoid cells with round nuclei, finely stippled chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and scant deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing numerous sharply defined clear vacuoles. The cells occur singly and in small groups against a background of red cells; the specimen appears to be blood or a dilute aspirate. The starry sky pattern mentioned in the case description is a tissue-section finding and cannot be seen on this smear. The cytologic features are consistent with Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia, which requires confirmation by flow cytometry (CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2-, surface light chain restricted, Ki-67 near 100% on tissue) and demonstration of MYC rearrangement.

title: Idiopathic Multicentric Castleman Disease- Lollipop
describe_en: Low-power view of the lymph node shows preserved architecture with multiple follicles of varying size, some with small germinal centers surrounded by expanded, concentrically layered mantle zones. Prominent vessels traverse the interfollicular region and approach the follicles, with increased interfollicular vascularity. Vessels radially penetrating germinal centers (lollipop follicles) are suggested but not clearly resolved at this magnification. The findings are compatible with Castleman disease-type morphology in the appropriate clinical setting.

title: TAFRO- CD138
describe_en: CD138 immunohistochemistry on the lymph node at low power highlights scattered plasma cells distributed diffusely through the interfollicular areas, without sheets or nodular aggregates. The small, regressed-appearing follicles are CD138 negative. Interpreting plasma cell density at this magnification is subjective; in this field the plasma cells appear moderate in number rather than sheet-like, the pattern expected in TAFRO-type idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease as opposed to the plasmacytic subtype. Light chain ISH/IHC should be reviewed to exclude a clonal plasma cell process.

title: HHV8 Positive MCD- Kappa IHC
describe_en: Lymph node section immunostained for kappa light chain shows considerable diffuse background staining, including the follicular dendritic cell meshwork of concentrically arranged follicles. No distinct strongly kappa-positive large cells are identified in and around the follicles, where lambda-positive plasmablasts were seen, whereas a band of kappa-positive mature plasma cells is present in one interfollicular area and scattered positive cells occur elsewhere. The title's statement that plasma cells are kappa-negative is therefore only partly reflected, as a subset of interfollicular plasma cells is kappa-positive and the background limits interpretation. Taken with the lambda stain, findings support lambda-predominant follicle-associated plasmablasts, consistent with HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease; kappa/lambda ISH would give cleaner assessment.

title: Refractory Anemia with Ring Sideroblasts
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows erythroid precursors with dysplastic features, including binucleated and nuclear-budding erythroblasts, megaloblastoid nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony and irregular, frayed cytoplasm, with occasional coarse cytoplasmic granules. Granulocytic cells present in the fields are not specifically assessable for dysplasia. Ring sideroblasts cannot be evaluated on this Giemsa-stained preparation; the reported Prussian blue stain showing 70% ring sideroblasts, together with refractory macrocytic anemia, supports myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts (SF3B1 testing recommended).

title: PLASMA CELL LEUKEMIA 1
describe_en: Photomicrograph taken through the eyepiece shows a densely cellular smear dominated by atypical mononuclear cells with few intervening red cells. The cells vary from medium to very large, with moderate grey-blue cytoplasm and round, indented or lobulated nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin, giving an immature, plasmablastic appearance; classic plasma cell features such as eccentric nuclei with clockface chromatin and a perinuclear hof are not reliably seen. Background refractile droplets are likely artifactual. Morphology alone is nonspecific at this resolution, but with the reported CD38+/CD138+ kappa-restricted phenotype the findings support plasma cell leukemia secondary to myeloma.

title: PLASMA CELL LEUKEMIA 2
describe_en: Photomicrograph taken through the eyepiece shows a densely cellular smear composed of monotonous medium-sized mononuclear cells with few red cells. The cells have scant pale cytoplasm and reniform, indented or lobulated nuclei with finely granular chromatin; conventional plasma cell features such as eccentric nuclei and a perinuclear hof are not appreciated. Background refractile droplets are likely artifactual and image resolution is limited. The morphology is nonspecific, but together with the reported CD38+/CD138+ kappa-restricted phenotype, it supports plasma cell leukemia with atypical lobulated nuclei.

title: Plasma cell myeloma 1
describe_en: Composite images show Romanowsky-stained bone marrow aspirate smears rather than histologic biopsy sections. There is a marked increase in plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, perinuclear hof and basophilic cytoplasm, many present in clusters. Atypical features include binucleated and multinucleated forms and cells with less condensed chromatin and nucleoli, admixed with residual erythroid and granulocytic precursors. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma; the specimen type differs from the title's 'biopsy' designation, and clonality should be confirmed by CD138 with kappa/lambda studies.

title: Plasma cell myeloma 2
describe_en: Composite images show Romanowsky-stained bone marrow aspirate smears rather than histologic biopsy sections. Cellular particles and trails contain numerous plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, coarse chromatin and pale to moderately basophilic cytoplasm with a perinuclear hof, including enlarged forms with more open chromatin. Residual erythroid precursors, lymphocytes and fat spaces are present. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma; note the specimen type does not match the 'biopsy' description.

title: Plasma cell myeloma 3
describe_en: Composite images show Romanowsky-stained bone marrow aspirate smears rather than histologic biopsy sections. Numerous plasma cells are present, many enlarged with abundant basophilic cytoplasm, eccentric nuclei, perinuclear hof and relatively open chromatin, including binucleated forms. Residual erythroid precursors, granulocytes and lymphocytes are admixed. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma; the specimen type differs from the 'biopsy' description, and CD138 with kappa/lambda studies on the core are recommended for quantification and clonality.

title: Pseudo Auer rods in Splenic marginal zone lymphoma. 2
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows cellular marrow with preserved trilineage hematopoiesis on H&E, in which a lymphoid infiltrate is not readily apparent. Immunohistochemistry for CD20 highlights an infiltrate of small B cells arranged in linear, intrasinusoidal chains, and these cells co-express BCL2 and IgD. The cytoplasmic Auer rod-like inclusions named in the title are not assessable in this biopsy image and are seen only on the smears. Findings are consistent with involvement by splenic marginal zone lymphoma with a predominantly intrasinusoidal pattern.

title: EBV-related Lymphoproliferative Disorder in Bone Trephine, Figure 3
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine section stained for EBV shows scattered large cells with strong, dense brown staining, while the background hematopoietic and small lymphoid cells are negative. The positive cells are markedly larger than surrounding cells and some have lobulated outlines. The staining fills the whole cell rather than showing a discrete nuclear signal, and the size and shape of some positive cells overlap with megakaryocytes, so correlation with the H&E and a nuclear EBER in situ hybridization is advisable. In the reported context of large atypical cells on the aspirate, findings support EBV infection of large atypical cells, consistent with an EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disorder.

title: Abnormal Mitosis in Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS)
describe_en: Marrow aspirate smear shows granulocytic precursors at myelocyte and metamyelocyte stages. Several cells show mitotic activity, including a large cell with two separated, irregular, condensed chromatin masses in an anaphase/telophase-like configuration, and another cell with two condensed chromatin clumps. The chromatin masses appear ragged and asymmetric, but multipolar spindles cannot be confidently resolved at this image quality. Isolated mitoses are not specific; atypical mitotic figures together with multilineage dysplasia and cytopenias are suggestive of, but not diagnostic for, a myelodysplastic neoplasm, which requires blast count, dysplasia quantitation, and cytogenetic/molecular correlation.

title: Blasts in AML
describe_en: Peripheral blood (or aspirate) smear shows three medium to large blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, round to slightly irregular nuclei with fine dispersed chromatin and faint nucleoli, and scant to moderate pale blue cytoplasm. Definite Auer rods, which would confirm myeloid lineage, are not convincingly seen at this resolution, although the caption reports them. Morphology alone is therefore suggestive of acute leukemia with blasts compatible with myeloblasts, and lineage assignment requires MPO cytochemistry or flow cytometry.

title: Extramedullary relapse of acute promyelocytic leukemia in cerebrospinal fluid 1
describe_en: Cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid at low magnification shows marked hypercellularity composed of numerous medium-to-large atypical mononuclear cells with round to irregular nuclei and moderate pale cytoplasm, admixed with red cells and occasional small lymphocytes. The diagnostic high-power features of abnormal promyelocytes, including coarse primary granules, Auer rods and bilobed nuclei, cannot be assessed at this magnification. Findings indicate CSF involvement by an acute leukemia and, in the documented clinical context with high-power confirmation, are consistent with extramedullary relapse of acute promyelocytic leukemia; PML::RARA testing of the CSF cells can confirm.

title: Barr body 2
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single segmented neutrophil with three to four lobes, clumped chromatin and finely granular cytoplasm, set in a background of normocytic red cells, scattered platelets and fine stain precipitate. The title indicates a Barr body (drumstick), a small round chromatin appendage attached to a nuclear lobe by a thin strand, but a definite drumstick cannot be distinguished from overlapping lobes at this resolution. The image is therefore only partially illustrative; drumsticks are a normal finding in female neutrophils (inactivated X chromosome) and have no pathological significance.

title: Sheet of Plasmacells with binuclear Plasmacells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large central clear space, likely a fat vacuole or bubble with fibrin strands, surrounded by crowded plasmacytoid cells with eccentric round nuclei, coarse chromatin and abundant gray-blue cytoplasm. The image is substantially out of focus, so binucleate plasma cells cited in the title cannot be confidently identified, and nucleoli cannot be assessed. The density of plasma cells in the surrounding cellular areas supports a plasma cell proliferation, but quantification on a well-spread area and clonality studies are required before a diagnosis of plasma cell neoplasm.

title: Developmental stages of Plasmodium vivax 3
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows two intraerythrocytic malaria parasites at the schizont stage, one containing approximately eight discrete chromatin dots in blue cytoplasm and the other a mature schizont densely filled with merozoites. The infected red cells do not appear enlarged relative to surrounding erythrocytes, and Schüffner stippling is not evident; background red cells show crenation artifact. Because the classic P. vivax features of host-cell enlargement, stippling and 12-24 merozoites cannot be confirmed in this field, species assignment should rely on the full smear, other stages and PCR or antigen testing. Findings are consistent with malarial schizonts, compatible with but not specific for Plasmodium vivax.

title: Klebsiella pneumoniae in periferal blood smear of immunocompromised patient 1
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with occasional crenated forms and scattered platelets. Two extracellular clusters of short, plump, uniformly sized rod-shaped bacteria are present, some in pairs and short chains, associated with pale pink amorphous material. No leukocytes, and therefore no phagocytosed organisms, are present in this field. Findings indicate circulating bacilli, suggestive of high-grade bacteremia in an immunocompromised patient; species identification (Klebsiella pneumoniae per history) requires blood culture, and contamination or delayed processing should be excluded.

title: Atypical Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Cells With Auer Rods-like Inclusions
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an absolute lymphocytosis composed predominantly of intermediate-sized lymphoid cells with clumped chromatin and moderate pale cytoplasm, including increased prolymphocytoid forms. Cytoplasmic Auer rod-like inclusions described in these cells are not clearly resolvable at this image resolution, but the lymphoid cells are negative for myeloperoxidase, with a neighboring granulocyte serving as a positive internal control. Flow cytometry shows a B-cell population with kappa light chain restriction and no increase in CD34-positive blasts. Findings are consistent with an atypical CLL/low-grade B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder with MPO-negative Auer rod-like inclusions, not acute myeloid leukemia.

title: Auer rod in AML
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large blast (arrow) nestled among a cluster of red cells. The blast has a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, finely dispersed chromatin, multiple pale nucleoli and a thin rim of basophilic cytoplasm. An Auer rod, as stated in the title, cannot be convincingly identified at this image resolution. Findings are consistent with a circulating blast; lineage assignment as myeloid would rest on a visible Auer rod, MPO cytochemistry or flow cytometry.

title: Eosinophiluria
describe_en: Cytocentrifuged urine sediment (Wright-Giemsa, oil immersion) shows numerous granulocytes, several of which have bilobed nuclei and coarse orange-red cytoplasmic granules consistent with eosinophils. Many of the remaining cells are degenerated, with smudged nuclei and poorly preserved granules, so the eosinophil fraction cannot be reliably quantified from this image, and focus is limited. The presence of urinary eosinophils is compatible with eosinophiluria, which may be seen in acute interstitial nephritis among other renal and urinary tract inflammatory conditions, although it is neither sensitive nor specific.

title: Image 1. Chronic myeloid leukemia with Roth spot
describe_en: Color fundus photograph of the left eye shows a single well-circumscribed intraretinal hemorrhage superotemporal to the optic disc, adjacent to the superior vascular arcade, with a faint pale rim along its upper edge. A definite central white fibrin-platelet core is not clearly resolved in this enhanced image, and no additional hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots or disc edema are evident; the central whitish patch is a light reflex artifact. The title describes chronic myeloid leukemia while the case is filed under CMML, and the ocular finding itself does not distinguish these entities. In a patient with leukemia, the hemorrhage is compatible with a Roth spot, reflecting anemia, thrombocytopenia and/or leukostasis.

title: CML(2)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked leukocytosis composed of granulocytes at all stages of maturation, including early precursors, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, band and segmented neutrophils, with an accompanying basophil. The upper arrowed cell is a large immature granulocyte with an oval nucleus, relatively fine chromatin and moderately abundant basophilic cytoplasm containing azurophilic granules; its granularity favors a promyelocyte (or a granular blast) over an agranular myeloblast. The lower arrowed cell is a myelocyte with an eccentric nucleus, condensed chromatin and pink secondary granulation. Findings are consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia; blast and basophil percentages should be enumerated by manual differential.

title: Gaucher's Disease: Aspirate 1
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive-appearing aggregate of cells with small, round, eccentric nuclei and moderate to abundant cytoplasm. Between the nuclei there are pale blue-white cytoplasmic areas with fine striations and small vacuoles, and a central cell shows pink-purple fibrillar cytoplasm, features that suggest lipid-storage histiocytes. The characteristic crumpled 'wrinkled tissue paper' cytoplasm is only focally suggested, and individual cell borders are hard to resolve, so the morphology is not diagnostic on its own. In the given clinical context, findings are suggestive of Gaucher cells; confirmation by glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay or GBA1 genotyping is required.

title: Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows three neutrophils with segmented nuclei and prominent toxic vacuolation of the cytoplasm. Platelets are markedly reduced, and red cells are largely normocytic with an occasional echinocyte. Faint thin intracytoplasmic and a few extracellular linear structures may represent bacteria, but they are not definitively resolved at this magnification, so review at oil immersion (and Gram stain) is recommended. In a febrile patient with DIC, toxic vacuolation with suspected fusiform organisms is suggestive of overwhelming bacteremia, here confirmed as Capnocytophaga canimorsus on blood culture.

title: Dermal Thrombosis in a case of PNH
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the posterior lower legs shows multiple large, irregular retiform purpuric plaques with angulated, branching borders. The lesions have central violaceous-black necrosis with eschar and an area of ulceration covered by yellow fibrinous slough, surrounded by a dusky erythematous hemorrhagic rim. No histology is shown in this image, so dermal vessel thrombosis itself is not directly visualized; the title refers to the biopsy findings. The clinical pattern of retiform purpura with necrosis indicates occlusive cutaneous microvascular thrombosis and, in the context of a large GPI-deficient granulocyte clone, is consistent with thrombotic complications of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.

title: Caseating granuloma on bone marrow 1
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy at low power shows two well-formed, circumscribed epithelioid granulomas composed of histiocytes with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and elongated nuclei, rimmed by small lymphocytes. The intervening marrow shows fat, hemorrhage and scattered residual hematopoiesis. A definite central zone of amorphous acellular caseous necrosis is not appreciated at this magnification, and giant cells are not clearly resolved. Findings are consistent with granulomatous inflammation of the marrow; caseation should be confirmed at higher power, and AFB and fungal stains with cultures are recommended given the association with mycobacterial infection.

title: Caseating granuloma on bone marrow 2
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows a large, well-formed granuloma composed of epithelioid histiocytes and several multinucleated giant cells, surrounded by concentric fibrosis and a dense rim of small lymphocytes. The adjacent marrow shows fat and residual hematopoietic elements. A definite central zone of amorphous acellular caseous necrosis is not evident in this field. Findings are consistent with granulomatous inflammation; caseation should be confirmed on additional levels, and special stains (AFB, GMS) and cultures are recommended to exclude mycobacterial or fungal infection.

title: Peripheral blood smear showing monocyte with intracellular fungal organisms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two adjacent leukocytes. The upper cell has a dense, irregularly lobated nucleus pushed aside by approximately six to seven small, uniform oval organisms, each with a clear halo and a basophilic crescent of stained cytoplasm; no kinetoplast is identified. The lower cell is a monocyte with a folded nucleus and grey, finely vacuolated cytoplasm without organisms. The dense lobated nucleus of the infected cell could represent a neutrophil rather than a monocyte, although distortion by the organisms limits lineage assignment. Findings are suggestive of circulating intracellular Histoplasma capsulatum yeasts, consistent with disseminated histoplasmosis; confirmation by culture, antigen testing, or GMS/PAS stains is recommended.

title: Peripheral blood smear showing neutrophil with intracellular fungal organisms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mature segmented neutrophil with finely granular cytoplasm and a small cytoplasmic vacuole. The cytoplasm contains several tiny dark basophilic bodies, including a short chain of three dots, a short rod, and an angular particle. These inclusions are smaller than typical Histoplasma yeasts (2-4 um) and lack a surrounding clear halo, so on this image alone they cannot be confidently distinguished from phagocytosed bacteria or overlying stain precipitate. In the context of the companion images showing haloed yeasts in leukocytes, findings are compatible with, but not diagnostic of, peripheral blood involvement by disseminated histoplasmosis; blood cultures and Histoplasma antigen testing are recommended.

title: ALCL cells in the bone marrow
describe_en: Section of bone marrow shows an infiltrate of large pleomorphic cells with abundant cytoplasm and irregular, folded to kidney-shaped nuclei with vesicular chromatin, set within a vacuolated background containing scattered eosinophils and small lymphoid cells. Definite hallmark cells with classic horseshoe nuclei are suggested but not unequivocally resolved at this image quality, and no cohesive sheets of normal hematopoiesis are apparent in the field. The morphology is suggestive of marrow involvement by a large cell lymphoma such as anaplastic large cell lymphoma; confirmation requires CD30 (strong, uniform), ALK and T-cell marker immunohistochemistry together with cytokeratin and melanoma markers to exclude metastatic tumor.

title: AML with biallelic CEBPA mutation
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows occasional circulating blasts with high N:C ratio and deeply basophilic cytoplasm, along with scattered mature neutrophils. The bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular for age, with interstitial to sheet-like infiltration by large immature mononuclear cells with oval to indented nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and small nucleoli; residual megakaryocytes and hemosiderin-laden macrophages are present. The aspirate smear contains numerous blasts with moderate grey-blue cytoplasm, some showing nuclear folding suggestive of monocytic differentiation; Auer rods are not identified in these fields. Findings are consistent with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia; morphology does not specify the genetic subtype, and the reported biallelic CEBPA mutation requires molecular confirmation.

title: The Parvovirus in Bone Marrow
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E) shows a cellular marrow adjacent to a bony trabecula with preserved fat. At higher power there are increased large cells with round nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and prominent nucleoli, resembling enlarged pronormoblasts. Immunohistochemical panels show membranous/cytoplasmic staining of scattered large cells (c), diffuse staining of many marrow cells (d), and a negative stain (e); the antibodies are not labeled in the figure. Characteristic glassy intranuclear inclusions are not definitively resolved at this resolution. Findings are suggestive of parvovirus B19 infection of the marrow, which should be confirmed by parvovirus B19 immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, or serum PCR.
